# Specification — Harness Runtime v1.101

## Change-note (v1.100 → v1.101)

**Status posture (SPEC-APPLIED 2026-07-18 — fork-apply; impl arc owed).** v1.101 is the Runtime-owned rider of the RATIFIED **B-51 / B-52 / B-54 OD audit-signing amendment arc** (`.harness/class_1_fork_b51_b52_b54_od_signing_amendment_arc.md`, **all ten gate items ratified AS RECOMMENDED 2026-07-18**; three dyadic council convenings at the apply leg per workspace `CLAUDE.md` §10.9 — dyad 1 B-51 C7 ⊥ C2, dyad 2 B-52 C7 ⊥ C9/C1, dyad 3 B-54 C7 ⊥ C9/C1 — **all-CONFIRM, zero deviations**), applied per workspace `CLAUDE.md` §4.3 back-flow + §4.5 clearance discipline. Unlike prior notes' BUILT posture, spec + impl do NOT land together here — the impl arc follows separately per the ratified sequencing (fork gate item 10: one bundle — OD v1.33 → v1.34 + CP v1.100 → v1.101 + THIS rider + the OD/CP/Runtime plan deltas). Sibling definition sites: **`Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_34.md`** (flag semantics §21.2.3; verification API §21.2.2; fifth canonical-message segment + tenant-bearing signing API + tenant-tag normalization §21.2.1) and **`Spec_Control_Plane_v1_101.md`** (§1 tenant-bearing `cp_audit_to_od_audit`; §2 §28.10.4 invariant-2 carve-out + post-effect catch-ordering; §3 §20.3.1 backend-aware blocking-walk reconciliation; §4 §20.1.1 narrow historical exception) — OD/CP-owned contract text is CROSS-REFERENCED, never restated here. Six Runtime-owned surfaces: **(A) `audit_signing_fail_closed` RuntimeConfig contract (§3 C-RT-03 — NEW field row + NEW MTC config-validation invariant).** `audit_signing_fail_closed: bool | None = None` — bool-like TRI-STATE: unset (`None`) → per-persona default (ON at `multi-tenant-compliance`, OFF elsewhere, OD v1.34 §21.2.3 row 2); explicit `false` INVALID at MTC (config-validation error at bootstrap, §21.2.3 row 3 — the flag is a non-MTC opt-in knob only; NO relaxation of `C-CP-20 §20.1`'s forward posture); fail-closed ON ⇒ a configured `SigningBackend` REQUIRED at bootstrap (§21.2.3 row 4 zeroth-site invariant — the `unsigned:*` placeholder is a policy violation at MTC). The OD rows DEFINE the policy; this rider owns the carrier + the enforcement site (the Runtime bootstrap/config-validation layer). Env-keyed via BOTH `config/loader.py::_ENV_SCALAR_FIELDS` (`HARNESS_AUDIT_SIGNING_FAIL_CLOSED`) AND `config_source.py::_RuntimeEnvSettings` — the committed dual-loader convention the v1.99 fields themselves cite (`[[runtimeconfig-scalar-needs-both-env-loaders]]`); dual registration is an EXPLICIT plan-delta acceptance criterion (dyad-2 precision note 3, the known dropped-env-override defect class). **(B) MTC tenant-scope bootstrap invariant (§3 C-RT-03 `tenant_id` row + invariant).** At MULTI_TENANT_COMPLIANCE, `tenant_id` is REQUIRED at config validation (OD v1.34 §21.2.1 row 6 — drop-when-`None` MUST NOT silently keep a compliance deployment on the tenant-unbound four-tuple). The upgrade story for an existing MTC deployment with history persisted under the `"_single"` tag is the OD v1.34 §21.2.2 authenticated cutover record MATERIALIZED by `harness migrate-audit-sidecar` retagging the named rows' sidecar `tenant_tag` to the attested `tenant_scope` (OD v1.34 §21.2.1 row 6 — entry content and `entry_hash` unchanged; the retag is the committed read mechanism, no dual-scope legacy read; the record MUST disposition EVERY existing `"_single"` identity — the migration REFUSES typed with zero retags on undispositioned leftovers, and only record-QUARANTINED rows remain unretagged, reported per §21.2.2 row 6 — the invariant does not orphan pre-existing history). **(C) MTC prewarm/keepalive DISABLE under fail-closed (fork gate item 8 — amends the v1.99 B-18-KEEPALIVE contract, ADR-D3 §1.5:189-190 lineage).** Under `audit_signing_fail_closed=ON` at MULTI_TENANT_COMPLIANCE (the ratified gate-item-8 scope; the lower-tier explicit-opt-in prewarm swallow is a NAMED RESIDUAL registered for operator disposition at the impl arc per OD v1.34 §21.2.3 row 8 — extending the disable below MTC was not ratified, and the propagation alternative breaks the committed v1.99 bootstrap-isolation contract), BOTH B-18-KEEPALIVE surfaces are DISABLED AS CONTRACT TERMS: (1) the `prompt_cache_boot_prewarm` stage-5 LOOP_INIT boot ping is NOT fired, and (2) the `_keepalive_loop` daemon coroutine (`cli/app.py:391-427`) is NOT SPAWNED — the LOOP itself, not merely the `prewarm()` entry point: the loop's own outer catch (`except Exception` → count as FAILED) is a swallow boundary that must be unreachable BY CONTRACT, not by coincidence of call order (dyad-2 precision note 1 — otherwise a post-provider-call KMS signing failure is swallowed while the process continues, the exact fail-open bypass OD v1.34 §21.2.3 row 8 forecloses). The disable is a POLICY SKIP composing with the existing `PrewarmOutcome` `SKIPPED_*` outcome family — a policy skip is NOT a `FAILED` outcome and MUST NOT count toward the keepalive `consec_fail` self-disable accounting (the exact member naming rides the Runtime plan delta). Flag-OFF behavior (the non-MTC default) is BYTE-PRESERVED — the v1.99 contract text stands verbatim for it (opt-in-default-off; 5m-TTL-only keep-alive; swallow-all best-effort posture). Ratified rationale: prewarm is a latency optimization; compliance-tier audit integrity outranks warm caches. **(D) Tenant threading through runtime-owned call sites.** The converter-based production call sites source the signing tenant from `StepExecutionContext.tenant_id` (OD v1.34 §21.2.1 row 3; CP v1.101 §1 row 4 — the converter forwards RAW; normalization is OD-owned at §21.2.1 row 2). The workflow-less prewarm path — which today signs `tenant_id=None` OUTSIDE any workflow (`llm_dispatch.py:849`) — signs NOTHING at MTC because surface (C) removes it there; no synthetic-scope policy is needed. The redaction-map carrier already holds tenant scope as its own `_tenant_id` (OD-owned, §21.2.1 row 4 — cross-referenced). The ten `except AUDIT_SIGNING_HARD_FAILURES` handler sites and the post-effect catch-ordering fence (caught AHEAD of the generic per-attempt classifier catch, result-preserving) are runtime-owned WIRING of OD v1.34 §21.2.3 rows 1/7 + CP v1.101 §2 — the site-level acceptance criteria ride the Runtime plan delta. **(E) C-RT-13 verifier CLI inputs (NEW §13.5 + §13 exit-contract amendment).** `harness-inspect` today checks ZERO signatures (dyad-3 probe) and pre-v1.101 §13 carries none of the verification inputs — leaving them out would force the impl arc to invent an unratified CLI surface (X-AL-3). NEW §13.5 declares the five operator-supplied audit-verification inputs (audit sidecar path; EXPECTED tenant scope; verification backend/key mapping — the OD v1.34 §21.2.2 row-1 resolver's operator-supplied form; the authenticated cutover record; the authoritative persona-tier/RuntimeConfig input, without which the inspector cannot distinguish MTC's mandatory UNVERIFIED-nonzero posture from lower tiers' preserved hash-only behavior) + the MTC inspection disposition (backend inputs REQUIRED at MTC or explicit `UNVERIFIED` with NONZERO exit — silent hash-only success prohibited, OD v1.34 §21.2.2 row 8). Exit-surface verified FIRST per the rider instruction: §14.18.2 governs C-RT-29 `HarnessRunCLI` (`RunResult.status` mapping) and does NOT govern the inspect surface — `harness-inspect` has its OWN §13 exit contract, so the UNVERIFIED-nonzero semantics are amended THERE (§13 bullet + NEW §13.5) and §14.18.2 is UNTOUCHED. **(F) B-53 — `harness migrate-audit-sidecar` §13.4 scripts-inventory row (fork gate item 7).** The B-47 migration CLI (`python -m harness_runtime.admin.migrate_audit_sidecar` — deliberately NOT `[project.scripts]`-registered at its landing precisely because the inventory is spec-committed) is PROMOTED to a subcommand under the existing flat `harness <subcommand>` namespace (§13.4's committed Q-J=(a) command model; the `python -m` module path stays as the implementation). ONE new §13.4 inventory row; the subcommand-count invariant refreshed 5 → 6. Acceptance criteria ride the Runtime plan delta, NOT this spec. **PD-8 witness obligations Runtime owns (each mutation-probed per Workflow v1.18 PD-8; plan-delta acceptance criteria):** (a) flag config-validation witnesses — explicit `false` at MTC rejected; fail-closed-ON-without-backend rejected at bootstrap; INCLUDING dual env-loader registration (an env-only `HARNESS_AUDIT_SIGNING_FAIL_CLOSED` override honored through BOTH loaders); (b) MTC-disable witnesses — under flag ON at MTC, the boot prewarm does not fire AND the keepalive LOOP is never spawned (loop-level witness, not merely a `prewarm()`-early-return witness); non-MTC/flag-OFF byte-preservation control; (c) tenant-bootstrap-invariant witness — MTC with `tenant_id=None` rejected at config validation; (d) inspect UNVERIFIED-nonzero witness — MTC inspection without backend inputs exits nonzero with an explicit `UNVERIFIED` disposition, never silent hash-only success; (e) migrate-audit-sidecar subcommand witness — `harness migrate-audit-sidecar` dispatches the existing module `main` under the flat namespace. **IS / AS / ADR / CXA specs UNCHANGED** (no new cross-axis edge — the flag + verifier inputs are intra-runtime carriers of OD/CP-defined policy). OD spec AMENDED at the same-arc `Spec_Operational_Discipline_v1_34.md`; CP spec AMENDED at the same-arc `Spec_Control_Plane_v1_101.md`; **OD + CP + Runtime plan deltas owed in the same arc** (the Runtime plan head v2.48 has no acceptance criteria for the flag, bootstrap validation, handler policy, prewarm/keepalive posture, or tenant threading). Clearance marker owed at `.harness/clearance/spec-harness-runtime-v1-101-cleared-2026-07-18.md` per workspace `CLAUDE.md` §4.5.

## Change-note (v1.99 → v1.100)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-07-15).** v1.100 closes **B-27** (`.harness/class_1_fork_cli_exit_code_paused_status_undefined.md`, ratified 2026-07-15 per the fork's Q1=A/Q2=ii/Q3=b recommended readings — roadmap-continue autonomous session). §14.18.2's exit-code table never assigned `RunResult.status == PAUSED` a disposition (unlike `PARTIAL`, whose addition explicitly extended the row-1 trigger set) — production code fell through to `EXIT_WORKFLOW_FAIL` (exit `1`), identical to a genuine `FAILED` run, even though `PAUSED` is a non-terminal outcome distinct in kind from a hard failure. **Fix:** §14.18.2 gains a NEW row — exit code `5` / `PAUSED` / `RunResult.status == PAUSED`. `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/cli/app.py` gains `EXIT_PAUSED = 5`; both mapping call sites (`_CP_STATUS_TO_EXIT_CODE` dict for daemon-client mode; the one-shot `if/elif` chain) now dispatch `paused` to it explicitly instead of falling through to the `failed`/`drained`/`partial` catch-all. **Naming correction (out-of-family `just codex-review` round 1):** the initial fix named the constant `EXIT_PAUSED_RESUMABLE` and the row `PAUSED_RESUMABLE`, implying every paused run carries a `PauseSnapshot` resumable via a future `resume()` call. Codex correctly flagged that `WAL_SEGMENT`/`RECONCILER_LOOP` engine-native pauses (`workflow_driver.py:4224-4248`, `:4259-4282`) intentionally return `RunStatus.PAUSED` with `pause_snapshot=None` — their durable state lives in the engine's own segment log / reconciler store (§7.4/§9), not the workflow-layer snapshot, so `api.resume(snapshot)` cannot resume them; the uniform "RESUMABLE" name would have misled automation into attempting an impossible resume call. Renamed to the non-overclaiming `EXIT_PAUSED`/`PAUSED`. **Follow-on correction (round 3, same PR):** the row-1 rewrite's own replacement text then asserted engine-native pauses ARE currently resumable via "a plain re-invocation of `harness run`" — also false. Codex traced `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/mcp_server.py`'s `run_id = _resume_snapshot.run_id if _resume_snapshot is not None else uuid.uuid4().hex`: a plain re-invocation (no snapshot) generates a FRESH run_id every time, and the engine recovery loop's `capture_pause` records key on `(workflow_id, run_id)` — a fresh run_id cannot locate the prior pause record, so re-invocation starts an unrelated new run and risks re-executing already-committed steps, not resuming anything. §14.18.2's row 5 is corrected to state plainly that case (b) (engine-native pauses) has NO safe resume path at v1.100, and that a future `resume` subcommand must both branch on `pause_snapshot is not None` AND solve run_id recovery for the snapshotless case before documenting or implementing re-invocation as a resume mechanism. Per Q3 (documentation-note-only, not an implementation obligation): no `resume` subcommand is authored at this version. `RunResult.status`'s `Literal` enum is UNCHANGED — only the exit-code *mapping* gained a row. Tests: `test_b27_workflow_paused_status_exits_five` (one-shot) + a new `("paused", EXIT_PAUSED)` parametrize case (daemon-client `_CP_STATUS_TO_EXIT_CODE` mapping test). IS / CP / OD / AS / ADR / CXA specs UNCHANGED. Co-published with a `.harness/clearance/` marker.

## Change-note (v1.98 → v1.99)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-07-11).** v1.99 materializes **B-18-KEEPALIVE** (R-FS-2 Wave 1) — the **ADR-D3 §1.5:189-190 boot pre-warm + daemon keep-alive** contract for Anthropic prompt-cache epochs. The arc closes in three surfaces: **(1) RuntimeConfig** gains three opt-in-default-off fields: `prompt_cache_boot_prewarm: bool = False` (fires a best-effort single prewarm ping at stage-5 LOOP_INIT for BOTH `harness run` and daemon), `prompt_cache_keepalive: bool = False` (spawns the 5m-TTL daemon keep-alive loop), and `prompt_cache_prewarm_model: str | None = None` (file/CLI-only; fallback model when `routing_manifest.per_workload_overrides` yields no Anthropic binding; does NOT gate correctness). Both bools are env-keyed via BOTH `config/loader.py::_ENV_SCALAR_FIELDS` and `config_source.py::_RuntimeEnvSettings` per `[[runtimeconfig-scalar-needs-both-env-loaders]]`. **(2) C-RT-15 `RuntimeLLMDispatcher`** gains `prewarm_model: str | None = None`, `PrewarmOutcome(StrEnum): WARMED / SKIPPED_NOT_ELIGIBLE / SKIPPED_NO_ANTHROPIC / FAILED`, and `async prewarm() → PrewarmOutcome`. The method is Anthropic-only (SKIPPED_NO_ANTHROPIC otherwise); gates on `frozen_tool_superset` non-vacuity (≥4096-tok combined prefix, SKIPPED_NOT_ELIGIBLE otherwise); resolves the model from `routing_manifest.per_workload_overrides` (priority 1) → `prewarm_model` config field (priority 2) → SKIPPED_NOT_ELIGIBLE; sends a `max_tokens=1` ping via `_dispatch_anthropic` directly (bypassing the HITL/retry wrapper chain — the gate at PRE_ACTION is inapplicable at boot); attributes cost to `workflow_id="__prewarm__"` via `_attribute_cost_best_effort`; swallows all exceptions and returns FAILED (best-effort — MUST NOT propagate). **(3) `HarnessContext` + `_MutableHarnessContext`** gain `bare_llm_dispatcher: Any = None` (stashed at stage 5 so `_keepalive_loop` can call `bare.prewarm()` without routing through the 3-layer retry/HITL wrapper). Stage-5 LOOP_INIT stashes the bare handle and conditionally fires the boot prewarm, wrapping it in a try/except so a failure MUST NOT propagate as `BootstrapFailure`. **`cli/app.py` daemon extension:** a standalone `_keepalive_loop(ctx, bare, *, sleep_fn, interval=240.0)` coroutine is spawned after bootstrap bind when `config.prompt_cache_keepalive and bare.cache_ttl == "5m"` (1h-TTL epochs are excluded — the long epoch already exceeds the 5m cache window; ADR-D3 §1.5:190 keep-alive applies only to the 5m default). Loop body: sleep 240s → check `ctx.drained_flag` → `bare.prewarm()` → self-disable after 3 consecutive FAILED outcomes (structured log). Cancel+await in the daemon's `finally` block BEFORE `await _shutdown(ctx)` (the task is outside the `{serve_task, drain_task}` race set; explicit cancel required to avoid "Task destroyed pending" + mid-shutdown prewarm against torn-down providers). **N7 single-epoch reality:** the daemon holds a single post-bootstrap `HarnessContext` → single `active_system_prompt` + `frozen_tool_superset` epoch → one canonical prewarm epoch per daemon lifetime. **R2 disposition (RE-DEFER):** the C11 "skip keep-alive under cost-ceiling pressure" carve-out (`u1-slice3b-epoch-partition-design.md` §3.3) remains DEFERRED — the cost ceiling is operator-asserted with no committed cell matrix in substrate, so an automatic skip-under-pressure has no signal to key on (building one would be X-AL-3 design extension). The shipping defaults (opt-in-default-off + 5m-TTL-only keep-alive) already bound the C11 risk; explicit re-defer with rationale closes item (6). **Tests:** hermetic (NO paid calls; fake Anthropic adapter + fake clock + injectable `sleep_fn`); 7.1 default-off control (prewarm never called with both flags False), 7.2 opt-in boot ping (max_tokens==1 + cache_control breakpoint), 7.3 eligibility skip (SKIPPED_NO_ANTHROPIC / SKIPPED_NOT_ELIGIBLE / sub-floor), 7.4 keep-alive fake clock (prewarm fires each interval; zero pings when pre-drained), 7.5 self-disable (3 FAILED → break + log), 7.6 drain cancel (cancel+await clean; zero leak), 7.7 cost record (`workflow_id="__prewarm__"` in sink), 7.8 bootstrap-failure isolation (prewarm raises → bootstrap still returns HarnessContext). IS / CP / OD / AS / ADR / CXA specs UNCHANGED. Co-published with one `.harness/clearance/` marker.

## Change-note (v1.97 → v1.98)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-07-10).** v1.98 closes the decorrelation-validated deferral `B-18-CACHE-TTL-OBSERVABILITY` registered at v1.97 (§ v1.96→v1.97 change-note; clearance `Spec_Harness_Runtime-v1_97-cleared-2026-07-10.md`). **Pure observability — no wire-behavior change** (byte-identical dispatch; the ttl already reached the wire marker at v1.94/v1.97). The gap: `_extract_anthropic_cache_request_attrs` scanned only `payload.messages`, but the U-1 (B-18) `cache_control` breakpoint is placed on the **tools** block (slice 1 / 3a) or the **system** block (slice 2) at translate-time on the wire kwargs — never on the frozen `ProviderAgnosticPayload` — so `anthropic.cache_breakpoint_id` + `anthropic.cache_ttl_seconds` went **unrecorded** for the common slice-1/2/3a/3b case (only an atypical message-content-block `cache_control` was observed). Fix: the extractor now scans the **TRANSLATED wire kwargs** (`tools → system → messages`, Anthropic's prefix-cache order) — the single source of truth for what was actually sent — and `_anthropic_response_bundle` threads the translated `kwargs` (all three Anthropic dispatch paths: plain / memory-loop / HITL-tool-loop). `cache_breakpoint_id` now reports the breakpoint **position** (`"tools"` / `"system"` / `"msg-{index}"`, low-cardinality ≤4 per C-AS-14 §14.2); the messages path preserves the pre-B-18 `"msg-{index}"` value verbatim. **Higher value at slice 3b:** the operator now has a direct `cache_ttl_seconds` signal that a selected `1h` ttl took effect (previously only the *effect* was visible via `anthropic.cache_read/creation_input_tokens`). **Canonical §14.2 attribute-reference table updated** (extraction source: translated request kwargs; breakpoint id domain: `tools`/`system`/`msg-{index}`). IS / CP / OD / AS / ADR / CXA specs UNCHANGED (the AS spec C-AS-14 §14.2 row is already position-agnostic — "which of ≤4 breakpoints hit", low cardinality — so this impl is now *more* conformant to it, not a contract change). Co-published with one `.harness/clearance/` marker.

## Change-note (v1.96 → v1.97)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-07-10).** v1.97 materializes the **ttl-selection half of the ADR-D3 §1.5 cacheable-epoch contract** (line 188: `ttl: 5min default; 1hr at Persona §6 cost-ceiling cells where epoch > 5min`) as **U-1 slice 3b** (forward register B-18). The `RuntimeLLMDispatcher` (C-RT-15) gains a `cache_ttl: Literal["5m","1h"] = "5m"` field (sibling to `frozen_tool_superset`), bootstrap-stage-5-bound via `cacheable_epoch.select_cache_ttl(workload_class, config.prompt_cache_long_ttl_workloads)`: the run's `workload_class` (bound at stage 5) selects `"1h"` iff it is a member of the new operator opt-in `RuntimeConfig.prompt_cache_long_ttl_workloads: frozenset[WorkloadClass]`, else `"5m"`. At translate-time (`_payload_to_anthropic_kwargs`; `ProviderAgnosticPayload` stays FROZEN per ADR-F1), the selected ttl replaces the previously-hardcoded `{"type": "ephemeral", "ttl": "5m"}` on the `cache_control` breakpoint — on the tools block (slice 1 path) OR the system block (slice 2 path); the ttl is **orthogonal** to which block is marked and to the superset CONTENT (slice 3a). The default empty opt-in set → every workload-class `"5m"` → **byte-identical to pre-slice-3b**. OpenAI/Ollama translators UNCHANGED.

**Why BUILD (not X-AL-3 back-flow) + why no council** (`.harness/u1-slice3b-epoch-partition-design.md`). The slice-3 findings' fork discriminator ("is `major-version-of-system-prompt` derivable, or genuinely absent → back-flow?") is **probe-resolved to BUILD**: a cache-correct epoch key is derivable NOW — Anthropic's cache is byte-exact, so `active_prompt_version.version_sha` IS the cache-correct system-prompt identity (a coarser semantic "major version" would be a cache-hit bug). The prescribed C2⊥C11 ttl council is **probe-resolved**: ADR-D3 §1.5 lines 188-190 already commit the ttl values (5m/1h) + the 1hr cost-ceiling trigger + keep-alive cadence — convening would re-litigate a §10.2-cleared surface. Persona §6 records the cost ceiling as per-class + operator-asserted (no cell matrix), so "cost-ceiling cells" = the operator opt-in field; the 1hr tier gates a cost optimization, not correctness (5m is always correct), so it is a file/CLI-only collection field (NOT env-keyed, mirroring the other RuntimeConfig collections).

**Decorrelated review + a registered deferral.** Decorrelated advisor (caught the missing config-coercion→selection witness — added: a raw string list on `RuntimeConfig` coerces to a `frozenset[WorkloadClass]` of enum members feeding `select_cache_ttl`) + out-of-family `just codex-review` (independently flagged, matching the advisor, the **cache-ttl observability gap** [P2]). **Deferred follow-on `B-18-CACHE-TTL-OBSERVABILITY`** (decorrelation-validated, NOT this slice): `_extract_anthropic_cache_request_attrs` scans only `payload.messages`, so the tools/system-block breakpoint's `anthropic.cache_ttl_seconds` is unrecorded — a **pre-existing** gap (slices 1/2/3a's 5m marker is equally unobserved; the marker lives on the translated kwargs, not the frozen payload). The wire behavior IS correct (Anthropic caches for the selected ttl) and the EFFECT is observable via `anthropic.cache_read/creation_input_tokens`; only the request-side `cache_ttl_seconds` attr is deferred. Closing it uniformly (slices 1/2/3a/3b) is a shared response-bundle-path refactor → its own arc, not folded here (surgical discipline). **Registered follow-ons** (NOT this slice): slice 3b-epochkey (version_sha cohort identity) + slice 3c (ADR-D4 §1.8 PARALLELIZATION pre-warm — its only consumer; high-blast-radius fan-out) ship together in a dedicated session; `B-18-LANEB-PROMPT-SEMVER` (an operator-declared semantic-version field on `PromptVersion`, the skill `frontmatter.version` analogue per ADR-D3 §1.8.1 — IS-spec amendment, NOT required since version_sha is the cache key). IS / CP / OD / AS / ADR / CXA specs UNCHANGED. Co-published with one `.harness/clearance/` marker.

## Change-note (v1.95 → v1.96)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-07-10).** v1.96 materializes **U-1 slice 3a** (forward register B-18) — the **child-scoped (descended sub-agent) frozen tool superset**, closing the **F1 latent C10 condition-2 gap** the slice-3 design pass surfaced in the merged slice 1 (`.harness/u1-slice3-findings-and-f1-c10-gap.md`). The slice-1 C10 verdict accepted the full frozen superset visible per step at single-privilege-tier **top-level** dispatch UNDER conditions — notably **condition 2**: sub-agent / downgraded dispatchers stay `frozen_tool_superset = None` → fall back to `payload.tools`. That guard was **assumed but never built**: a child workflow reuses the parent `ctx.step_dispatchers` → the parent `RuntimeLLMDispatcher` with the parent's `frozen_tool_superset`, so a sub-agent inference emitted the PARENT's superset (a visibility-only leak — execution stays registry/trust/sandbox/effect-fence-gated — latent because `frozen_tool_superset` is `None` at MVP with no MCP tools).

v1.96 materializes condition 2 as the **ADR-D4 §1.5 default-downgrade REMOVE half**. (1) `compute_frozen_tool_superset(...)` gains a `remove_tiers: frozenset[BlastRadiusTier]` param that OMITS tools whose `ToolContract.blast_radius_tier` is in the set (filtered at COMPUTE time, where the tier is in hand — the projected tuple drops it); the child policy `CHILD_DOWNGRADE_REMOVE_TIERS = {EXTERNAL_IRREVERSIBLE}` (only `REMOVE`; `local-mutation`/`external-reversible` stay VISIBLE — `external-reversible`'s `DOWNGRADE_TO_ASK` is a gate-level concern enforced separately at the HITL gate, NOT a visibility one). (2) `RuntimeLLMDispatcher` (C-RT-15) gains a `child_frozen_tool_superset` field (sibling to `frozen_tool_superset`), bootstrap-stage-5-bound to the downgraded union of the SAME `ctx.mcp_client_hosts`. (3) At translate-time, `dispatch()` selects `child_frozen_tool_superset` when `step_context.sub_agent_descent` is True (a descended sub-agent inference) else `frozen_tool_superset`. Empty-child disambiguation: when the run HAS MCP tools (`frozen_tool_superset is not None`) but the downgraded union is empty (parent registry held ONLY external-irreversible tools → all REMOVE'd → `child_frozen_tool_superset is None`), the descended dispatch emits an EMPTY superset `()` → wire `tools: []` (no visible tools), NEVER the legacy `payload.tools` fallback (which would re-expose the removed tool the child step declares). A descended child in an MVP run with NO MCP tools (`frozen_tool_superset is None`) keeps the legacy `payload.tools` path — nothing to downgrade.

The descent marker rides the CP `StepExecutionContext.sub_agent_descent` carrier (paired CP spec **v1.85 → v1.86**): a RUN-LEVEL constant that `execute_workflow(sub_agent_descent=...)` threads onto every composed `StepExecutionContext` (linear + the 5 non-linear strategies; branch children inherit via `compose_branch_child_context`'s `model_copy`); the runtime `child_workflow_runner` re-enters `execute_workflow(sub_agent_descent=True)`, the top-level `api.run` uses the `False` default. Monotonic-sticky (once True, all descendant runs True — correct because the REMOVE downgrade is idempotent). `ProviderAgnosticPayload` stays FROZEN (ADR-F1); OpenAI/Ollama translators UNCHANGED; both supersets `None` at MVP → byte-identical to pre-slice-3a. **Blast-radius re-confirmation** (C10, `.harness/u1-slice3a-c10-reconfirmation.md`): the child superset is a monotone SUBSET of the parent's (downgrade can only REDUCE visibility), the empty case is strictly safest (no tools), and execution gating is untouched — no blast-radius regression; conditions 1 and 2 both satisfied. Decorrelated advisor (caught the wrapper-propagation witness question) + out-of-family `just codex-review` (caught the empty-child `payload.tools` fallback [P2], fixed). **Registered follow-ons** (NOT this slice): slice 3b (cacheable-epoch primitive) + slice 3c (ADR-D4 §1.8 PARALLELIZATION concurrent-cache pre-warm). IS / OD / AS / ADR / CXA specs UNCHANGED; CP spec paired at v1.86. Co-published with `.harness/clearance/` markers.

## Change-note (v1.90 → v1.91)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-27).** v1.91 records the RUNTIME half of the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-SUBAGENT-FANOUT-CHILD-SAVE-POINT`** — the **SAVE_POINT slice** of the `…-FANOUT-CHILD-SAVE-POINT-RECONCILER` follow-on the v1.90 carrier-segregation note registered (paired with CP spec **v1.84 → v1.85**). The runtime typed mirror `_SUBAGENT_RECOVERABLE_FANOUT_CHILD_ENGINE_CLASSES` (`sub_agent_dispatch.py`) — the fan-out-engine leg of the `subagent_child_recoverable` conjunct 2, which gates the composer's deterministic `child_run_id_seed` — is widened from **{ESR,WAL}** to **{ESR,WAL,SAVE_POINT}**: a fan-out child (`PARALLELIZATION` / `ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS` / `HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION`) whose engine is `SAVE_POINT_CHECKPOINT` now gets the deterministic seed, so on the parent's re-dispatch it re-runs under its deterministic run_id and reconstructs its AGGREGATE through the EXISTING B-FANOUT-OUTPUT-REPLAY branch store. The change mirrors the CP `_FANOUT_REPLAY_ENGINE_CLASSES` widen (the agreement witness enforces parity; the shared `payload_child_recoverable` handles nested grandchildren — one source of truth).

**Grounding overturned the v1.90 "no fan-out replay store" anticipation (SAVE_POINT only).** The fan-out branch-capture store is the engine-class-AGNOSTIC `EngineOutputStore`, the fan-out aggregate reconstruction (`_determine_fanout_resume`) consumes ONLY that store (NOT the ESR/WAL-only §8.1 cached-output-replay channel), and the §14.22 effect fence is auto-active for SAVE_POINT (`_DURABLE_AUTO_FENCE_ENGINE_CLASSES` includes all four durable classes). SAVE_POINT is the C-CP-11 §11.2 ABOVE_ENGINE reading — the harness branch store is the sole aggregate authority, no engine-owned competing substrate, NO CAS/F-1 window. RECONCILER (the §11.2 RECONCILER reading — engine owns reconvergence) carries an ungrounded two-authorities + CAS/F-1 question → stays fail-closed, the registered `…-FANOUT-CHILD-RECONCILER` follow-on (the decompose, mirroring #779→#781).

**Cross-topology at-most-once — already covered by the #788 fold (no new hole).** The CP `_payload_engine_signature` dual-gate marker already folds `f"{topology}:{engine}"`, so a fan-out SAVE_POINT signature `parallelization:save-point-checkpoint` is distinct from the bare LINEAR-SAVE_POINT marker and every other combo → a LINEAR↔fan-out or fan-out↔fan-out SAVE_POINT swap fails the dual gate closed. The runtime `_linear_step_disambiguator` likewise already folds topology into the seed. No new identity dimension — `{engine_class, topology_pattern}` stays the complete recovery-selecting pair; SAVE_POINT only adds a member to the already-folded engine axis.

**Invariants.** NO new contract (a constant widen of an existing predicate), NO new fail-class, NO §5.2-hash change (the seed-gating + the linear-seed disambiguator are non-attested / per-run transient), NO `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening, NO new CXA edge. at-most-once PRESERVED (SAVE_POINT fires NO CAS-claim → no F-1 window; the in-flight-branch disposition is the EXISTING B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN family, no new window). **CP spec C-CP-25 §25.15 v1.84 → v1.85** is the paired primary contract. IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`); advisor full-transcript (BEFORE substantive work — the decompose discriminator, the CAN-vs-DOES capture-producer witness, the #788 swap-fold check, the RECONCILER representability tie-breaker) + out-of-family Codex on the diff; NO operator gate (additive recovery for a previously-fail-closed surface, no committed-invariant sacrifice). Witnessed: the predicate verdict flip (fan-out {ESR,WAL,SAVE_POINT}→True + fan-out RECONCILER→False carrier-segregation control + LINEAR scope unaffected), the extended CP↔runtime agreement witness (fanout-child-save-point True / fanout-child-reconciler False / nested-fanout-save-point-grandchild True / nested-fanout-reconciler-grandchild False), the by-execution SAVE_POINT fan-out child crash-resume reconstruction + committed-effect-bearing-branch non-re-fire — RED-without-fix (`test_fanout_child_save_point_reconstructs_aggregate_under_deterministic_seed`), the cross-topology signature fold for the new engine (`test_recursive_signature_catches_save_point_topology_swap`). ## Change-note (v1.89 → v1.90)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-27).** v1.90 records the RUNTIME half of the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-SUBAGENT-FANOUT-CHILD`** — the **case-(a) [the child is itself FAN-OUT]** slice the v1.89 §case-(a) registered (paired with CP spec **v1.83 → v1.84**). But a fan-out child reconstructs at the SEPARATE `_crash_fan_out_resume` site (the B-FANOUT-OUTPUT-REPLAY branch store), not that LINEAR seed. Witnessed: the predicate verdict flip (fan-out {ESR,WAL}→True RED-without-fix + fan-out {SAVE_POINT,RECONCILER}→False carrier-segregation control + the LINEAR scope unaffected), the extended CP↔runtime agreement witness (fan-out-child-esr True / fan-out-child-save-point False / nested-fanout-esr-grandchild True / nested-fanout-save-point-grandchild False), the by-execution fan-out child crash-resume reconstruction + committed-effect-bearing-branch non-re-fire (`test_fanout_child_crash_resume_witness.py`), the cross-topology signature fold (`test_recursive_signature_catches_topology_swap`) + the linear-sequential seed topology fold (`test_linear_sequential_seed_binds_topology`). ## Change-note (v1.88 → v1.89)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-27).** v1.89 records the RUNTIME half of the R-FS-1 standalone arcs **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-SUBAGENT-NONLEAF-CHILD`** (worker) **+ `…-ORCHESTRATOR-…-NONLEAF-CHILD`** — the **case-(b) [nested SUB_AGENT grandchild]** slice (paired with CP spec **v1.82 → v1.83**). The typed mirror predicate `subagent_child_recoverable` (`sub_agent_dispatch.py`) — which gates the composer's deterministic `child_run_id_seed` — is made **RECURSIVE**: a `SINGLE_THREADED_LINEAR` ∧ durable-engine child whose own child step is itself a recoverable `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` (a recursive-leaf grandchild) is now admitted, where the prior leaf-only condition fail-closed on ANY nested sub-agent (`MANAGED_AGENTS` stays hard-excluded). This is a **conjunct-3 semantic relaxation** (a strictly larger recoverable set), NOT a value added to a frozenset. **TWO runtime changes co-land — the predicate alone is a double-fire regression:**

- **(1) ONE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the recoverability decision.** The runtime composer's nested recursion in `subagent_child_recoverable` no longer `SubAgentDispatchPayload.model_validate`s the nested payload — it DELEGATES to the SHARED CP `payload_child_recoverable` (out-of-family Codex [P1]). A runtime-only model_validate would REJECT a partially-valid nested payload (valid `child_manifest_entry`/`child_steps` but missing `child_workflow_id`/`brief`) that the CP defensive mirror ADMITS (CP cannot model_validate — a forbidden `harness_cp`→`harness_runtime` import) → a CP-True/runtime-False drift → the outer child's marker admits re-dispatch while the composer passes NO seed → the outer child re-runs fresh → its committed prefix DOUBLE-FIRES. Delegating to the shared predicate classifies nested payloads IDENTICALLY on both sides (recoverability depends only on engine+topology+child_steps; `child_workflow_id`/`brief` affect DISPATCHABILITY, fail closed at the dispatcher's own model_validate). The by-execution agreement witness (incl. a partially-malformed nested payload) enforces parity.

- **(2) A THIRD deterministic-seed surface (`is_linear_sequential_dispatch`).** The recursive predicate admits a LINEAR child whose nested SUB_AGENT grandchild is dispatched at the `SINGLE_THREADED_LINEAR` inline step loop — a surface the prior seed gating (fan-out worker `branch_index is not None` ∨ orchestrator `is_orchestrator_dispatch`) did NOT cover. Without a seed there, a maybe-ran parent's re-dispatch of that LINEAR child re-dispatches the grandchild with a FRESH `uuid` → the grandchild re-runs fresh → **DOUBLE-FIRE**. The composer now seeds it, gated on the NEW hash-inert `StepExecutionContext.is_linear_sequential_dispatch` flag (the CP driver sets it `True` only on the LINEAR inline loop's per-step context). The linear-loop step is once-per-run — its `(run_id, step_index)` recurs only as a SAME-LOGICAL-STEP forward resume (`resume_at` advances forward; the EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER step-index-reuse hazard never reaches the linear loop) — so a deterministic seed is safe.

**The seed + the recursive marker bind the FULL at-most-once identity tuple `{ordinal, step_id, child_workflow_id, engine_class}` — COMPLETE BY CONSTRUCTION.** This is exactly **(a)** the fields the grandchild run_id derives from (`compose_child_run_id_seed`'s `parent_idempotency_key` IS the child-step-index key → ordinal; `child_workflow_id`; the linear-sequential disambiguator `branch_path = "linear-step:" + json([step_id, engine_class])`) **+ (b)** the field that selects the recovery mechanism (`engine_class` — ESR/WAL replay vs SAVE_POINT vs RECONCILER CAS). Every grandchild-payload field NOT in the tuple — `workload_class`, `persona_tier`, `layer_budgets`, `fallback_chain`, `per_step_overrides`, `hitl_placements`, `brief` — neither derives the run_id nor selects the recovery mechanism; editing it changes how REMAINING (uncommitted) steps run while the committed prefix is auto-resumed (NOT re-fired) — normal at-most-once-safe resume-after-edit. (`topology_pattern` is verdict-enforced LINEAR; a change flips the recoverability verdict → the resumed-side recursive re-computation fails closed.) So any identity-changing edit (rename / reorder / engine swap / re-point) changes BOTH the seed AND the CP recursive marker → the dual gate fails closed before the outer child is recovered → no re-dispatch → no double-fire. **No new contract**, **ONE hash-inert per-step flag** (`is_linear_sequential_dispatch`, the same category as `is_orchestrator_dispatch` — NOT a §6-chain / §5.2-hash contract), **no new fail-class**, **no §5.2-hash change**, **no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening**, **no new CXA edge**. **CP spec C-CP-25 §25.15 v1.82 → v1.83** is the paired primary contract. IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED.

**Case-(a) [the child is itself FAN-OUT] stays fail-closed → registered, not folded** (`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-SUBAGENT-FANOUT-CHILD`): a fan-out child's `final_state` aggregate reconstruction is a separate LINEAR-excluded mechanism (the `reconstruct_final_state` seed site is SINGLE_THREADED_LINEAR-only; the B-FANOUT-OUTPUT-REPLAY family reconstructs a fan-out aggregate through the parent barrier, unwitnessed). The case-(b) close is **parent-agnostic** (the new code is entirely at the child→grandchild seam; the worker/orchestrator difference lives only in the unchanged outer seam #774/#777) — closing both worker + orchestrator with the shared mechanism + the parent-agnostic depth-2 witness (the orchestrator close rests on COMPOSITION with #777, NOT a dedicated orchestrator e2e). FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`); advisor full-transcript (the regression finding, the completeness argument, the honest composition narrative) + out-of-family Codex (6 genuine at-most-once findings, converged round 7) on the diff; NO operator gate (additive recovery for a previously-fail-closed surface, at-most-once PRESERVED). Witnessed: the recursive classifier verdict flip (nested-recoverable→True RED-without-fix + fan-out/PURE_PATTERN/MANAGED grandchild → False controls + depth-3), the CP↔runtime agreement (incl. partially-malformed nested parity), the by-execution **depth-2 crash-resume** (`test_maybe_ran_nonleaf_child_grandchild_auto_resumes_at_most_once` — real `compose_child_workflow_runner` → `execute_workflow` × `RuntimeSubAgentDispatcher`; the grandchild auto-resumes its committed prefix, only the in-flight step re-dispatched — RED→GREEN on the seed, the double-fire fix), the resumed-side stale-verdict + full-identity edit-detection (engine / step_id / ordinal / workflow_id) + the linear-seed step_id+engine binding. Co-published with one `.harness/clearance/` marker (runtime v1.89).

## Change-note (v1.87 → v1.88)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-27).** v1.88 records the RUNTIME half of the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-SUBAGENT-RECONCILER-CHILD`** (paired with CP spec **v1.81 → v1.82**): the typed mirror predicate `subagent_child_recoverable` (`sub_agent_dispatch.py`) — which gates the composer's deterministic `child_run_id_seed` — has its child-engine-class conjunct extended from `{EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY, WAL_SEGMENT, SAVE_POINT_CHECKPOINT}` to **`{EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY, WAL_SEGMENT, SAVE_POINT_CHECKPOINT, RECONCILER_LOOP}`** (the `_SUBAGENT_RECOVERABLE_CHILD_ENGINE_CLASSES` set) — **ALL FOUR durable resumable engine classes** are now members; `PURE_PATTERN_NO_ENGINE` (non-durable, no resume) is the sole non-member. A maybe-ran fan-out / orchestrator `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` whose child is a `SINGLE_THREADED_LINEAR` RECONCILER_LOOP leaf now gets the deterministic seed (so its OWN crash-resume auto-resumes from the durable store) and is admitted by the CP classifier dual gate — recovering instead of failing the run closed. ## Change-note (v1.85 → v1.86)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-26).** v1.86 records the RUNTIME half of the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-ORCHESTRATOR-MAYBE-RAN-SUBAGENT`** (paired with CP spec **v1.77 → v1.78**) — the ORCHESTRATOR analogue of the v1.85 worker arc. ONE §14.7.4 `C-RT-17` mechanism addition:

- **The seed extends to the orchestrator dispatch (`is_orchestrator_dispatch`).** The v1.85 composer threaded the deterministic `child_run_id_seed` ONLY for a **recoverable fan-out worker** (`step_context.branch_index is not None` ∧ `subagent_child_recoverable(payload)`), which EXCLUDED the orchestrator (`steps[0]`, `branch_index is None` — like a sequential-loop iteration). The orchestrator is now ALSO seeded, gated on a NEW hash-inert `StepExecutionContext.is_orchestrator_dispatch` flag (the CP driver sets it `True` only on `_execute_orchestrator_workers`' `orchestrator_context`; RESET `False` on every fan-out child via `compose_branch_child_context`). The orchestrator is a SINGLE, once-per-run step — UNLIKE a loop iteration it dispatches EXACTLY ONCE, so the deterministic seed is SAFE (no iteration-2 to alias iteration-1's store; the loop-suppression hazard the `branch_index is not None` gate forecloses stays foreclosed — `is_orchestrator_dispatch` is `False` for loop iterations). The orchestrator seeds with `branch_path=None` (it is unique within the run, no fan-out siblings); a worker INSERTS its `branch_path`, so `compose_child_run_id_seed(orchestrator_idempotency_key, child_wf, branch_path=None)` stays DISTINCT from any worker's `compose_child_run_id_seed(orchestrator_idempotency_key, child_wf, branch_path)` even on the same `child_workflow_id` (no orchestrator↔worker child aliasing). The seed RE-DERIVES IDENTICALLY on a parent-crash re-dispatch (`orchestrator_idempotency_key` is the deterministic step_index-0 key) → the orchestrator's child auto-resumes from the shared durable store. `is_orchestrator_dispatch=False` (the default, every non-orchestrator dispatch) ⟹ byte-identical to v1.85. The `subagent_child_recoverable` predicate + the `child_run_id_seed` / `ChildWorkflowRunner` E1 mechanism are REUSED VERBATIM from v1.85 (no new typed surface).

The recovery is at-most-once: the orchestrator's effects live at its CHILD's tool sinks (recursively fenced), and the deterministic seed lets the child's OWN crash-resume auto-resume rather than re-fire (the v1.85 compositional-recursive-child property, applied at the orchestrator dispatch site). ## Change-note (v1.84 → v1.85)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-26).** v1.85 records the RUNTIME half of the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-SUBAGENT`** (paired with CP spec **v1.76 → v1.77**): a maybe-ran fan-out **SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH worker** on a strict-tier crash-resume is now RECOVERABLE-by-re-dispatch — unlike a TOOL_STEP (fenced at its own sink) or MANAGED_AGENTS (vendor-session fence), a sub-agent's external effects live at its CHILD's tool sinks, so recovery is **compositional recursive child crash-resume**. Two §14.7.4 `C-RT-17` mechanism additions:

- **E1 — deterministic child run_id (`child_run_id_seed`).** `ChildWorkflowRunner.__call__` gains an additive `child_run_id_seed: str | None = None` kwarg. On a FIRST dispatch (no `pause_snapshot_input`) the runner prefers the composer-supplied deterministic seed over a fresh `uuid.uuid4().hex`; on a resume it keeps reusing the snapshot's run_id (unchanged). The seed (`compose_child_run_id_seed`) is `sha256("child-run:" + parent_idempotency_key + ":" + branch_path + ":" + child_workflow_id)`. **`branch_path` (§25.16 `{parent_action_id}:{branch_index}`) is REQUIRED for a fan-out worker (out-of-family Codex [P1]):** `compose_branch_child_context` inherits `parent_idempotency_key` VERBATIM from the fan-out parent (the branch-distinct key is composed downstream, NOT folded into `parent_idempotency_key`), so two sibling workers dispatching the same `child_workflow_id` would otherwise derive the SAME child run_id → aliased durable store/fence state EVEN WITHOUT A CRASH. The seed RE-DERIVES IDENTICALLY on a parent-crash re-dispatch (run key recovered from the preserved run_id; step_index + branch_index are deterministic manifest positions) → the child's durable store + effect-fence reserves are recoverable → the child's OWN crash-resume auto-resumes from the shared store, with result-faithful `final_state` reconstruction (B-CHILD-CRASH-RESUME-FINAL-STATE-RECONSTRUCT, v1.75). `None` ⟹ legacy fresh-`uuid` (byte-identical to pre-arc).
- **The recoverability predicate (`subagent_child_recoverable`) + seed-gating.** The composer threads the seed ONLY for a **recoverable fan-out worker** — `step_context.branch_index is not None` ∧ `subagent_child_recoverable(payload)`, where recoverable ⟺ (child engine ∈ `{EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY, WAL_SEGMENT}`) ∧ (child topology == `SINGLE_THREADED_LINEAR`) ∧ (no child step is `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` / `MANAGED_AGENTS`). Three conjuncts, each a fail-closed boundary: a SAVE_POINT/RECONCILER child has no durable output store → suffix-only `final_state` → fold corruption (the registered `…-SAVE-POINT-RECONCILER` arc); a fan-out child engages its OWN unwitnessed fan-out reconstruction; a nested sub-agent / managed child step is deeper recursion / an unfenced vendor sink. A non-recoverable / non-fan-out dispatch → `None` → fresh `uuid` → pre-existing behavior (no auto-resume → no suffix-only corruption). **Restricting to `branch_index is not None` also EXCLUDES the sequential-loop topologies (EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER / RECONCILER_LOOP)** whose iterated steps reuse the same declared `step_index` (→ same `parent_idempotency_key`) across iterations — a deterministic seed there would make loop iteration 2 auto-resume iteration 1's store (the loop-suppression hazard finding-v1 §2 named). At-most-once PRESERVED — the child still runs once on the happy path; on a re-dispatch the stable per-branch key lets the child's own crash-resume auto-resume. FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`); design-vetted advisor full-transcript (BEFORE substantive work — the GO + the corrected predicate + the seed-gating correction over the #746 reverted branch) + out-of-family Codex on the diff (caught the [P1] sibling-collision — branch_path + fan-out-worker scope added in response) + the loop-suppression empirical confirmation at `workflow_driver.py:2040`; NO operator gate (additive recovery for a previously-fail-closed surface, no committed-invariant sacrifice, at-most-once preserved). Witnessed by the E1-live full-chain reconstruction (`test_recursive_child_crash_resume_final_state_witness.py`) + the recoverability-predicate negative controls + the fan-out sibling-distinctness witnesses (`test_lifecycle_sub_agent_dispatch.py`). ## Change-note (v1.81 → v1.82)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-25).** v1.82 marks the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-MAYBE-RAN-UNFENCED-EXTERNAL`** BUILT — the §14.22 C-RT-31 effect fence is EXTENDED to the §14.20 C-RT-28 `MANAGED_AGENTS` vendor-session sink. MANAGED_AGENTS was the ONE effect-bearing fan-out kind with NO fence at all (its `create_session` + `send_event` vendor effect reaches no tool sink), so the #742 TOOL_STEP fence-recovery slice left a maybe-ran fan-out MANAGED_AGENTS worker fail-closed. With the fence extended, a maybe-ran MANAGED_AGENTS branch on a strict-tier crash-resume now RECOVERS (suppress-with-captured-outcome / ambiguous-PAUSE / fresh-fire) instead of failing closed. Paired CP delta **v1.66 → v1.67** (the consumer classifier: MANAGED_AGENTS added to `_FANOUT_MAYBE_RAN_FENCE_RECOVERABLE_KIND_VALUES` + a same-kind-equality guard). FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`); design-vetted advisor full-transcript + out-of-family Codex (3-round convergence) + direct grounding; NO operator gate (additive fence extension, no committed-invariant sacrifice); WHOLE close → `standalone_registered` 6 → 5.

**The build (§14.20 C-RT-28 dispatcher fence integration).** `ManagedAgentsStepDispatcher` gains an additive `effect_fence: EffectFenceProtocol | None = None` + `effect_fencing_explicit: bool = False` (both default to the pre-arc byte-identical no-fence path). The stage-5 `materialize_managed_agents_dispatcher_stage` factory threads a `RuntimeEffectFence` over the SAME `repository_root/.harness/effect-fence` claim dir as the tool dispatcher (the key namespaces are disjoint — see the key recipe below — so sharing the dir is collision-free). The dispatch applies the §14.22 fence gate VERBATIM (the tool-dispatcher precedent): the per-run gate is `effect_fencing_explicit OR step_context.run_engine_class ∈ _DURABLE_AUTO_FENCE_ENGINE_CLASSES` (managed agents is never `idempotent`, so no per-tool exemption); the dispatch **reserves before** `create_session` and **captures the outcome after** a validated success ONLY; on a lost reserve it applies the key-bound directive (RE_FIRE via `try_consume_refire` + `clear_claim` → fire fresh; SKIP_AS_FIRED → an empty-but-fully-keyed outcome; ABORT → raise `EffectFenceAbortedError`) else the captured-output split (present → suppress-and-fold-verbatim; absent/corrupt → raise `EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError` → §26.2 PAUSE). The whole gate is guarded on `effect_fence is not None`, so a fence-bound dispatcher always receives a real `step_context` (the CP driver composes one at every dispatch site) while an unbound dispatcher skips the block (the pre-arc path a unit test may exercise with no context).

**The key recipe (the payload-independent leading-domain-tag — out-of-family Codex [P2]).** The fence key is `H("managed_agents" : parent_idempotency_key : step_id)` — sha256, the domain tag in the LEADING slot. The tool key is `H(parent : step_id : tool_id)` (§14.9.7); a TRAILING `:managed_agents` tag (the first draft) would be byte-identical to a TOOL_STEP whose `tool_id == "managed_agents"` at the same `(parent, step_id)` → a cross-sink fence collision against the shared claim dir. Leading the tag makes the key disjoint from EVERY tool key by construction (a collision would require a harness-composed `parent_idempotency_key` to begin with the literal `managed_agents:`, which a run key never is). The key carries NO `agent_id` / payload component → a resumed agent-swap under the same `step_id` composes the SAME key → it is SUPPRESSED (returns the prior captured outcome), accepted-parity-or-stricter vs the cleared TOOL_STEP tool-swap (which keys on `tool_id` → fires fresh) — per-key at-most-once preserved.

**Why MANAGED_AGENTS is a LEAF (result-fidelity by construction — the contrast with the reverted #746 SUBAGENT slice).** The managed-agents dispatch returns ONE opaque outcome mapping with NO harness-side reconstruction; a fence suppress returns the CAPTURED outcome verbatim → the fan-out parent folds the exact original outcome. The #746 SUBAGENT slice was reverted because a deterministic-run_id child re-dispatch engages the child's OWN recursive fan-out reconstruction → a suffix-only/empty child `final_state`; that recursive-RESULT-fidelity trap does NOT transfer to a leaf. The disposition matrix is sound: a non-success terminal status and a poll-budget exhaustion both raise WITHOUT capturing → the claim is held + no output → a resume is genuinely ambiguous → §26.2 PAUSE (never a false suppress of a failed outcome).

**Scope discipline.** v1.82 is **change-note-level** (the §14.22 C-RT-31 fence contract + the §14.20 C-RT-28 managed-agents dispatcher are the existing carriers; the `effect_fence` / `effect_fencing_explicit` fields + the dispatch fence gate are an additive integration mirroring the v1.60–v1.73 tool-dispatcher fence). The §14.20.1–.7 + §14.22.1–.9 + the v1.59–v1.81 narrative are PRESERVED VERBATIM. **No new contract** (additive fields on C-RT-28), **no new fail-class** (reuses `EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError` / `EffectFenceAbortedError` + the §26.2 EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS pause), **no §5.2-hash change** (the fence claim/output is a sidecar, not a state-ledger entry, not in the §6 chain), **no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening** (the fence rides the dispatcher's own fields + the existing hash-inert `StepExecutionContext.effect_fence_resolution` channel), **no new CXA edge**. **CP spec C-CP-25 §25.12 / §25.15 v1.66 → v1.67** is the paired consumer contract (the fence-recoverable classifier extension + the same-kind guard). IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. The impl: `harness-runtime` (`managed_agents_dispatch.py` — the fence fields + the `_compose_managed_agents_idempotency_key` leading-domain-tag composer + the dispatch gate + capture; `managed_agents_dispatcher_factory.py` — the fence threading); `harness-cp` (`workflow_driver.py` — the recoverable-set + same-kind conjunct). Decorrelated review: advisor full-transcript (the LEAF-vs-recursive distinction; the disposition-matrix risk surface; the same-kind + payload-independent-key constraints) + out-of-family Codex on the diff (R1 pyright redeclaration / R2 the fence-key collision / R3 clean). Witnesses: 14 real-fence dispatcher witnesses through a counting vendor port (`test_managed_agents_dispatch_effect_fence.py`) + 8 CP classifier units (`test_workflow_driver_managed_agents_fence_classifier.py`) + 2 full-chain witnesses — MANAGED_AGENTS recovers + cross-kind-swap fails closed (`test_workflow_driver_fanout_output_replay_full_chain.py`).

## Change-note (v1.80 → v1.81)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-25).** v1.81 records the §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` extension paired with the CP `B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-ORCHESTRATOR-MAYBE-RAN-RESOLUTION` build (CP spec **v1.63 → v1.64**): the ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS `steps[0]` orchestrator dispatched-marker now records the orchestrator's **DISPATCH-TIME step kind**, and a new read method exposes it, so the CP orchestrator-maybe-ran re-fire-safety classifier keys on the ORIGINAL kind rather than the (possibly changed) resumed manifest's kind — the single-orchestrator analogue of the v1.80 per-branch dispatched-marker kind extension. FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`); design-vetted advisor full-transcript ×2 + the orchestrator-kind-reachability grep + out-of-family Codex; NO operator gate.

**The build (§14.23 C-RT-32 orchestrator dispatched-marker kind extension + cardinality presence reader).** `record_orchestrator_dispatched(run_key, step_id)` gains a `step_kind: str` parameter — `record_orchestrator_dispatched(run_key, step_id, step_kind)` — persisting the orchestrator's dispatch-time step kind alongside the existing `step_id` in the same single `{sha256(run_key)}.branches/orchestrator.dispatched` marker (a `{"step_id": …, "step_kind": …}` JSON line; same crash-atomic `_append_path`, the v1.80 branch-marker shape). A new read method `orchestrator_dispatched_kind(run_key) → str | None` returns the orchestrator's recorded dispatch-time kind (the single-orchestrator analogue of the v1.80 worker `dispatched_branch_kinds`). A marker missing / with an unreadable / non-str `step_kind` (a pre-v1.81 v1.79-era orchestrator marker, which recorded only `step_id`, or a torn write) maps to `None`. Presence remains the v1.79 fail-closed signal (`orchestrator_dispatched`); the kind is best-effort and `None`-on-absence. **Additionally** the store gains a presence-only `fanout_cardinality_present(run_key) → bool` (a sibling of the existing `read_fanout_cardinality`, mirroring `orchestrator_present` / `present_dispatched_indexes`): it returns whether the cardinality MARKER file exists, distinct from `read_fanout_cardinality` which returns `None` for BOTH an absent AND a present-but-TORN marker. The CP orchestrator re-fire-safe relaxation keys its corruption guard on this presence (a torn cardinality still proves the run advanced past orchestrator capture — `[[durable-recovery-presence-validity-scope]]`).

**Why the dispatch-time kind (the at-most-once changed-manifest guard).** The CP orchestrator-maybe-ran re-fire-safety relaxation (CP spec v1.64 §1) re-dispatches a maybe-ran orchestrator only when its dispatch-time kind is re-fire-safe (`{DECLARATIVE_STEP, INFERENCE_STEP}` — no non-idempotent external effect; the common ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS shape where `steps[0]` is an LLM that farms sub-tasks). Reading the kind from the RESUMED manifest would open the same at-most-once hole the v1.80 worker extension closed: a same-shape changed-manifest resume that re-supplies an effect-bearing-dispatched orchestrator as a re-fire-safe kind would be mis-classified safe and re-dispatched, double-firing the original effect. Recording the kind IN THE MARKER at dispatch time makes the classifier immune to manifest changes; an un-kinded (pre-v1.81 / torn) marker fails closed (cannot prove re-fire-safety — the conservative reading preserves the v1.79 behavior exactly). A re-dispatch records the marker afresh with the resumed kind (idempotent, last-wins).

**Scope discipline.** v1.81 is **change-note-level** (the §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` is the existing carrier; the orchestrator dispatched-marker kind field + read method are an additive sibling extension of the v1.79 orchestrator-marker API + the v1.80 branch-marker-kind precedent). The §14.23.1–.7 + §14.24 + the v1.59–v1.80 narrative are PRESERVED VERBATIM. **No new contract** (a field + read method on C-RT-32), **no new fail-class in the runtime** (the CP consumer maps an effect-bearing / un-kinded maybe-ran orchestrator to the existing CP-side `fan-out-crash-resume-orchestrator-maybe-ran`), **no §5.2-hash change** (the marker is non-attested — not a state-ledger entry, not in the §6 chain), **no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening**, **no new CXA edge** (the store is consumed via the `cp_is_wiring` getattr idiom). **CP spec C-CP-25 §25.12 / §25.15 v1.63 → v1.64** is the paired primary contract. IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. The impl: `harness-runtime` (`engine_output_store.py` — the `step_kind` param on `record_orchestrator_dispatched` + the `orchestrator_dispatched_kind` reader); `harness-cp` (the orchestrator-block reserve site passes `str(orchestrator_step.step_kind.value)` + `_determine_fanout_resume` keys the orchestrator-maybe-ran classification on `orchestrator_dispatched_kind`). Decorrelated review: advisor full-transcript ×2 (the design proposal + the decomposition reconcile, where advisor reversed its own "build the pause-route" steer once grounded against the v1.62 worker precedent) + the orchestrator-kind-reachability grep (confirms the orchestrator `steps[0]` kind is unconstrained → the effect-bearing leg is a real registered follow-on, not vacuous) + out-of-family Codex on the diff. Witnesses: the real-store `orchestrator_dispatched_kind` round-trip + distinct-from-`step_id` across restart (`test_engine_output_store.py`) + the full-chain re-fire-safe-recovers / effect-bearing-fails-closed / changed-manifest-fails-closed / pre-v1.81-marker-fails-closed (`test_workflow_driver_fanout_output_replay_full_chain.py`).

**Why the dispatch-time kind (the at-most-once changed-manifest guard — out-of-family Codex [P1]).** The CP maybe-ran re-fire-safety relaxation (CP spec v1.62 §1) re-dispatches a maybe-ran branch only when its step kind is re-fire-safe (no non-idempotent external effect). Reading the kind from the RESUMED manifest opened an at-most-once hole: on a same-cardinality changed-manifest resume, a branch that dispatched as an effect-bearing `TOOL_STEP` and crashed before terminal capture could be re-supplied at the same ordinal as a re-fire-safe `DECLARATIVE_STEP`/`INFERENCE_STEP` — the classifier would mark it safe and re-dispatch, double-firing the original tool effect. Recording the kind IN THE MARKER at dispatch time makes the classifier immune to manifest changes: a maybe-ran branch is classified by its original dispatch-time kind, and an un-kinded (pre-arc / torn) marker fails closed (cannot prove re-fire-safety). A re-dispatch records the marker afresh with the resumed kind (idempotent, last-wins; only relevant once the branch is provably re-dispatched).

## Change-note (v1.78 → v1.79)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-24).** v1.79 marks the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-ORCHESTRATOR-DISPATCH`** BUILT — the **reserve-before-DISPATCH** at-most-once primitive extended to the ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS `steps[0]` orchestrator's OWN sequential dispatch. v1.78 added reserve-before-DISPATCH for fan-out WORKER/PEER branches but explicitly left the orchestrator's own dispatch-before-capture window OUT (CP spec v1.60 §1 scope note). This delta closes it: a crash in the orchestrator's fire→capture window is now provably-not-run (no marker → fresh re-run) or maybe-ran (marker present, no capture → fail closed) rather than a silent re-dispatch of `steps[0]` → a double-fire on the compliance tier. The §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` gains an **orchestrator dispatched-marker sibling method pair**; the CP driver gains the strict-tier orchestrator-block write site + the orchestrator-dispatch classification that consumes it (paired CP spec **v1.60 → v1.61**). FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`); design-vetted advisor full-transcript + the §25.15 at-most-once probe (no council); NO operator gate.

**The build (§14.23 C-RT-32 orchestrator reserve-before-dispatch API).** `EngineOutputStore` gains sibling methods to the v1.78 branch dispatched-marker API: `record_orchestrator_dispatched(run_key, step_id)` + `orchestrator_dispatched(run_key) → bool` (a SINGLE per-run marker — there is exactly one orchestrator — a `{sha256(run_key)}.branches/orchestrator.dispatched` file, no collision with the `orchestrator.jsonl` reserve-before-COMMIT capture file). The CP driver writes the marker SYNCHRONOUSLY + fsynced STRICTLY BEFORE the orchestrator body dispatches; the orchestrator dispatch is itself SYNCHRONOUS (no `ensure_future` / yield between the marker write and the dispatch), so unlike the worker path no atomicity dance is needed — no false-positive marker is possible. Within an instrumented run, marker-absent ⟺ the orchestrator's effect did NOT fire. Same crash-atomic `_append_path` (fsync + ancestor-dir fsync) as the branch markers; same `_fanout_replay_store` gate; gated by the same per-run `record_dispatch_instrumented` cross-version stamp (also written in the orchestrator block before the dispatch).

**Why presence-only.** `orchestrator_dispatched` is presence-only (a torn/unreadable marker still proves dispatch began → the conservative maybe-ran reading). The CP at-most-once decision keys on the orchestrator marker's **presence alone** + the absent terminal capture: present marker + no `read_orchestrator_output` ⟹ maybe-ran ⟹ the CP driver fails closed; absent marker ⟹ provably-not-run / pre-arc ⟹ fresh re-run. The cross-version guard is INHERENT — `orchestrator.dispatched` is a NEW file written only by the instrumented code, so a pre-arc journal carries none (→ fresh); the classifier needs NO dispatch-instrumented stamp gate, and an orphaned marker without the stamp (an inconsistent store, since the stamp is written before the marker) still fails closed rather than re-dispatching fresh (out-of-family Codex [P2]).

**Scope discipline.** v1.79 is **change-note-level** (the §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` is the existing carrier; the orchestrator dispatched-marker API is a sibling extension, the v1.78 branch-marker precedent). The §14.23.1–.7 + §14.24 + the v1.59–v1.78 narrative are PRESERVED VERBATIM. **No new contract** (sibling methods on C-RT-32), **no new fail-class in the runtime** (the CP consumer maps a maybe-ran orchestrator to `RunStatus.FAILED` via the NEW CP-side `fan-out-crash-resume-orchestrator-maybe-ran`; the runtime store raises no new taxonomy), **no §5.2-hash change** (the marker is non-attested — not a state-ledger entry, not in the §6 chain), **no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening**, **no new CXA edge** (the store is consumed via the `cp_is_wiring` getattr idiom). **CP spec C-CP-25 §25.12 / §25.15 v1.60 → v1.61** is the paired primary contract. IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. The impl: `harness-runtime` (`engine_output_store.py` orchestrator dispatched-marker API); `harness-cp` (the orchestrator reserve-before-dispatch marker + stamp at the `_execute_orchestrator_workers` dispatch block + the `_determine_fanout_resume` orchestrator maybe-ran classification + the PARALLELIZATION topology-mismatch widening + the `_FanOutStoreOrchestratorMaybeRanError` → FAILED mapping). Decorrelated review: advisor (the synchronous-dispatch-needs-no-atomicity-dance simplification; the maybe-ran residual + the PROCEED-window-isn't-covered-by-#724 catch → the registered follow-on; the `_append_path`-fsync confirmation; the HIERARCHICAL nesting witness) + out-of-family Codex on the diff. Witnesses: the real-store orchestrator-marker round-trip + distinct-from-capture across restart (`test_engine_output_store.py`) + the full-chain crash→resume through the REAL `execute_workflow` (`test_workflow_driver_fanout_output_replay_full_chain.py`: orchestrator maybe-ran fails closed under CASCADE_CANCEL + PAUSE + HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION; provably-not-run recovers fresh re-firing the orchestrator once; PARALLELIZATION orchestrator-marker topology-mismatch fails closed; PROCEED writes no marker) + the `_determine_fanout_resume` isolation unit tests (maybe-ran raises; an orphaned marker without the stamp fails closed [the inconsistent-store case, never fresh]; provably-not-run [no marker] → fresh).

## Change-note (v1.77 → v1.78)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-24).** v1.78 marks the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-CRASH-RESUME-STRICT-TIER-INCOMPLETE`** BUILT — the **reserve-before-DISPATCH** at-most-once primitive for fan-out branches that lets a strict-tier (PAUSE / CASCADE_CANCEL) crash-resume re-dispatch ONLY the PROVABLY-not-run branches instead of failing closed on any incomplete recovery. The §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` gains a **dispatched-marker + instrumented-stamp sidecar API**; the CP driver gains the strict-tier write sites + the incomplete-recovery classification that consumes it (paired CP spec **v1.59 → v1.60**). The fan-out analogue of the §14.22 C-RT-31 effect-fence's `try_reserve` at branch granularity. FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`); design-vetted advisor full-transcript + the §25.15 at-most-once probe (no council); NO operator gate.

**The build (§14.23 C-RT-32 reserve-before-dispatch API).** `EngineOutputStore` gains sibling methods to the v1.55 branch API: `record_branch_dispatched(run_key, branch_index, step_id)` + `present_dispatched_indexes(run_key) → set[int]` (the per-(run, branch) dispatch markers — a per-branch `{sha256(run_key)}.branches/branch-{i}.dispatched` file, no collision with the `branch-*.jsonl` terminal-capture files) + `record_dispatch_instrumented(run_key)` + `dispatch_instrumented(run_key) → bool` (the per-run cross-version stamp — a `{sha256(run_key)}.branches/dispatch-instrumented.marker` file). The CP driver writes the marker SYNCHRONOUSLY + fsynced STRICTLY BEFORE the branch dispatches (atomic with the dispatch scheduling), so within an instrumented run marker-absent ⟺ effect-not-fired. Same crash-atomic `_append_path` (`O_EXCL`/`os.link`-class fsync + ancestor-dir fsync) as the branch capture; same `_fanout_replay_store` gate.

**Why marker presence, not a readability gate.** `present_dispatched_indexes` is presence-only (unlike `present_branch_indexes − read_branch_records`, the capture's present-vs-readable discriminator). A dispatch marker proves only that the branch BEGAN dispatch (its effect MAY have fired); a torn/unreadable marker still proves dispatch began, which is the conservative reading (treat as maybe-ran → fail closed). The at-most-once decision keys on the set difference `present_dispatched_indexes − recovered`: empty (every dispatched branch was captured) + the instrumented stamp ⟹ every absent branch is provably not-yet-run ⟹ the CP driver re-dispatches only those; non-empty ⟹ a maybe-ran branch ⟹ fail closed.

**The cross-version stamp (the presence-validity guard).** The "no marker ⟹ not-run" invariant holds only for runs the marker-instrumented code wrote from the start. A PRE-arc crash journal has no markers for ANY branch, including a maybe-ran one. The per-run `dispatch_instrumented` stamp (written at fan-out start by the new code only) is the guard: the CP classifier trusts the markers ONLY when the stamp is present, else retains the v1.57/CP-v1.60 conservative incomplete-recovery fail-closed (`[[durable-recovery-presence-validity-scope]]`).

**Scope discipline.** v1.78 is **change-note-level** (the §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` is the existing carrier; the dispatched-marker + stamp API is a sibling extension, the v1.55 branch-API / v1.56 synthesis-API precedent). The §14.23.1–.7 + §14.24 + the v1.59–v1.77 narrative are PRESERVED VERBATIM. **No new contract** (sibling methods on C-RT-32), **no new fail-class in the runtime** (the CP consumer maps a maybe-ran / un-stamped incomplete recovery to `RunStatus.FAILED` via the retained `fan-out-crash-resume-cascade-policy-incomplete-recovery`; the runtime store raises no new taxonomy), **no §5.2-hash change** (the markers + stamp are non-attested — not state-ledger entries, not in the §6 chain), **no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening**, **no new CXA edge** (the store is consumed via the `cp_is_wiring` getattr idiom). **CP spec C-CP-25 §25.12 / §25.15 v1.59 → v1.60** is the paired primary contract. IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. The impl: `harness-runtime` (`engine_output_store.py` dispatched-marker + stamp API); `harness-cp` (the `_mark_branch_dispatched` reserve-before-dispatch helper at the strict-tier dispatch sites + the dispatch-instrumented stamp + the two consume-site classifications). Decorrelated review: advisor (the cross-version double-fire hazard → the instrumented stamp; the synchronous-marker atomicity catch; the index-scheme-agnostic `dispatched − recovered` classification) + out-of-family Codex on the diff. Witnesses: the real-store marker/stamp round-trip across restart (`test_engine_output_store.py`) + the full-chain crash→resume through the REAL `execute_workflow` (`test_workflow_driver_fanout_output_replay_full_chain.py`: provably-not-run incomplete recovers + re-dispatches only the not-run branch under PAUSE / CASCADE_CANCEL / ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS; cardinality-only no-dispatch recovers fresh; maybe-ran fails closed; mixed not-run+maybe-ran fails closed; the cross-version un-stamped journal fails closed; the no-double-fire witness).

## Change-note (v1.76 → v1.77)

**Status posture (BUILT 2026-06-24).** v1.77 marks the **PR2 slice** of the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-OUTPUT-REPLAY`** BUILT — the **synthesis self-hash + captured-synthesis-output replay** that RELAXES the v1.76 / CP v1.55 §3 synthesis-bearing crash-resume fail-closed. The §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` gains a **synthesis-output sidecar API**; the CP driver gains the capture + replay that consumes it (paired CP spec **v1.55 → v1.56**). A terminal `POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` fan-out (§14.24 C-RT-33) that crash-resumes under `CascadePolicy.PROCEED` now REPLAYS its captured aggregate (the W3 window — a crash after synthesis-capture) instead of failing closed, or — for a crash BEFORE the synthesis ran — re-dispatches fresh on the reproduced branches. The slice the operator already RATIFIED at the §25.12-D1 gate (A, #721: "the synthesis output gets a record-local capture-time self-hash either way"); sequenced as the PR2 follow-on per v1.76. FULL-SPEC. Design body: `.harness/r-fs-1-b-fanout-output-replay-impl-design.md`.

**The build (§14.23 C-RT-32 synthesis sidecar API).** `EngineOutputStore` gains `record_synthesis(run_key, step_id, output, self_hash)` + `read_synthesis(run_key) → (step_id, output, self_hash) | None` + `synthesis_present(run_key) → bool` (a per-run `{sha256(run_key)}.branches/synthesis.jsonl` sidecar, sibling to the orchestrator record). The record carries a **record-local capture-time self-hash** — sha256 over canonical JSON of `(step_id, output)`, computed by the CP caller (the `_compute_snapshot_hash` shape). This is the synthesis's ONLY integrity gate: the synthesis is non-deterministic and carries NO ledger `response_hash` (the #719 C9 residual), so on a W3 crash the store is its sole authority with nothing to cross-check. The CP consumer recomputes + verifies the self-hash on replay (fail-closed on mismatch); a record missing the `self_hash` field (a pre-PR2 / tampered capture) is treated as UNREADABLE (`synthesis_present` True + `read_synthesis` None → fail closed). Capture is **RESERVE-before-COMMIT** (fsynced BEFORE the synthesis terminal ledger-append), gated on the SAME `_fanout_replay_store` predicate as the branch capture.

**Reproducibility scope (the honesty boundary).** PR2 reproducibility covers the **post-capture W3 window ONLY**: a crash AFTER the synthesis was captured → REPLAY the captured aggregate (byte-identical). A crash BEFORE the synthesis ran → fresh dispatch on the reproduced branches (a NEW non-deterministic compose; consistent but NOT byte-reproducible). The synthesis is effect-free, so a fresh re-dispatch fires no duplicate effect. See CP spec v1.56 §1.

**The PAUSE-resume synthesis path stays FAIL-CLOSED.** Only the CRASH-resume synthesis fail-closed is lifted. The explicit-pause synthesis reject (`post-join-synthesis-on-resume-unsupported`) is unchanged — the registered `B-FANOUT-PAUSE-SYNTHESIS` follow-on (it needs a synthesis identity on the `PauseSnapshot` carrier).
