## Change-note (v1.75 → v1.76)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-23).** v1.76 marks the §14.23.7 / §14.21.7-registered follow-on **concurrent-fan-out output recording BUILT** — the **PR1 core slice** of the R-FS-1 standalone arc **`B-FANOUT-OUTPUT-REPLAY`**. The §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` gains a **non-attested, branch-index-KEYED fan-out branch sidecar API**, and the CP driver gains the fan-out crash-resume entry that consumes it (paired CP spec **v1.54 → v1.55**). This makes the DETERMINISTIC fan-out fold crash-resume-reproducible: a concurrent fan-out (`PARALLELIZATION` / `ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS` / `HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION`) that crashes mid-execution replays its completed branches from the durable store on resume (each fires AT-MOST-ONCE across crash+resume) and re-dispatches only the incomplete ones; the recovered aggregate AND the re-materialized ledger are identical to the no-crash trajectory. **OPERATOR-RATIFIED** (A — the non-attested keyed sidecar, AskUserQuestion 2026-06-23, #721); design-vetted C1⊥C9 dyadic council #719 + advisor. FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`). Design body: `.harness/r-fs-1-b-fanout-output-replay-impl-design.md`.

**The build (§14.23 C-RT-32 branch sidecar API).** `EngineOutputStore` gains sibling methods to the linear `record` / `read_outputs`: `record_branch(run_key, branch_index, step_id, terminal_status, output | None)` + `read_branch_records(run_key) → {branch_index: (step_id, terminal_status, output | None)}` + `present_branch_indexes(run_key) → set[int]` + `record_orchestrator` / `read_orchestrator_output` / `orchestrator_present`. The store records the terminal **DISPOSITION** (`completed` with/without output, `timed_out`, and — v1.84, additive — `scoped_aborted`) for every branch — not just clean successes — so a crash-resume distinguishes recover-and-fold, recover-as-terminal (ran-and-errored, effect landed → never re-dispatched), fail-closed (`timed_out`, ambiguous), and operator-scoped-aborted (`scoped_aborted` — `ABORT_BRANCH`, CP v1.74 §1: output `None`, never re-dispatched, distinguished from a ran-and-errored `completed`-no-output so the CP crash-resume reconstruct reproduces the in-resume all-abort FAILED; the read-back closed-set guard accepts it, an unknown value still failing closed as corruption); an output-only schema made every non-clean-success disposition invisible (the at-most-once fail-open class). `_append_path` fsyncs every newly-created ancestor directory (not just the leaf) so the first sidecar write's dirents are durable. Each branch is captured to its OWN per-branch file (`{sha256(run_key)}.branches/branch-{branch_index}.jsonl` — N concurrent branch writers, no shared-file contention; the linear store is single-writer), **RESERVE-before-COMMIT** (fsynced BEFORE the branch's terminal ledger-append, the same skew discipline as the linear `_record_durable_step_output`). The `present_branch_indexes − read_branch_outputs.keys()` difference is the per-branch **present-vs-readable** fail-closed discriminator (the branch-level analogue of `journal_exists`): a branch file that EXISTS but yields no parseable record is corruption / tamper → the CP consumer fails closed (never silently re-dispatches a corrupt branch). The store is the **SOLE which-branches-completed authority** on a fan-out crash-resume — the §25.12 D1.b concurrent-fan-out ledger is BINARY (branch terminals buffer + drain ATOMICALLY at the barrier), so a mid-fan-out crash leaves the ledger empty but the per-branch journals hold the completed outputs.

**The D1 framing CORRECTION (supersedes the v1.74/v1.75 forward-note).** v1.74 §14.21.7 + v1.75 change-note framed this follow-on as requiring *"a NEW durable per-branch-completion substrate committing in COMPLETION order — which sacrifices §25.12 D1 ... a SECOND committed-invariant sacrifice."* The **#719 C1⊥C9 council corrected that (a Class-3 over-claim) and the operator ratified the corrected mechanism (#721).** §25.12 D1 scopes the **ATTESTED LEDGER's** append order, NOT a recovery substrate's physical write order. The sidecar is **non-attested**: it commits in completion order but reads back by `branch_index` and is **NOT part of the §6 hash chain** (exactly the linear `EngineOutputStore` precedent, #665 — landed with no §25.12 amendment). On resume the recovered + re-dispatched branches drain at the barrier in branch-index order → the attested chain is order-identical to a no-crash run. **§25.12 D1 is PRESERVED LITERALLY — no second sacrifice.** See CP spec v1.55 §4.

**Synthesis-bearing crash-resume is FAIL-CLOSED in this slice; the relax is PR2.** A `POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` fan-out (§14.24 C-RT-33) that crash-resumes is fail-closed (CP spec v1.55 §3 — the §14.24 synthesis would otherwise re-dispatch FRESH, a non-reproducible W3-window aggregate). The synthesis self-hash + captured-synthesis-output replay that RELAXES it (the #719 C9 residual: the synthesis output is the one non-deterministic, no-ledger-digest, sole-authority residual warranting a record-local capture-time self-hash) is the **registered PR2 follow-on slice** — which flips the arc-ledger `registered → built` → `closure_gate.py` G1.1 → R-FS-1 resolves. NOT this slice.

**Scope discipline.** v1.76 is **change-note-level** (the §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore` contract body is the existing carrier; the branch API is a sibling extension, the linear `record`/`read_outputs` precedent). The §14.23.1–.7 + §14.24 + the v1.59–v1.75 narrative are PRESERVED VERBATIM. **No new contract** (sibling methods on the existing C-RT-32 store), **no new fail-class** (a corrupt branch / inconsistent store maps to the CP driver's `RunStatus.FAILED` via `fan-out-crash-resume-store-corrupt` / `post-join-synthesis-on-resume-unsupported`; the runtime store raises no new taxonomy code), **no §5.2-hash change** (the sidecar is non-attested — not a state-ledger entry, not in the §6 chain), **no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening**, **no new CXA edge** (the recovery reuses the existing pause-resume `FanOutResumeState`/`resume_snapshot` seam; the store is consumed via the `cp_is_wiring` getattr idiom — harness-cp does not import the runtime store type). **CP spec C-CP-25 §25.12 v1.54 → v1.55** is the paired primary contract. IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. The impl: `harness-runtime` (`engine_output_store.py` branch sidecar API); `harness-cp` (`_fanout_replay_store` shared gate + the 3 capture sites + `_determine_fanout_resume` + the `_execute_workflow_body` crash-resume entry + the `crash_fan_out_resume` strategy threading + the synthesis-crash fail-closed). Decorrelated review: advisor (the store-as-authority correction + the synthesis-crash open-path catch + the shared-gate / wire-both-or-fail-closed traps) + out-of-family Codex on the diff. Witnesses: the real-store on-disk round-trip (crash+restart across a fresh store instance, `test_engine_output_store.py`) + the full-chain crash→resume through the REAL `execute_workflow` (`test_workflow_driver_fanout_output_replay_full_chain.py`: fire-once, incomplete-re-dispatch, aggregate-matches-no-crash, orchestrator+worker recovery, top-level HIERARCHICAL, corrupt-store fail-closed, synthesis-crash fail-closed, no-store byte-identical negative control) + the `_determine_fanout_resume` isolation unit tests.

## Change-note (v1.74 → v1.75)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-23).** v1.75 marks the v1.74-registered gated arc **`B-POSTJOIN-LLM-SYNTHESIS` BUILT** — the opt-in `StepKind.POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` terminal step's RUNTIME consumer contract. Adds a NEW **§14.24 C-RT-33** (`PostJoinSynthesisStepDispatcher`), the runtime half paired with **CP spec v1.53 → v1.54** (the §5.2/§25.2 StepKind 6→7 + the §25.12 Point-2 aggregator-purity sacrifice + the post-barrier dispatch semantics + the `StepExecutionContext.sibling_outputs` carrier). **OPERATOR-RATIFIED** (arc-a `A`, AskUserQuestion 2026-06-23): the operator chose synthesis + loud disclosure NOW over both the hollow capture-only B and the reproducible-but-larger B-full, after grounding showed the cached-replay form re-creates the #705 hollow trap (the §25.12-D1 binary-ledger has no partial fan-out state to recover; finding `.harness/r-fs-1-arc-a-postjoin-14.23-hollow-finding.md`). Design vetted (C1⊥C9 dyadic council #711 + probe-resolution + advisor). FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The build (§14.24 C-RT-33).** The CP driver carves the terminal `POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` step out of a concurrent fan-out's branch set, drains the barrier, then dispatches it SYNC post-barrier supplying the branch-index-ordered sibling outputs on `StepExecutionContext.sibling_outputs` (CP spec v1.54 §3). The `PostJoinSynthesisStepDispatcher` (bound to `StepKind.POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` in the stage-5 `StepKindDispatcherRegistry`, under `requires_inference`) **wraps the inner LLM dispatcher** (the same C-RT-16 `RetryBreakerFallbackDispatcher` chain `INFERENCE_STEP` uses, wrapped in the stage-5 `SyncDispatcherFacade` — so the synthesis dispatcher is itself sync, no further facade): it composes the siblings into ONE trailing context `user` message appended AFTER the synthesis step's declared `payload.messages` (the operator's synthesis instruction), then dispatches the composed step through the inner LLM dispatcher. **Read-only / effect-free** (a pure read-of-siblings + compose; no effect-fence-carrying tool dispatch). The non-determinism of the LLM compose is the §25.12 Point-2 sacrifice, disclosed at the CP driver's durable synthesis step ledger entry (`action_id` `workflow:{wf}:post-join-synthesis:{N}`) — NOT in the runtime dispatcher (the OTel span/trace-attribute is the standard deferred D6-ingestion layer, the v1.59 RESUMPTION precedent).

**Reproducible cached-replay is the registered follow-on, NOT this arc.** Capturing + replaying the synthesized aggregate across a fan-out crash-resume requires a NEW durable per-branch-completion substrate committing in COMPLETION order — which sacrifices §25.12 **D1** (branch-index-order append; completion-order is the *foreclosed anti-pattern*), a SECOND committed-invariant sacrifice that gets its OWN C1⊥C9 council + operator gate when opened. Registered as **`B-FANOUT-OUTPUT-REPLAY`** (spine ledger). In the CURRENTLY-wired harness the divergence window is empty (the 5 non-linear strategies are crash-resume-blind), so the non-opted default deterministic fold is byte-identical + fully reproducible, and a synthesized run is always a fresh first-and-only dispatch.

**Scope discipline.** v1.75 adds ONLY the NEW **§14.24** (C-RT-33); all of §9 / §14.1–§14.23 + the v1.59–v1.74 narrative are PRESERVED VERBATIM. **No new fail-class** (an unbound dispatcher reuses the existing `StepKindDispatcherNotBoundError` → `RT-FAIL-STEP-KIND-DISPATCHER-NOT-BOUND`), **no §5.2-hash change** (the synthesis non-determinism rides the CP driver's disclosing step entry, not a new IS field; the `sibling_outputs` carrier is hash-inert per CP spec v1.54 §2), **no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening** (the dispatcher satisfies the existing sync `dispatch(binding, step, *, step_context)` signature), **no new CXA edge** (the synthesis LLM dispatch reuses the already-landed C-RT-16 LLM-dispatch seam). **CP spec C-CP-25 §5.2/§25.2/§25.12 v1.53 → v1.54** is the paired primary contract. IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. The impl: `harness-runtime` (`post_join_synthesis_dispatch.py` + the stage-5 binding); `harness-cp` (StepKind 6→7 + `sibling_outputs` + the carve + post-barrier dispatch across the 3 concurrent strategies). Decorrelated review: advisor (the two-layer hollow-trap surfacing + the coherent-A scope) + out-of-family Codex on the diff (6 rounds — converged on effect-free enforcement, failure-taxonomy, durable-HITL-pause→FAILED, zero-sibling rejection, and the params-route tool-binding bypass) + the harness-adversarial-reviewer (F1 effect-free-bypass converged with Codex round 6; 3 Class-3 doc-hygiene absorbed). ## Change-note (v1.73 → v1.74)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-22).** v1.74 is a **surgical stale-carry correction** to the §14.21.7 + §14.21.5 framing of the registered follow-on `B-INTERSTEP-NONLINEAR` (concurrent-fan-out inter-step recording). No contract, field, enum, fail-class, §5.2-hash, Protocol, or CXA-edge change; no impl change. The §14.21 C-RT-34 `InterStepOutputChannel` contract body (§14.21.1–.4) is PRESERVED VERBATIM; only three prose surfaces are corrected — §14.21.5 invariant-4, the §14.21.6 forward-arc cross-reference, and the §14.21.7 follow-on bullet (all re-disposing `B-INTERSTEP-NONLINEAR` consistently). Mode-agnostic record-correction (`[[stale-carry-text-disposition]]`); arc-ledger + spine-ledger re-disposition co-lands. FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The false claim being corrected.** v1.59 §14.21.7 stated, of the concurrent non-linear strategies, that *"the genuine inter-step reads in these topologies are sequential (orchestrator synthesis post-join), so the channel composes once recording lands."* **This is false at HEAD** (body-read of `harness_cp.workflow_driver._aggregate_orchestrator_workers` + `_aggregate_parallelization`, advisor-confirmed): the concurrent strategies (ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS, PARALLELIZATION, HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION) compose their result via a **deterministic fold** (C-CP-25 §25.11/§25.12 — "first to finish wins is forbidden") that receives `branch_outputs` **directly**, not via the channel. The aggregate fold docstring states it verbatim: *"there is NO second 'compose' dispatch (that would need the deferred inter-step DATA flow, B-INTERSTEP)."* There is no post-join LLM read, and topology is per-workflow (the fold output IS the terminal `RunResult` — no subsequent linear step in a fan-out workflow). So recording concurrent siblings (or the aggregate) into the channel has **no non-vacuous consumer** → it would fail the §14.21.5 invariant-6 non-vacuity bar (a HOLLOW carrier, `[[r-cxa-seam-wiring-is-producer-discovery]]`).

**The genuine capability is gated, not buildable-now.** A real inter-step read for these topologies requires a **post-join LLM synthesis step** — but an LLM compose makes ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS output **non-deterministic**, contradicting the C-CP-25 §25.12 determinism guarantee. That sacrifices a committed decision → a Class-1 topology-semantics fork / **operator gate** (`[[feedback-gate-only-on-meaningful-architecture-change]]`), registered as the new gated arc **`B-POSTJOIN-LLM-SYNTHESIS`** (spine ledger). `B-INTERSTEP-NONLINEAR` is therefore re-disposed **RESOLVED-AS-HOLLOW** (recording has no non-vacuous consumer under the cleared deterministic-fold semantics; the DECENTRALIZED_HANDOFF case it once enumerated already closed at `B-INTERSTEP-HANDOFF`, #677). The §14.21.7 bullet + §14.21.5 invariant-4 are corrected to state this. No design extension is performed here (X-AL-3): the gated capability is registered, not built.

## Change-note (v1.72 → v1.73)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-22).** v1.73 marks the registered §14.22.7 follow-on **`B-EFFECT-FENCE-PAUSE-RESOLUTION` BUILT** — the resume-side RESOLUTION of the §26.2 `WorkflowPauseReason.EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS` pause that v1.72 (§14.22.8) opened. v1.72 ships the ambiguous-pause CAPTURE (a labeled, non-terminal, hash-valid pause); until this delta a naive `api.resume` re-pauses identically (INERT). v1.73 wires the resume to RESOLVE it via an operator-supplied resolution (new **§14.22.9**). R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc (spine ledger). **NO operator gate — BUILD-not-gate** (the #702 registration's "operator-gated + safety-sensitive" label flipped at design-vet; advisor-concurred). Design vetted at `.harness/class_1_fork_effect_fence_pause_resolution.md`. FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The reframe that dissolves the gate (the #529 `cascade-cancel` out-of-domain precedent).** The fence raises `EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS` *specifically to ASK the operator one question — "did the effect fire?"* — because the harness genuinely cannot tell (the crash fell in the fire→capture window). The three resolutions are the operator ANSWERING with ground-truth the harness lacks: `SKIP_AS_FIRED` = "it fired" (the prior attempt fired then crashed pre-capture); `RE_FIRE` = "it did NOT fire" (the prior attempt claimed then crashed pre-fire); `ABORT` = "can't determine." `RE_FIRE` therefore does NOT breach at-most-once — when the operator has correctly determined the effect did not fire, re-firing is the FIRST-and-only execution, still at-most-once *from the true state of the world*. The operator COMPLETES the at-most-once decision the harness couldn't compute, not overrides it. A mis-assertion is operator-error responsibility (the C-AS-03 `idempotent` / `blast_radius_tier` mis-declaration posture). The palette composes only committed primitives (a fence claim-clear + re-dispatch + the existing empty-output accumulate + the existing FAILED mapping) → no new primitive → no operator gate.

**§14.22.9 — the resume-side resolution (the build).** (1) `RuntimeEffectFence.clear_claim(idempotency_key)` — the inverse of `try_reserve`: atomically unlink the held `<digest>.claim` + any `<digest>.output` (missing-ok), so a subsequent `try_reserve` WINS and the effect re-fires fresh (the RE_FIRE substrate). (2) The operator's resolution is delivered one-shot via the NEW `ResumeContext.effect_fence_resolution` (CP spec §26.8, the `EffectFenceResolution` enum) on `api.resume`; the CP driver PEEKS the `ResumeContextHolder` (non-consuming — the runtime HITL composer retains its one-shot `consume_and_clear`) gated on the snapshot carrying `PauseSnapshot.effect_fence_resume` (CP §26.2), KEY-BINDS the resolution to that carrier's `idempotency_key`, and threads an `EffectFenceResolutionDirective` onto the RESUMED linear step's `StepExecutionContext.effect_fence_resolution` (hash-inert, the `run_engine_class` channel precedent) — only the resumed step (`step_index == resume_at`). (3) The tool dispatcher applies it at the §14.22 fence gate ONLY when the recomputed dispatch key equals the directive's `idempotency_key` (key-bind, correctness-by-construction — a stale resolution can never mis-apply to a different fenced effect): **RE_FIRE** → `clear_claim` before `try_reserve` → fires fresh through the normal step-7 path (+ post-fire `capture_output` + success emission) — **the clear is gated on a durable one-way `.refire` consume-once latch (`try_consume_refire`)**, so a `RetryBreakerToolDispatcher` retry of the re-fire (or a crash-resume) reusing the same `step_context` LOSES the latch → does NOT re-clear → `try_reserve` loses to the re-fire's own held claim → the suppress/ambiguous split applies (a retryable error during the re-fire can never double-fire the effect — Codex [P1]); **SKIP_AS_FIRED** → return an EMPTY-output success wrapper (the lost output is genuinely unrecoverable) + the balancing `sandbox.exit` (no `mcp.tool.call` span — no effect fired this dispatch), NEVER re-firing; **ABORT** → raise the NEW `EffectFenceAbortedError`, which the driver maps to FAILED via its generic exception path (terminal; not a `_TRANSIENT_TOOL_DISPATCH_ERRORS` member, so the retry-breaker re-raises it verbatim). A resume with NO resolution (or a key-mismatch) preserves the v1.72 INERT re-pause.

**Scope discipline.** v1.73 marks the §14.22.7 PAUSE-RESOLUTION follow-on BUILT + adds the NEW **§14.22.9** (resume-side resolution: `clear_claim` + the dispatcher three-branch split + the `EffectFenceAbortedError` symbol); the v1.60–v1.72 fence narrative (§14.22.1–.8) is PRESERVED VERBATIM as the historical record. **CP spec C-CP-26 §26.8 + §26.2 v1.51 → v1.52** co-amends (the `EffectFenceResolution` enum + `EffectFenceResumeState` carrier + `EffectFenceResolutionDirective` + the additive `ResumeContext.effect_fence_resolution` + `PauseSnapshot.effect_fence_resume` fields + the `StepExecutionContext.effect_fence_resolution` hash-inert field). **No new fail-class taxonomy code** (`EffectFenceAbortedError` maps to the existing generic FAILED), **no §5.2-hash change** (the `effect_fence_resume` carrier rides the `PauseSnapshot` `_compute_snapshot_hash`, NOT the IS state-ledger six-field hash; the directive is hash-inert), **no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening** (the resolution rides the hash-inert `StepExecutionContext` field), **no new CXA edge** (RE_FIRE's fresh success reuses the existing CP→IS success seam; the pause/resume seam is unchanged). IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. The impl: `harness-runtime` (`effect_fence.py` `clear_claim` + `EffectFenceAbortedError`; `resume_context_holder.py` `peek`; `runtime_tool_dispatcher.py` three-branch split); `harness-cp` (the type carriers + `workflow_driver.py` carrier population + directive threading + the durable-protocol override forward). Decorrelated review: advisor (the BUILD-not-gate reframe + the key-bound/consume-once + the clear_claim + ABORT-claim witnesses) + out-of-family Codex on the diff. Witnesses: dispatcher RE_FIRE-fires-fresh / SKIP-empty-no-refire / ABORT-raises / key-mismatch-ignored + clear_claim file-level unit; driver carrier-population + hash-integrity + ABORT→FAILED + the full-chain directive-threading producer (peek-not-consume, key-bound, resumed-step-only).

## Change-note (v1.71 → v1.72)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-22).** v1.72 marks the registered §14.22.7 follow-on **`B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE` BUILT** — the §14.22 C-RT-31 effect fence's lost-reserve re-dispatch no longer uniformly fail-closes; it now SPLITS two ways on a newly-captured output (new **§14.22.8**). R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc (spine ledger). **OPERATOR-GATED + RATIFIED** (AskUserQuestion 2026-06-22 — the operator AUTHORIZED this build over the other gated arcs + the quality track): relaxing the fence's load-bearing fail-closed into a two-case split + a NEW pause-reason value are committed-behavior gates the choice ratified. Design vetted at `.harness/class_1_fork_effect_fence_hitl_route.md` (advisor-vetted; the crux + the two-case invariant + 3 verifications resolved). FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The build (post-fire output capture + two-case split — the #701 decline-mirror transferred).** (1) The fence gains **post-fire / pre-commit durable output capture** at the sink (`capture_output(key, payload)` / `read_output(key) -> payload | None`, the same crash-atomic `O_EXCL`/`os.link` primitive + the same per-(run, step, tool) digest keying as `try_reserve`). The dispatcher captures the VALIDATED response as the LAST step before the success return (post-schema-validation, post-cost-attribution → "captured ⟹ valid success ∧ cost attributed once"). (2) A lost-reserve re-dispatch SPLITS on `read_output`: **present** ⟹ the effect demonstrably completed AND its result is in hand ⟹ **suppress-and-continue** (the sink returns the captured output, NEVER re-firing); **absent or corrupt** ⟹ the crash fell in the fire→capture window ⟹ the sink raises the NEW `EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError`. (3) The driver name-matches the ambiguous error at the linear/TOOL_STEP step-dispatch boundary (harness-cp cannot import harness-runtime — the `HITLPauseRequestedSignal` precedent) and routes it to a **§26.2 `WorkflowPauseReason.EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS` PAUSE** when a `PauseResumeProtocol` is bound, else FAILED (the conservative opt-out default). **NEVER an auto-re-fire** on either branch — auto-proceed happens ONLY on proof-of-completion (the #701 decline-mirror invariant transferred: the relaxation is safe ONLY under captured-output-present, fail-to-operator outside it).

**The crux — 'the prior output' was never persisted (advisor-sharpened).** The v1.60 §14.22.7 entry deferred suppress-and-continue to `B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY`, but the 2026-06-22 probe found replay CANNOT supply it: the F2 `EntryPayload` carries only a `response_hash` digest, and the §14.23 replay rehydrate is `resume_at`-driven + deliberately ignores the suppressed step's OWN uncommitted output. So this arc MUST add its own output substrate — it does, at the fence (atomic, so `present ⟹ complete-and-valid`; a present-but-corrupt output fail-closes to PAUSE, never a valid suppress source).

**The pause-reason home — §26.2 (C-CP-26), NOT §22.1 (C-CP-22) (advisor + primary-source correction).** The fork doc's verification 1 framed the value as the engine-layer §22.1 `PauseReason`; primary-source grounding corrected it: the DRIVER-routed pause path (`ctx.pause_resume_protocol.capture_pause_snapshot(...)` → `RunResult.pause_snapshot`) is typed `WorkflowPauseReason` (C-CP-26 §26.2). The §22.1 `PauseReason` is the engine-native replay-pause substrate the driver never calls here. The HITL precedent is exact (a driver-detected HITL pause uses `WorkflowPauseReason.HITL_PENDING`, not the engine `HITL_INVOCATION_PENDING`). The new value homes in `WorkflowPauseReason` only.

**Resolution is a registered follow-on, not over-claimed (Codex pre-merge catch).** v1.72 builds the ambiguous-pause CAPTURE (a labeled, non-terminal, inspectable, hash-valid pause — strictly better than the v1.60 terminal FAILED). The resume-side RESOLUTION (operator `skip-as-fired` / `re-fire` [clear the claim] / `abort`) is the safety-sensitive registered follow-on `B-EFFECT-FENCE-PAUSE-RESOLUTION` (§14.22.7); until it lands a naive resume re-pauses identically (INERT — resume is caller-initiated, pinned by a by-execution test). The headline deliverable (suppress-and-continue, the common case) is fully built + witnessed.

**Scope discipline.** v1.72 marks the §14.22.7 HITL-ROUTE follow-on BUILT + registers `B-EFFECT-FENCE-PAUSE-RESOLUTION` + adds the NEW **§14.22.8** (two-case split + output-capture substrate) + a section-head forward-pointer at §14.22's contract-surface intro; the v1.60 interim narrative (§14.22.1–.7) is preserved as the historical record, with the lost-claim behavior refined at §14.22.8. The `EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError` symbol is RETIRED (its sole raise site is replaced by the two-case split) → renamed `EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError`. **CP spec C-CP-26 §26.2 v1.50 → v1.51** co-amends (the new `WorkflowPauseReason.EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS` value). **No new fail-class taxonomy code, no §5.2-hash change, no `StepDispatcher` Protocol widening, no new CXA edge** (the driver's CP→IS `PAUSE_CAPTURED` emission reuses the existing seam with `event_kind_index=3`, disambiguating the effect-fence path from the drain-flag [=1] + HITL-signal [=2] paths). IS / OD / AS / ADR specs UNCHANGED. CXA v2.20 UNCHANGED. The impl: `harness-runtime` (`effect_fence.py` capture/read + the rename; `runtime_tool_dispatcher.py` two-case split + capture); `harness-cp` (`WorkflowPauseReason.EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS`; `workflow_driver.py` name-match PAUSE branch). Decorrelated review: advisor (the enum-layer correction + the crux + the byte-identical-string caveat) + out-of-family Codex on the diff. Witnesses: dispatcher-level suppress-and-continue (no re-fire) + ambiguous-absent / ambiguous-corrupt raise + durable suppress across a process restart; driver-level ambiguous → PAUSED (bound) / FAILED (unbound); retry-breaker verbatim re-raise; 6-class `WorkflowPauseReason` cardinality.

## Change-note (v1.69 → v1.70)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-21).** v1.70 marks the registered §14.22.7 follow-on **`B-EFFECT-FENCE-PER-TOOL` BUILT** — the §14.22 C-RT-31 `RuntimeEffectFence` now EXEMPTS a declared-idempotent tool from the per-(run, step, tool) reserve, so only declared-**non-idempotent** tools are fenced (the §14.22 line-142 stated intent — "at-most-once EXECUTION of a non-idempotent tool-step effect" — that the v1.60 interim conservatively over-delivered by fencing every tool under an active fence). R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc (spine ledger; design authority = the §14.22.7 follow-on text itself, which named "per-tool idempotency classification to fence only declared-non-idempotent tools"). **NO operator gate** — fence-all-when-active is the conservative IMPL of the at-most-once-for-non-idempotent intent (NOT a committed invariant; §14.22.7 NAMES this follow-on, the `B-EFFECT-FENCE-DURABLE-AUTO` v1.67 precedent); the AS-side field is additive with a fence-by-default safe default (no committed invariant sacrificed). FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The build (per-tool exemption at the existing fence gate).** The `RuntimeToolDispatcher` already resolves the per-tool `ToolContract` (from `tool_registry`, for the tier-floor check) at the dispatch site, so the fence gate gains one conjunct: the per-dispatch reserve fires on **`(effect_fencing_explicit OR run_engine_class ∈ durable-set) AND NOT contract.idempotent`**. A tool whose contract declares `idempotent=True` skips the reserve entirely — it fires + is **safely retryable** (the v1.60 interim fail-closed an idempotent tool's transient `RetryBreakerToolDispatcher` retry, which is over-conservative: re-running an idempotent tool is safe by definition). Default `idempotent=False` → fenced (byte-identical to v1.69). The dispatch signature is UNCHANGED (the gate reads the already-in-scope `contract`).

**Tool-intrinsic / all-invocations — the safety-load-bearing semantic (advisor decorrelated catch).** Idempotency for a write/mutate tool is `(tool, args)`-dependent, which is precisely WHY the fence keys per-invocation `(run, step, tool, idempotency_key)`. A per-tool `idempotent` flag is therefore sound ONLY for a STRICT tool-intrinsic property: **every invocation re-executes with no additional external effect, for ALL arguments** (AS spec C-AS-03 §3.1 v1.12 — a pure read trivially qualifies; a PUT-style set-to-value qualifies; an append / send / counter-increment does NOT). The default `false` is the conservative fence-by-default (undeclared tools stay fenced); a mis-declaration is the contract author's responsibility (exactly as `blast_radius_tier` is). The exemption is monotone-safe: it never weakens the at-most-once guarantee for a genuinely-non-idempotent effect.

**Cross-axis cascade (AS spec C-AS-03 §3.1 v1.11 → v1.12).** `ToolContract` gains the optional `idempotent: bool = False` field (AS-side leg), threaded by the AS↔runtime registration seam: `RawContractInput.idempotent` + the `validate_tool_contract_at_registration` converter (authored contracts) + the NEW per-server `MCPClientConfig.default_idempotent` stamped by the stage-3a `MCPToolContractConverter` (discovered tools — MCP advertisements carry no idempotency semantics, so the per-server default is the policy source, the `default_forces_*` precedent). `idempotent` does NOT enter the C-AS-02 §2.3 `sandbox_tier_floor` composition (a fence-only concern, distinct from the v1.11 forcing discriminators).

**Scope discipline.** v1.70 marks the §14.22.7 follow-on status (change-note-level — §14.22 has no expanded body section) + documents the one-conjunct fence-gate refinement + the per-server `default_idempotent` field. The §14.22 C-RT-31 contract carrier (the fence schema, `try_reserve` at-most-once semantic, the §22.1 fail-closed `EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError` raise) is **PRESERVED VERBATIM**. **No new contract, no new fail-class, no §5.2-hash change** (the gate refinement + `MCPClientConfig.default_idempotent` are runtime-/config-internal; `ToolContract.idempotent` is an additive AS field with a safe default). **CP spec UNCHANGED.** AS spec **C-AS-03 §3.1 v1.11 → v1.12** co-amends (the field declaration). IS / OD / ADR specs UNCHANGED. The impl adds `contract.idempotent` to the dispatcher fence gate + `ToolContract.idempotent` / `RawContractInput.idempotent` + the converter passthrough (harness-as) + `MCPClientConfig.default_idempotent` + the host-factory stamp (harness-runtime). Decorrelated review: advisor (BUILD-vs-gate discriminator — fence-all is conservative-impl not a committed invariant; the tool-intrinsic-vs-invocation-dependent strict-semantic catch) + out-of-family Codex on the diff. Witnesses: an idempotent tool under a durable engine is NOT fenced (re-dispatch fires twice, no fence error) + a non-idempotent (default) tool IS fenced (negative control) + the converter/per-server-default threads `idempotent` through to the dispatched contract.

**§14.22.7 follow-on status update.** `B-EFFECT-FENCE-PER-TOOL` is now **BUILT** (this delta). `B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE` (§22.1 operator-resolvable pause + suppress-and-continue via `B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY`) remains the one registered §14.22.7 follow-on.

## Change-note (v1.68 → v1.69)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-21).** v1.69 **closes the §14.6.1 scope-boundary** and marks the registered follow-on **`B-L2-ROUTING-SPAN-LAYER-ATTRIBUTION` BUILT** — the inner C-RT-15 `gen_ai` span's `routing.layer` now reports the **real EMBEDDING/L3 layer** the C-RT-16 wrapper resolved for the routed PRIMARY, instead of the inner's faithful DECLARATIVE echo (`RoutingLayer.DECLARATIVE == "manifest"`). R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc (spine ledger; design authority = the §14.6.1 scope-boundary itself, which named this gap + registered this exact follow-on). **NO operator gate** — observability-additive; sacrifices no committed invariant; selection/dispatch behavior is byte-unchanged (only the span attribution is corrected). FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The gap this closes (§14.6.1 scope-boundary).** Under `routing_activation`, B-L2-FALLBACK-COMPOSITION resolves the layered-routing decision ONCE at the wrapper (route-once-then-fallback) and reverts the inner dispatcher to FAITHFUL — so the inner re-derives a DECLARATIVE-echo `RoutingDecisionTrace` for the (already-routed) rebound candidate and stamps `routing.layer = "manifest"` on the `gen_ai` span, NOT the EMBEDDING/L3 layer that actually PICKED the model. The routed model itself was always faithfully dispatched; only the span's `routing.layer`/`routing.binding_rationale` attribution was wrong (an observability-fidelity gap, production-dormant until a second provider makes routing-among-candidates meaningful).

**The build (ContextVar-threaded resolved trace — the §14.6.1-named "per-dispatch context" mechanism).** `resolve_routed_binding` now returns a `RoutedPrimaryResolution` (the routed `ModelBinding` it already returned + the resolving `RoutingDecisionTrace` + binding rationale it previously DISCARDED). The wrapper extracts `.model_binding` for chain composition unchanged, and — for the routed PRIMARY candidate ONLY — publishes `(routing_trace, binding_rationale)` on a module `ContextVar` (`ROUTED_PRIMARY_SPAN_TRACE`) around the inner dispatch; `_invoke_provider` reads it for `routing.layer`/`routing.binding_rationale`. A **ContextVar** (not an instance attribute) because the C-RT-15 dispatcher is shared across concurrent fan-out branches — the per-task isolation mirrors the B-INTERSTEP-PERRUN-ISOLATION (v1.64) precedent. The `StepDispatcher` Protocol is **NOT widened** (the §14.6.1 alternative); `routing.provider`/`routing.model` still reflect the actually-dispatched candidate on every path.

**Scope boundary held — fallback candidates stay faithful.** The ContextVar is published ONLY for the routed primary; a CHAIN-selected fallback candidate (the routed primary failed → `_advance_or_exhaust`) is NOT routing-selected, so its span keeps the faithful DECLARATIVE echo (the ContextVar is cleared to `None` for it). This is witnessed by execution (a routed primary that fails → the haiku span reports `"embedding"`, the opus fallback span reports `"manifest"`).

## Change-note (v1.67 → v1.68)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-21).** v1.68 marks the registered follow-on **`B-HITL-WRAP-FAIL-CLASS-SURFACING` BUILT** — the wrap-time HITL gate's terminal exceptions now surface their canonical **`RT-FAIL-HITL-*` code** in the driver `fail_class` (instead of the bare Python class name), via a self-describing `rt_fail_class` marker the CP driver reads. **The gap this closes.** `harness-cp` cannot import the `harness-runtime` HITL exception TYPES (the axis dependency graph), so the CP driver surfaced a caught wrap-time HITL exception via the generic `step-failure: {type(exc).__name__}: …` — e.g. `HITLGateRejectedError` instead of the canonical `RT-FAIL-HITL-GATE-REJECTED` the §14.8 taxonomy + the exception docstrings declare. (The pre-existing per-name canonicalization — e.g. the `ManagedAgentsSessionError` name-match — covered some classes by hardcoded string, but the 4 wrap-time HITL terminal exceptions fell through to the generic path.)

The CP driver composes `fail_class` via a `_step_fail_class(prefix, exc)` helper that reads `getattr(exc, "rt_fail_class", None) or type(exc).__name__` — import-free, applied at ALL per-topology step-dispatch failure sites (linear / EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER / ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS / DECENTRALIZED_HANDOFF). A non-marker exception falls back to the class name (byte-identical to pre-arc); the mechanism generalizes to ANY runtime exception that opts in by carrying the marker. `HITLCellExcludedError` is intentionally NOT marked (it has no §14.8 taxonomy code — documented as "not in §14.8" — so it correctly stays generic).

**Scope discipline.** v1.68 refreshes the §14.8 `RT-FAIL-HITL-GATE-EDIT-DECODE` row's surfacing clause (the v1.62 "generic `{type}`" description → the now-precise marker surfacing) + marks the follow-on LANDED (change-note-level). The §14.8 fail-class taxonomy codes, the wrap-time composer body, and all other sections are **PRESERVED VERBATIM**. **No new contract, no new fail-class, no new §14.8 code** (the codes already exist), **no §5.2-hash change** (the `rt_fail_class` marker + the `_step_fail_class` helper are runtime-/driver-internal). ## Change-note (v1.66 → v1.67)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-21).** v1.67 marks the registered follow-on **§14.22.7 `B-EFFECT-FENCE-DURABLE-AUTO` BUILT** — the §14.22 C-RT-31 `RuntimeEffectFence` now AUTO-activates for durable-execution engine classes, removing the operator `RuntimeConfig.effect_fencing=True` opt-in for the common durable case. R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc (spine ledger; design authority = the §14.22.7 follow-on text itself, which anticipates this + names the mechanism: "auto-construct it whenever `manifest_entry.engine_class` is durable … a per-run reserve gate keyed on the engine class"). **NO operator gate** — additive; sacrifices no committed invariant; the per-run gate keeps non-durable runs fence-free. FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The build (per-run reserve gate — the option §14.22.7 names).** The stage-5 tool-dispatcher factory now constructs the `RuntimeEffectFence` UNCONDITIONALLY (its claim dir is created LAZILY on first reserve, so a run that never reserves leaves no directory — the pre-v1.60 byte-identical footprint). The dispatcher carries a NEW `effect_fencing_explicit: bool` (the operator's `effect_fencing` opt-in) and gates the per-dispatch reserve on **`effect_fencing_explicit OR step_context.run_engine_class ∈ durable-set`**. The per-run engine class arrives on a NEW hash-inert `StepExecutionContext.run_engine_class` field (the CP driver sets it from `manifest_entry.engine_class` at every step-context composition site — the `hitl_placements` producer precedent) — **NOT cached on the daemon-reused dispatcher singleton** (it travels with the per-dispatch `step_context`). The spec's other named option, "thread the engine class to the factory," is wrong for a multi-run daemon and was avoided. **`run_engine_class` is DELIBERATELY the run/manifest engine class, NOT `StepEffectiveBinding.engine_class`** (out-of-family Codex [P2]): the binding resolves a per-step `StepOverride.engine_class`, so a per-step override to a non-durable class on a DURABLE workflow would wrongly skip the fence for a step the RUN still resumes + re-dispatches (a double-fire window). What governs resume is the run engine class, so the gate keys on that.

The `B-EFFECT-FENCE-PER-TOOL` / `B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE` follow-ons remain registered. | §14.22.7 |

The impl reads the durable-auto-fence set as `{SAVE_POINT_CHECKPOINT, EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY, WAL_SEGMENT, RECONCILER_LOOP}`, EXCLUDING `PURE_PATTERN_NO_ENGINE` (the "no-engine" pipeline-automation baseline = the spec's "non-durable run" carve-out). A strict improvement over the pre-v1.60 all-opt-in default (no regression: the 4 real durable engines move opt-in → auto-on; pure-pattern is unchanged + can still opt in). ## Change-note (v1.64 → v1.65)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-20).** v1.65 **adds §14.6.1** — the layered-routing (`routing_activation`, C-CP-02 §2.2) composition with the C-RT-16 retry/breaker/fallback chain — and marks the registered follow-on **`B-L2-FALLBACK-COMPOSITION` BUILT**. R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc (`.harness/class_2_fork_b_l2_fallback_composition.md`; spine ledger; design authority = the §14.5.3 "the C-RT-16 wrapper owns model-candidate selection / no two-authority-at-dispatch" invariant + the §14.6 "the wrapper invokes the inner dispatcher exactly once per attempt with a rebound binding" contract, which JOINTLY prescribe the fix). **NO operator gate** — additive correctness that SACRIFICES no committed invariant; it *restores* the §14.6 inner-is-faithful contract that `routing_activation` (B-L2-EMBEDDING-ACTIVATION) had broken, and the opt-out default (`routing_activation=False`) is byte-identical. **NO council** — the only nameable cross-domain tension (routing-layer-home vs reliability-composition: should the routing decision live at the inner routing surface or the fallback wrapper?) is FORECLOSED by the cleared §14.5.3 / §14.6 invariants (the wrapper owns selection; the inner faithfully dispatches the rebound candidate) → probe-resolved, advisor + out-of-family Codex (the same §10.9 discriminator). FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The gap this closes (the silent fallback-defeat).** B-L2-EMBEDDING-ACTIVATION (v1.64-era; C-CP-02 §2.2) made the **inner** C-RT-15 dispatcher able to OVERRIDE `binding.model_binding` — when `routing_activation` is on and the manifest does not bind the request's tuple, the inner's DECLARATIVE layer DECLINES and `route()` falls through to the EMBEDDING classifier (then L3), picking a DIFFERENT model. But the C-RT-16 wrapper drives fallback by re-binding `binding.model_binding` to each successive chain candidate and re-invoking the inner per attempt (§14.6 step 4). So under `routing_activation` the inner **re-routed on every fallback re-invocation** and re-picked the SAME embedding/router candidate, IGNORING the wrapper's rebound fallback candidate → the chain never advanced (a SILENT fallback-defeat). This is exactly the **two-authority-at-dispatch** anti-pattern §14.5.3 forecloses ("indexing the per-role model at the inner too would create TWO authorities … and silently defeat fallback"). The interim B-L2-EMBEDDING-ACTIVATION guard detect-then-refused (`LLMDispatchBindError`) a `routing_activation` + non-empty `fallback_chains` deployment until this arc.

**The build (route-once-then-fallback-the-chain — the U-RT-114 §14.5.3 pattern applied to layered routing).** The layered-routing decision is now made **ONCE at the C-RT-16 wrapper** (NOT re-run per attempt) and SEEDS the wrapper's PRIMARY fallback candidate; the inner reverts to FAITHFUL (it dispatches the wrapper's rebound candidate exactly once per attempt per §14.6). Mechanism: (1) the route()+L3 SELECTION is factored to `harness_cp.routing_core_surface.resolve_routing_trace` (the SELECTION half of `infer`, no dispatch); (2) a NEW `RuntimeLLMDispatcher.resolve_routed_binding` runs that selection (DECLARATIVE-decline → EMBEDDING → L3) and returns the routed `ModelBinding`, or `None` when `routing_activation` is off OR a DETERMINISTIC binding governs (per-step `override_applied` / per-role `per_role_bindings` / model-bearing per-workload override — DECLARATIVE would echo, so the existing chain primary IS the selection); (3) the stage-5 factory hands the wrapper a DIRECT handle to that method (NOT via the HITL `inner`, which is two layers above the routing-capable dispatcher), and the wrapper promotes the routed model to its PRIMARY candidate via the SAME `_augment_primary` chain-augmentation U-RT-114 uses (routed primary + original chain as deduped tail). The inner's `_declarative_echo` reverts to a pure echo; the interim factory guard is RETIRED.

| What v1.65 changes | Substance | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **NEW §14.6.1** | The layered-routing-vs-fallback **composition contract**: under `routing_activation`, the wrapper resolves the routed candidate ONCE (via the inner's `resolve_routed_binding` SELECTION surface) and seeds it as the chain PRIMARY, composing with C-RT-16 fallback; the inner faithfully dispatches each rebound candidate. Precedence: a deterministic binding (per-step override / per-role / model-bearing per-workload) takes the primary (routing declines); routing fills ONLY the no-deterministic-binding gap (mutual-exclusivity per the §2.2 hit-invariant). | §14.5.3 + §14.6 (jointly) |
| **§14.6 step 2/step 4 (PRESERVED, clarified by §14.6.1)** | The cleared "first candidate is `binding.model_binding`; the inner is invoked exactly once per attempt with a rebound binding" contract is RESTORED for `routing_activation` (B-L2-EMBEDDING-ACTIVATION had broken it at the inner). §14.6 step bodies are PRESERVED VERBATIM; §14.6.1 documents where the routing decision composes. | §14.6 |
| **§14.5.3 (PRESERVED)** | The "wrapper owns model-candidate selection / no two-authority-at-dispatch" invariant is the governing authority; this arc honors it (layered routing joins the per-role binding as a wrapper-side primary source). No §14.5.3 change. | §14.5.3 |

**Scope discipline.** v1.65 adds ONLY §14.6.1 (additive). §14.5 / §14.5.3 / §14.6 step bodies / §14.7+ / §9 / §14.20–§14.23 + all `RuntimeConfig` / `HarnessContext` / `RunResult` fields are **PRESERVED VERBATIM** (no new field; `routing_activation` is unchanged). **No §5.2-hash change** (routing selection is ephemeral, not persisted/hashed). **CP spec UNCHANGED** — `resolve_routing_trace` is an additive factoring of the existing `infer` within `harness_cp` (CP-pure; the runtime imports it, the normal runtime→CP direction; no new CP contract, no `harness_cp`→`harness_runtime` import). IS / OD / ADR specs UNCHANGED. **Observability scope-boundary (registered follow-on `B-L2-ROUTING-SPAN-LAYER-ATTRIBUTION`):** under wrapper-routing the inner's `gen_ai` span carries the DECLARATIVE-echo `routing.layer`, not the real EMBEDDING/L3 layer the wrapper used — a minor fidelity gap, production-dormant until a second provider; the routed model itself is faithfully dispatched. Additive + opt-out-byte-identical; decorrelated review (advisor pre-build — the inner-is-HITL-composer catch + the two-primary-sources precedence + the dual non-vacuity properties; out-of-family Codex on the diff).

## Change-note (v1.63 → v1.64)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-20).** v1.64 **closes §14.21.5 invariant 7** (the run-scoped-no-cross-run-leak invariant of the §14.21 C-RT-34 `InterStepOutputChannel`) — previously bounded honestly to (a) sequential reuse + (b) concurrent-within-timeout, with (c) the `drain_timeout_seconds` TIMEOUT-ZOMBIE named as a registered residual — and marks the §14.21.7 follow-on **`B-INTERSTEP-PERRUN-ISOLATION` BUILT**. R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc (`.harness/class_1_fork_b_interstep_perrun_isolation.md`; spine ledger; design authority = the B-INTERSTEP fork §3/§5, which prescribed the mechanism). **NO operator gate** — additive correctness that SACRIFICES no committed invariant (it *removes* B-INTERSTEP's serialization + *closes* a registered residual); the opt-out default (channel unbound) is byte-identical, and no nameable cross-domain tension (internal concurrency correctness) → advisor + out-of-family Codex, not council (the same §10.9 discriminator the B-INTERSTEP fork applied). FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

**The fork B-INTERSTEP closed (the systemic residual).** B-INTERSTEP allocated its run-scoped channel at **bootstrap** scope on the frozen `HarnessContext`; in daemon-client mode (U-RT-108) one bootstrapped ctx serves many `run_workflow` invocations, so concurrent runs SHARED the one channel. B-INTERSTEP fenced (a)+(b) with a per-run `reset()` + a per-loop single-flight **lock**, but the lock *serializes* rather than *isolates* and CANNOT fence (c): a run exceeding `drain_timeout_seconds` leaves a non-cancellable `asyncio.to_thread` worker that keeps recording after the lock releases. The fork §3/§5 named this **SYSTEMIC across every bootstrap-ctx holder** (the IDENTICAL exposure `cost_record_accumulator` carries, §82 Class-3) and registered the proper fix.

**The build (ContextVar-bound per-run holders — the fork-prescribed mechanism).** Each run-scoped mutable holder is scoped **per run** via a `ContextVar` resolved at dispatch; the frozen ctx binds a stable PROXY that delegates to the current run's holder. The `run_workflow` handler sets a fresh holder per run; the set propagates into the `to_thread` driver worker via `contextvars.copy_context()` (verified empirically), so (a)+(b) need NO lock and (c) is closed — a timed-out zombie writes only the holder captured in ITS context copy, never a following run's. Closes BOTH named holders with ONE mechanism: (1) `InterStepOutputChannel` (`RunScopedInterStepOutputChannel` proxy + `INTER_STEP_CHANNEL_VAR`, opt-in — opt-out stays `None`, byte-identical); (2) the always-on `CostRecordAccumulator` (`RunScopedCostRecordAccumulator` proxy + `COST_ACCUM_VAR`; the per-dispatch cost wrappers now thread the PROXY instead of a `.records` list captured once at bootstrap — the capture that defeated isolation; `api.run`/`resume` set a fresh accumulator around `[invoke + cost-read]` so the post-run rollup read resolves the same accumulator the wrappers appended to). The B-INTERSTEP single-flight lock (`_inter_step_run_lock` / `_INTER_STEP_RUN_LOCKS`) is **removed**.

Supersedes the v1.59 "(a)+(b) closed, (c) registered" bound. | Fork §3/§5 |
| **§14.21.7 (follow-on BUILT)** | `B-INTERSTEP-PERRUN-ISOLATION` is **BUILT**: ContextVar-bound per-run isolation of the inter-step channel + the identical `cost_record_accumulator` exposure (§82 Class-3), one mechanism. Other bootstrap-ctx holders assessed (see disposition note) — `resume_context_holder` is set-per-run overwrite, `engine_output_store` is `run_idempotency_key`-keyed, ledger writers are ADR-F2 single-writer + run_id-tagged — none accumulate run-scoped contents on a shared holder, so none need isolation; the generic proxy primitive composes for any future holder that does. | Fork §3/§5 |

The cost proxy is always-bound (cost is always-on) but single-run output is unchanged — daemon multi-run goes buggy→correct, no regression. | Fork §4 |

## Change-note (v1.62 → v1.63)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-19).** v1.63 adds a **NEW contract §14.23 C-RT-32 `EngineOutputStore`** — a hand-rolled (I-6) durable **output-carrying event-history store** that materializes the C-CP-08 §8.1 `engine_replay` "**activity outputs cached and replayed**" clause for `EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY`. R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc **B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY** (`.harness/class_2_fork_b_engine_output_replay_output_carrying_substrate.md`; spine ledger; `.harness/r-fs-1-e-impl-1-finding.md` §4 — `design-fork-first per X-AL-3, since the output-carrier substrate is a new surface`). This closes the degenerate half of §8.1: U-CP-93 delivers "no re-execution of activities" (skip-prefix), but "outputs cached and replayed" was empirically unbuildable — the F2 `EntryPayload` (C-IS-07 §7.1) carries only a `response_hash` **digest**, never the activity output (E-impl-1 Finding 1), and on a skip-prefix resume the (now-built, B-INTERSTEP) inter-step channel is fresh-empty, so a downstream consumer reads `None` where a fresh run reads the upstream output (fresh-run ≠ resumed-run).

**The build.** (1) A dedicated durable store (NOT the IS `EntryPayload` — extending it would ripple the C-IS-05 §5.2 entry hash + JSONL shape + IS contract for a CP/runtime-local replay concern; foreclosed by I-6 + ADR-F2 + the `JournalWorkflowPauseStore` precedent — probe-resolved, advisor not council), mirroring `JournalWorkflowPauseStore` crash-safety (per-key JSONL, `fsync` + dir-fsync, torn-append self-heal, fail-soft-per-line), keyed by `run_idempotency_key` (the SAME stable id the resume join uses), co-located under `<state_ledger_dir>/engine-output`. (2) The CP driver durably records each completed step output **BEFORE** the F2 ledger-append (`_append_step_ledger_entry`) — the **RESERVE-before-COMMIT** skew discipline (the B-EFFECT-FENCE shape): the store always holds ≥ the ledger's materialized prefix, so an `EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY` resume never finds a materialized step with a missing stored output. (3) On resume the driver rehydrates the inter-step channel from the stored prefix **driven by `resume_at`** (NOT "load whatever's in the store" — a crash AFTER the store-write but BEFORE the ledger-append leaves one extra uncommitted record, ignored), **FAIL-CLOSED** if a step the ledger says materialized is missing from the store OR its stored `step_id` ≠ the re-supplied body (store↔ledger skew / body-change corruption — the B-FANOUT-PAUSE identity-check symmetry).

**§1.1 disposition — reuse B-FANOUT-PAUSE verbatim, NO operator gate.** Carrying outputs across a resume breaks the R-CC-1 design §1.1 "position-only / data-stateless resume" model — but §1.1 is a *descriptive MVP scoping note with an explicit §6 re-open trigger* ("a future execution model … would need a state-restoration story + a durable store carrying more than the position-only `PauseSnapshot`"), NOT a forbidding invariant. This arc IS that designed re-open firing. Adopt-and-note + clearance under the FULL-SPEC directive (the B-FANOUT-PAUSE precedent — contrast B4-Slice-4's §14.5.3 inv 2, which DID gate). The `api.resume` docstring's "no working-state rehydration" prose was refreshed at B-FANOUT-PAUSE to note the fan-out exception; this arc's linear exception composes the same way.

**Honest framing + scope.** The observable replay effect is **narrow** — the channel exposes only `most_recent_output()` (immediate-prior), so the replay's sole effect is "the first re-dispatched step reads its recovered predecessor's output". The capability is **opt-in + capability-built** (NOT "fires in production"): observable ONLY when `engine_output_replay=True` (the store) + `inter_step_data_flow=True` (the consumer channel) + an `EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY` workflow compose; default off → byte-identical. **LINEAR `EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY` only** — `WAL_SEGMENT` (shares the store, E-impl-2) + the non-linear resume-blind strategies (B-FANOUT-PAUSE family) are registered forward arcs (`B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY-WAL-SEGMENT` / the existing non-linear-resumption arcs). Built end-to-end (store + producer + rehydrate + consumer), not a vacuous write-only slice.

| What v1.63 adds | Substance | Source |
|---|---|---|
| **§14.23 C-RT-32 (NEW contract)** | `EngineOutputStore` durable per-run output-carrying event-history store: the carrier (crash-safe per-run JSONL, `record` + `read_outputs`) + `RuntimeConfig.engine_output_replay` flag + `HarnessContext.engine_output_store` field + the CP-driver RESERVE-before-COMMIT producer + the resume-rehydrate of the inter-step channel. | Fork §1/§2 |
| **§14.23.5 invariants (NEW)** | Opt-out byte-identical; producer GATED on `EVENT_SOURCED_REPLAY` + store-write BEFORE the ledger-append (RESERVE-before-COMMIT); rehydrate driven by `resume_at`; the empty-`read_outputs` edge DISCRIMINATED by FILE EXISTENCE — file absent → degrade to the empty-channel path (config-flip, NOT a false-failure), file present but unreadable → FAIL-CLOSED (`engine-output-replay-unreadable-store`, NOT a false-success), partial-prefix (some records, missing a committed step) → FAIL-CLOSED (skew), stored-step_id≠body → FAIL-CLOSED (identity); keyed by `run_idempotency_key`; no §5.2-hash / IS-contract change (dedicated store, not the F2 ledger); genuine non-vacuity (real store on disk → rehydrate → real LLM dispatcher → real provider receives the recovered output + a negative control, no proxy). | Fork §2/§4 + decorrelated review |

## Change-note (v1.61 → v1.62)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-19).** v1.62 lands **functional operator EDIT** at the wrap-time HITL gate — R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc **B-EDIT-CARRIER** (`.harness/class_1_fork_hitl_edit_carrier_drift_str_vs_mapping.md`; spine ledger). It RESOLVES the U-RT-120 / B3-impl-3 carrier-drift fork (D-edit.B interim) and **amends §14.8.2 step 4i + NOTE 6-ii** so the `EDIT` branch APPLIES the operator's edit instead of raising the interim `HITLGateEditCarrierDriftError`.

**The gap (recap).** §14.8.2 step 4i + NOTE 6-ii mandate **replace-not-merge**: the operator's `edited_proposal` becomes the new `step.step_payload` verbatim. The mandate presumes the CP-canonical *structured* carrier (`HITLGateResult.edited_proposal: Mapping[str, Any]`), but the wired runtime ask-surface returns `AskUserQuestionResult.edited_proposal: str | None` because MCP elicitation is **flat-schema** (primitives only — it cannot deliver a nested Mapping). So the operator's `str` could not be applied verbatim to the `Mapping[str, Any]` step_payload without the decode/mutation semantics NOTE 6-ii deferred to "a future workflow-mutation-discipline arc." B3-impl-3 landed an honest interim raise (`HITLGateEditCarrierDriftError`) to surface the drift rather than silently drop the edit; this arc is that workflow-mutation-discipline arc.

**The resolution — mutation discipline (A) JSON-decode-then-replace.** The fork enumerated three candidate disciplines; the **cleared constraints foreclose to one**: the landed flat-`str` MCP-elicitation carrier + the committed **replace-not-merge** mandate + the arbitrary-nested `step_payload` target. (B) structured-flat typed-field elicitation cannot carry an arbitrary nested payload (e.g. an `INFERENCE_STEP`'s `ProviderAgnosticPayload`); (C) field-level patch/merge would **override** the committed replace-not-merge mandate. Only **(A) JSON-decode the operator `str` → a `Mapping`, then replace `step.step_payload` verbatim** preserves replace-not-merge AND carries arbitrary nesting — and it mirrors the already-landed tool-args precedent `r_cxa_2_producer_loop_factory._parse_edited_arguments`. Because (A) *preserves* (does not sacrifice) the committed decision, this is the deferred decode-semantics fill — FULL-SPEC pre-authorized, **no operator gate** (probe-resolved; the fork's "operator ratification" framing predates the FULL-SPEC directive).

**What v1.62 amends.**

Retires the interim `HITLGateEditCarrierDriftError`'s fork-pending runtime-shape surfacing. The step-4h audit records the attempt (`edited_proposal_hash` over the raw `str`) BEFORE the raise (symmetric to REJECT).

The durable-async **resume** path (§14.8.2 step 4-bis pause → resume) currently dispatches the resumed step UNCHANGED for ALL response types — `hitl_gate_composer.py` reads `resume_state.hitl_response` and `return self._dispatch_inner(...)` per the v2.24 AC #7 MVP "auto-approve the resumed gate" shape, the resumed-response integration into the 4h/4i flow being explicitly deferred per FM-2. ## Change-note (v1.59 → v1.60)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-18).** v1.60 adds a **NEW contract §14.22 C-RT-31 `RuntimeEffectFence`** — a hand-rolled (I-6) durable **effect-boundary fence** at the `RuntimeToolDispatcher` `call_tool` sink that guarantees **at-most-once EXECUTION** of a non-idempotent tool-step effect across durable-engine retries and resumes. R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc **B-EFFECT-FENCE** (`.harness/class_1_fork_b_effect_fence_at_most_once_execution.md`; spine ledger line 49, `design-fork-first per X-AL-3, since a sink-fencing surface is new`). This closes the floor-(ii) gap the durable engine classes (E sub-program) advertise but did not deliver: the U-RT-123 reconciler CAS (and every durable resume) guarantees at-most-once *claim of a revision*, NOT at-most-once *execution* of the steps a resume re-runs — so a crash between a tool-step's effect (`workflow_driver.py:2031` dispatch) and its per-step ledger COMMIT (`:2336`) re-dispatches the effected-but-uncommitted step (`_determine_resume_at` advances `resume_at` to the first step absent from the contiguous-materialized prefix — shared by all four durable engine classes) → the same external effect (`git_push`/`send_email`/any side-effecting MCP tool) fires a SECOND time.

**Additive + operator-opt-in, no committed invariant sacrificed.** Gated on a NEW `RuntimeConfig.effect_fencing: bool = False`; default `False` → no fence constructed → the dispatcher reserves nothing → **byte-identical to pre-v1.60** (no claim files, no behavior change). The `StepDispatcher.dispatch` signature is **UNCHANGED** (the fence is read off the dispatcher's frozen construction reference). **No operator gate** — additive + opt-in; the mechanism is the U-RT-123 reconciler's crash-atomic `O_EXCL`/`os.link` claim re-keyed to the per-effect `idempotency_key`, resolved by landed precedent; the one nameable C10⊥C11 fence-scope tension (uniform-all-tools vs per-tool-classified vs opt-in) is **probe-resolved** by scoping to "tool steps under a durable/resumable engine" — fence I/O is paid only when a resume can re-fire (exactly when double-fire is possible), no new `ToolContract` classification field, no AS fork → advisor, not council (§10.9). FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`) pre-authorizes the build + the back-flow.

**At-most-once *per (run, step) invocation*, NOT exactly-once (the honest residual — mirrors the reconciler).** `try_reserve(idempotency_key)` is the atomic claim on the harness's **per-invocation identity** (the per-(run, step, tool) `idempotency_key`): the FIRST dispatch wins (the effect fires); any re-dispatch of the *same* effect LOSES — both the cross-process RESUME re-dispatch of an effected-but-uncommitted step AND an in-process `RetryBreakerToolDispatcher` retry (the fence error is not a transient class, so the breaker fail-fasts it; for a non-idempotent effect, fail-closing a transient-failure retry is the *correct* conservative behavior — you cannot safely retry an effect that may have fired). A *fresh* re-invocation of the same declared tool step within one run is **not** conflated with a resume re-fire: a looping topology already assigns a distinct key per invocation (EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER's monotonic `entry_index` as `parent_idempotency_key` at `workflow_driver.py:3620-3628`; fan-out's branch-scoped `compose_branch_path`) — it MUST, else the IS `idempotency_key`-only dedup (C-IS-07 §7.5) would silently drop iteration-2's ledger entry — so a loop iteration gets a NEW key (fires), only a resume re-dispatch reuses the key (fenced). A lost claim raises `EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError`; the **v1.60 interim** maps it to a **FAILED `RunResult`** (honest, never a silent double-fire), and the genuine §22.1 operator-resolvable PAUSE is the registered `B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE` follow-on (§14.22.7). The fire-then-crash-before-commit window is ambiguous to the harness, so the conservative fail-close (a reserved-but-unfired effect also fail-closes its re-dispatch) is the honest answer, mirroring the reconciler's §22.1 posture. **COMMIT = the EXISTING per-step ledger entry** (one source of truth); the fence adds only the RESERVE (pre-fire) marker — no second commit record.

**Non-vacuity is the deliverable (the live trap — advisor; cf. B-TOOL-GATE #653 wired-but-production-dead).** v1.60 ships the fence at the REAL sink, proven by-execution with NO proxy: a real `RuntimeToolDispatcher` re-dispatching the same effect fires the underlying tool body EXACTLY ONCE (a counting MCP tool), with a NEGATIVE CONTROL proving that *without* the fence the same two dispatches double-fire, and a fresh-dispatcher-over-the-same-on-disk-fence-dir test standing in for a genuine process restart (crash-then-resume). The driver re-dispatch hands the sink a byte-identical per-step `idempotency_key` (proven through the real `execute_workflow` resume path) so the fence resolves the re-dispatched effect to the SAME claim.

**Single-host (the reconciler's bound posture).** The default claim is atomic on a local filesystem; cross-host effect-fencing is distributed-impossible under {I-6 ∧ no-unsafe-TTL} and folds into the deferred F-CC multi-host recovery item — exactly as for U-RT-123. Three follow-ons registered (§14.22.7): auto-activation under durable engine classes (`B-EFFECT-FENCE-DURABLE-AUTO`), per-tool idempotency classification to fence only declared-non-idempotent tools (`B-EFFECT-FENCE-PER-TOOL`), and the §22.1 HITL-routing refinement that turns the interim fail-closed raise into a genuine operator-resolvable pause (`B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE`, composes with `B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY` for suppress-and-continue).

**No §5.2-hash / IS-spec / CP-spec contract / OD-spec / ADR change.** The fence claim is a side file (a separate durable store under `repository_root/.harness/effect-fence`), NOT a state-ledger entry — the per-step ledger entry shape is byte-identical, so the C-IS-05 §5.2 entry hash is unchanged; the CP `StepDispatcher`/`StepExecutionContext` contracts are byte-unchanged (the fence reads the existing `step_context.parent_idempotency_key`); I-6 honored (no vendored Temporal/DBOS activity-dedup); ADR-F2 single-threaded-write honored (the fence is a separate store, not the ledger writer).

**Source of fix.** B-EFFECT-FENCE fork doc + the E-impl-3b finding §4 F-2 (`.harness/r-fs-1-e-impl-3b-finding.md`) + HEAD body-grounding of `workflow_driver.py` (the effect-at-`:2031` / commit-at-`:2336` window + `_determine_resume_at` `:2432`), `runtime_tool_dispatcher.py` (the `call_tool` sink + `_compose_idempotency_key`), `reconciler_pause_resume_substrate.py` (the `_claim_resume_revision` crash-atomic claim precedent), `retry_breaker_tool.py` (the `_TRANSIENT_TOOL_DISPATCH_ERRORS` fail-fast classification) + advisor (full-transcript) review (non-vacuity-FIRST; the durable-resume scoping that collapses the C10⊥C11 tension; suppress-not-replay; the RESERVE-is-the-new-piece / COMMIT-is-the-existing-ledger-entry decomposition).

**Amendments.**

| **§14.22 C-RT-31 (NEW contract)** | `RuntimeEffectFence` durable at-most-once effect fence: the carrier (crash-atomic `O_EXCL`/`os.link` `try_reserve`) + `RuntimeConfig.effect_fencing` flag + the `RuntimeToolDispatcher` sink reserve-before-`call_tool` + `EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError` fail-close. | Fork §1/§2 |
| **§14.22.5 invariants (NEW)** | Opt-out byte-identical; dispatch signature unchanged; at-most-once (resume + retry both fail-close); COMMIT = existing per-step ledger entry; single-host; no §5.2-hash change; genuine non-vacuity (real sink, counting tool, negative control, no proxy). | Fork §2/§4 |

## Change-note (v1.57 → v1.58)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-18).** v1.58 adds a **third** per-run cost-rollup field to **§9 C-RT-09 `RunResult`** — **`cost_attribution_by_provider_discriminator: tuple[CrossFamilyCostRollup, ...]`** — the cross-family **family-tag** (`frontier_managed` / `frontier_managed_alt` / `local_ollama`) cost breakdown, **and populates it in production** by tagging each LLM-dispatch `SpanCostRecord.provider_discriminator` with the dispatched provider's family. R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc **B-FALLBACK-CHAIN-FAMILY-COST-COMPOSITION** (`.harness/class_1_fork_b_fallback_chain_family_cost_composition.md`; spine ledger line 120; registered at arc CA v1.53 §9 + arc B-COST-DISCRIMINATOR-TAXONOMY **OD v1.30 §15.1.2** — *"the field stays reserved for the §15.3 fallback-chain composition to populate"*). This makes `RollupAxis.PER_PROVIDER_DISCRIMINATOR` **non-vacuous in production** — it was defined + admissible but always empty (every production LLM cost record wrote `provider_discriminator = None`).

**Additive, no committed invariant sacrificed (LIKE v1.53 / v1.57).** The new field is **optional with default `()`** — a minor bump per the §9 version-evolution invariant, mirroring v1.45's `pause_snapshot` + v1.57's `cost_attribution_by_dispatch_kind`. The existing `cost_attribution` (PER_PROVIDER_AND_MODEL) + `cost_attribution_by_dispatch_kind` (PER_DISPATCH_KIND) fields are **PRESERVED VERBATIM**. **No operator gate** (adopt-and-note per workspace `CLAUDE.md` §12.4.1 + `[[feedback-gate-only-on-meaningful-architecture-change]]`; advisor-confirmed advisor-not-council/no-AUQ — runtime-internal cost surfacing + a provider→family map, no nameable cross-domain tension; the apparent A/B "parent-record vs tag-the-record" fork was **probe-resolved** as a span-layer-vs-record-layer false dichotomy at OD §15.1.2). **No OD spec change** — OD v1.30 §15.1.2 already defines the field's `str | None` shape AND assigns population to *this* arc — so v1.58 is **runtime-only**. FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`) pre-authorizes the build + the back-flow.

**LLM-subtotal partition (NOT a full-run partition — UNLIKE v1.53 / v1.57).** This axis **skips records whose `provider_discriminator` is `None`** (tool / validator / webhook dispatches have no provider family, §15.1.2), so `sum(e.total_cost)` here equals the **LLM-dispatch subtotal**, NOT the total run cost. The other two axes partition the full dollar total; this one partitions the LLM slice. The correct invariant is therefore `Σ cost_attribution_by_provider_discriminator.total_cost == Σ(LLM-dispatch records).total_cost` (no LLM record double-counted) — deliberately **NOT** the v1.53/v1.57 "`Σ == total run cost`" invariant (asserting that would be a false RED).

**Mapping (provider-fixed, per the OD §15.1 example).** `ANTHROPIC → frontier_managed`, `{OPENAI, GOOGLE} → frontier_managed_alt` (the §15.3 example chain "Anthropic → cross-family OpenAI/Gemini → local Ollama" groups OpenAI/Gemini as the cross-family middle tier), `LOCAL_OPEN_WEIGHT → local_ollama`. This is impl-to-cleared-**example**; `CrossFamilyTag` is deliberately **NOT extended**. The `ProviderFamily → CrossFamilyTag` map is homed in `harness-runtime` (`harness_runtime/lifecycle/cross_family_cost_tag.py`) — `CrossFamilyTag` is OD-homed + `ProviderFamily` is CP-homed, so a map in either axis is a cross-axis cycle (`[[carrier-home-defect-pattern]]`).

**Reconciles a v1.57 §9 body-application miss (bundled doc-hygiene, `[[spec-prose-plan-body-drift-pattern]]`).** v1.57's change-note declared `cost_attribution_by_dispatch_kind` added to §9 C-RT-09, but the §9 **body table + invariants** were never edited — the field is code-landed (`api.py`) + change-note-declared, yet the canonical §9 table omitted it. v1.58 adds **both** the missing `cost_attribution_by_dispatch_kind` row/invariant (reconcile) **and** the new `cost_attribution_by_provider_discriminator` row/invariant (both touch the same §9 table).

**Source of fix.** B-FALLBACK-CHAIN-FAMILY-COST-COMPOSITION fork doc + HEAD body-grounding of `retry_breaker_fallback.py` (the production fallback traversal — outer chain span, per-attempt inner dispatch), `llm_dispatch._attribute_cost_best_effort` (the cost callsite, `provider_name` in scope), `cost_attribution_llm_dispatch.py` (the helper), `cross_family_rollup.py` (`PER_PROVIDER_DISCRIMINATOR` + `_validate_family_tag` skips-`None`), OD spec §15.1 / §15.3 / §15.1.2 + advisor (full-transcript) review (resolved the span-layer §15.3 vs record-layer §15.1.2 false dichotomy; flagged the LLM-subtotal invariant + the hollow-`FallbackChainCostComposition` trap — that carrier has no consumer, so it is NOT constructed in production).

## Change-note (v1.56 → v1.57)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-18).** v1.57 adds a second per-run cost-rollup field to **§9 C-RT-09 `RunResult`** — **`cost_attribution_by_dispatch_kind: tuple[CrossFamilyCostRollup, ...]`** — the dispatch-type (llm/tool/validator/webhook) cost breakdown. R-FS-1 standalone `B-*` arc **B-COST-DISCRIMINATOR-TAXONOMY** (`.harness/class_1_fork_b_cost_discriminator_taxonomy.md`; spine ledger line 118; surfaced + registered at arc CA, v1.53 §9 line 51 — *"the dispatch-type breakdown is the most operator-meaningful rollup and is exactly the one this latent defect blocks"*). The paired **OD spec v1.30** authors the new `RollupAxis.PER_DISPATCH_KIND` + the `DispatchKind` vocabulary + the `provider_discriminator` per-dispatch-optional correction this field consumes.

**Additive, no committed invariant sacrificed (LIKE v1.53, UNLIKE v1.56).** The new field is **optional with default `()`** — a minor bump per the §9 version-evolution invariant, exactly mirroring v1.45's `pause_snapshot: PauseSnapshot | None = None` and v1.53's axis-naming. The existing `cost_attribution` field (PER_PROVIDER_AND_MODEL, v1.53) is **PRESERVED VERBATIM**. No operator gate (adopt-and-note per workspace `CLAUDE.md` §12.4.1 + `[[feedback-gate-only-on-meaningful-architecture-change]]`; advisor-confirmed advisor-not-council/no-AUQ — OD-internal cost-taxonomy type design + a runtime surfacing, no nameable cross-domain tension). FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`) pre-authorizes the build + the OD/runtime back-flow.

**Sum-invariant preserved (two orthogonal single-axis partitions).** `cost_attribution` (per-(provider, model)) and `cost_attribution_by_dispatch_kind` (per-dispatch-kind) are **separate single-axis** tuples, NOT one concatenated multi-axis tuple. Each record has exactly one `dispatch_kind` and exactly one `(provider, model)`, so **each field independently** satisfies `sum(e.total_cost) == total run cost` — two orthogonal partitions of the same dollar total, no double-count (the multi-axis-flat-tuple hazard v1.53 §9 named is avoided by the separate field).

**Source of fix.** B-COST-DISCRIMINATOR-TAXONOMY fork doc §2 (Options B+C converge; spec authority C-OD-15 §15.1 resolves `provider_discriminator` = family tag → production write is the bug) + HEAD body-grounding of `harness_od.cross_family_rollup` + `harness_od.idempotency_join_dedup` (`SpanCostRecord`) + the four `cost_attribution_*_dispatch.py` helpers + `api.py` `_build_run_result` / `_rollup_cost_attribution` + the v1.53 §9 amendment (the precedent) + advisor (full-transcript) review.

## Change-note (v1.55 → v1.56)

**Status posture (PROPOSED 2026-06-17).** v1.56 authors **§14.9.11 — per-tool sandbox-tier resolution + per-dispatch driver selection** (NEW), the R-FS-1 arc **B6 Slice 2** (`B-PER-TOOL-SANDBOX-TIER`; `.harness/beyond-mvp-capability-boundary-ledger.md` line 126; grounding `.harness/r-fs-1-arc-and-unit-map.md` §"R-FS-1·B6"). Per `.harness/class_1_fork_b6_slice_2_per_tool_sandbox_tier.md` (filed this arc), **Option A operator-ratified** (AskUserQuestion 2026-06-17 — "Full per-tool (A)"). This lifts the per-server-uniform→per-tool carve-out that §14.9.9 Scope-boundary + §14.9.10 D4 / inv-3 / Scope-boundary(b) named as "the distinct future arc B6". The B6-Slice-1 (v1.54 §14.9.8) per-*host* `compose_transport_floor` left the within-host resolver **constant** (`_build_default_policy_sandbox_resolver` — `resolve(_contract,_step)` ignores both args, `runtime_tool_dispatcher_factory.py:103`); v1.56 replaces it with a per-`(contract, step)` call to the full 10-row `sandbox_tier_floor(tool, deployment_surface, blast_radius_tier, mcp_transport, mcp_server)` (C-AS-02 §2.3), `max()`-composed with the §14.9.8 deployment-surface default — so the per-tool **forcing** rows (1-2: `forces_computer_use`/`forces_code_execution` → TIER_4) + per-tool **blast-radius** rows (7-10) become reachable per tool.

**The one committed-invariant relaxation (operator-gated).** §14.9.9 inv-3 + §14.9.10 inv-3 ("per-server-uniform, construction-time" driver) are **RELAXED** to per-dispatch driver selection: each host gets a `dict[SandboxTier, ToolExecutionDriver]` registry (one driver per tier reachable by that host's tools — computable at the stage-5 factory because `tool_registry` is "immutable after start()", §14.9.1), and dispatch selects the driver matching the per-tool resolved tier. This is the genuine ratification-boundary fork (mirrors B4 Slice 4's §14.5.3 relaxation). **FR-1 (delivered ≥ resolved) is PRESERVED and TIGHTENED** — Option A delivers `delivered == resolved` per tool (no over-isolation), so the `sandbox_tier` span/result (§14.9.1) + the per-tier cost attribution (v1.53 §9 CA arc) report the tier **actually delivered** (the audit/cost-fidelity discriminator that drove Option A over the spec-complete Option B, which pinned-at-max and under-reported). The driver self-guard stays exact-match `== required_tier` (`docker_tool_execution_driver.py:71`) — correct under Option A because the selected driver's tier == the resolved tier.

**UNLIKE the additive v1.53** (CA — no committed invariant sacrificed) **and v1.54** (B6 Slice 1 — *fulfilled* a committed ADR-D2 §1.3 mandate, sacrificing nothing), v1.56 **relaxes a committed invariant** (per-server-uniform driver) → **operator-gated**, ratified per the fork doc AUQ. FULL-SPEC (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`) pre-authorizes the build + back-flow.

**Continuity (no regression of B6 Slice 1).** Slice 1's `compose_transport_floor` (STDIO→TIER_3, per-host) is **subsumed** by `sandbox_tier_floor` rows 3-6 per-tool (`sandbox_tier_floor` rows 3-6 ≡ `mcp_transport_floor`, AS C-AS-10 §10.1 AC5). The per-tool resolver maxes the **surface default** (`resolve_effective_sandbox_defaults`, the surface-aware default WITHOUT the host-blast transport floor) with the full per-tool `sandbox_tier_floor` — so a STDIO tool still floors to TIER_3 (row 3, per-tool), **preserving** the Slice-1 ADR-D2 §1.3 mandate while refining the blast input from per-host to per-tool. The L0-remote REFUSE outcome is unreachable-by-construction (refused at registration `mcp_host.py`); a resolver REFUSE is a defensive raise.

**Cross-axis cascade.** `ToolContract` gains the `ToolMetadata` forcing discriminators (`forces_computer_use`/`forces_code_execution`/`is_deterministic_inhouse`) — AS spec **C-AS-03 §3.1** (v1.10 → v1.11), additive with safe non-forcing defaults (every existing contract resolves byte-identically; only a new declaration opts into rows 1-2). The AS↔runtime registration seam (`RawContractInput` + the v1.40 stage-3a `MCPToolContractConverter`) threads the new fields.

**Scope discipline.** v1.56 authors ONLY §14.9.11 (new) + the inv-3 relaxation it names; §14.9.1–§14.9.10, §14.10+, §14.20, §9, §5.2-hash, and all prior change-note blocks are **PRESERVED VERBATIM** (delta-only-spec convention). **No new fail class** (a per-tool resolved tier with no registrable driver reuses the existing §14.9.9 `RT-FAIL-SANDBOX-DRIVER-UNAVAILABLE`, now raised per-tier at the factory). **No IS-spec / §5.2-hash change** (the sandbox decision is dispatch-time policy output, not a determinism config dimension — unchanged from §14.9.8). **No ADR change** (`sandbox_tier_floor` / `ToolMetadata` / `SandboxTier` are the reused C-AS-02 / ADR-D2 §1.5.1 AS types; ADR-F4's "guarantee not advisory" posture is honored — delivered == resolved). The resolver body, the per-host per-tier driver-registry build (a `PerTierToolExecutionDriver` composite implementing the `ToolExecutionDriver` protocol — so the bare dispatcher's `dict[ServerName, ToolExecutionDriver]` field is byte-unchanged), and the dispatch-time driver selection are **impl-discretion** (the `harness-runtime` + `harness-as` impl lands in this arc).
