## §14.20 C-RT-28 — `ManagedAgentsStepDispatcher` + `ManagedAgents` executable-consumer contract (new at v1.55)

**Contract surface.** A production `StepDispatcher` for `StepKind.MANAGED_AGENTS` (CP spec v1.39 §5.2/§25.2) that executes a workflow step's body via a **vendor-run Managed Agents session** (Anthropic `beta.sessions.*`) rather than a harness-orchestrated loop. Consumed at the single CP driver dispatch seam (`step_dispatchers.lookup(StepKind.MANAGED_AGENTS).dispatch(...)`); bound at bootstrap stage 5 gated on `DeploymentSurface.MANAGED_CLOUD` + an operator config opt-in. Formalizes the already-built, R-820-live-proven carrier `harness-runtime/src/harness_runtime/lifecycle/managed_agents.py` and authors the missing production-wiring surface. Mirrors C-RT-27 (skill activation) + C-RT-24 (pause/resume) + C-RT-22 (memory tool) operator-opt-in stage-5-factory precedent.

**PRD enablement.** Completes the managed-cloud deployment surface (ADR-D1/D2 3-tier: local-development / self-hosted-server / managed-cloud). The `managed_agents.*` namespace producer-side surface is already built (AS spec §14.5 `managed_agents.*` 3-attribute schema + the `managed_agents.runtime` span helper) + live-proven (R-820, PR #380 → H_T-AS-8f SUBSTANTIVE_RETIRED in `.harness/substitutions.yaml`); C-RT-28 closes the missing piece — a production dispatch path that reaches the carrier from `execute_workflow`. Before C-RT-28 the only importers of `lifecycle.managed_agents` were the R-820 proof script + its unit test; no step kind routed to it.

**ADR commitment(s) honored.** ADR-D1 v1.2 (engine + replay; managed-cloud admits engine class 1) + ADR-D2 v1.2 §Decision (3 deployment surfaces incl. managed-cloud, Anthropic/AWS/GCP candidates) + ADR-D6 v1.2 (OTel `managed_agents.*` namespace ingestion at OD).

**Fork-resolution provenance.** `.harness/class_1_fork_m_managed_agents_stepkind_c_rt_28.md` — Class 1, operator-ratified 2026-06-17 (this arc, same-session-as-filing). Option B (new `MANAGED_AGENTS` StepKind, not overload `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH`); §14.20 slot; contract-id C-RT-28 (honor reserved); surface-gated `MANAGED_CLOUD` + opt-in. The closed-at-5 `StepKind` extension is the operator-gated half (paired CP v1.39); C-RT-28 is the additive runtime back-flow authored against that ratification.

### §14.20.1 Architectural surfaces introduced

**Formalized (built carriers at `lifecycle/managed_agents.py` — contract-bound here, no code change):**

- `ManagedAgentsClientProtocol` — minimal async port. `create_session(*, agent_id: str, environment_id: str, title: str | None = None, metadata: Mapping[str, str] | None = None) -> ManagedAgentSession`; `send_event(*, session_id: str, event: ManagedAgentEvent) -> ManagedAgentEvent`; `retrieve_session(*, session_id: str) -> ManagedAgentSession`; `cancel_session(*, session_id: str) -> ManagedAgentSession`.
- `AnthropicManagedAgentsClient` — SDK adapter satisfying the Protocol (wraps `client.beta.sessions.*` in `asyncio.to_thread`; tags `betas=[ANTHROPIC_MANAGED_AGENTS_BETA]`; `cancel_session` interrupts + archives, returns `status=CANCELED`).
- `ManagedAgentSession` (frozen, slots): `session_id` / `agent_id` / `environment_id` / `status: ManagedAgentSessionStatus` / `runtime_ms: int` / `billable_seconds: float`. `ManagedAgentEvent` (frozen): `event_type: str` / `payload: Mapping[str, Any]`. `ManagedAgentSessionStatus` (9-state StrEnum: `CREATED`/`IDLE`/`RUNNING`/`RESCHEDULING`/`PAUSED`/`COMPLETED`/`FAILED`/`CANCELED`/`TERMINATED`).
- `managed_agents_runtime_span(*, tracer, session=None, session_id=None, runtime_ms=None, billable_seconds=None)` — async-ctx emitting the `managed_agents.runtime` span with the AS §14.5 namespace (`managed_agents.runtime_ms` / `managed_agents.session_id` / `managed_agents.billable_seconds`).
- `ANTHROPIC_MANAGED_AGENTS_BETA = "managed-agents-2026-04-01"`.

**NEW (the production-wiring surface):**

`ManagedAgentsStepDispatcher` — satisfies the CP `StepDispatcher` Protocol (C-CP-25 §25.3.3.4). The dispatch is **async** (the client is async) per the C-RT-15 inner / C-RT-17 sub-agent precedent; bound via `SyncDispatcherFacade` at the `StepKindDispatcherRegistry` (the driver per-step seam is sync, the facade bridges per the U-RT-59 Path-B INFERENCE_STEP pattern):

```python
class ManagedAgentsStepDispatcher:
    """Dispatches a StepKind.MANAGED_AGENTS step to a vendor-run Managed
    Agents session. Constructed at bootstrap stage 5 by
    materialize_managed_agents_dispatcher_stage per §14.20.3. Holds a
    ManagedAgentsClientProtocol + the ctx.tracer_provider. The harness does
    NOT orchestrate the agent loop — the vendor does (no topology-admissibility,
    no subagent.* spans; cf. C-RT-17 SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH).
    """
    async def dispatch(
        self,
        binding: StepEffectiveBinding,
        step: WorkflowStep,
        *,
        step_context: StepExecutionContext,
    ) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
        ...  # §14.20.2
```

`ManagedAgentsConfig` (RuntimeConfig sub-model §3 — presence + `DeploymentSurface.MANAGED_CLOUD` signals operator opt-in; parallel to `SkillActivationHookConfig` / `ValidatorFrameworkConfig` / `PauseResumeProtocolConfig`). It carries the operator-supplied client object + the decoupled managed-agents facade timeout (no credentials embedded — the SDK client is operator-constructed):

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ManagedAgentsConfig:
    """Opt-in sub-model — presence + DeploymentSurface.MANAGED_CLOUD signals
    operator opt-in to managed-agents step dispatch.

    `client` is the concrete ManagedAgentsClientProtocol (e.g.
    AnthropicManagedAgentsClient over a live SDK client), supplied at the
    operator-controlled bootstrap site. Typed `Any` (not the structural
    Protocol) so Pydantic v2 schema-generation at RuntimeConfig introspection
    succeeds — the runtime_checkable Protocol is duck-typed at dispatch, not
    validated at the dataclass layer (same pattern as
    SkillActivationHookConfig.hook). No credentials embedded.

    `step_timeout_seconds` is the SyncDispatcherFacade `result_timeout_seconds`
    used ONLY for the StepKind.MANAGED_AGENTS facade — DECOUPLED from the
    shared RuntimeConfig.step_dispatch_timeout_seconds (30s) per §14.20.3.
    """
    client: Any = None
    step_timeout_seconds: float = 600.0
```

`HarnessContext.managed_agents_client: ManagedAgentsClientProtocol | None` (NEW field §4; `None` when not opted-in or surface ≠ managed-cloud).

### §14.20.2 Dispatch discipline

A `MANAGED_AGENTS` step dispatches as (the dispatcher reads its inputs from `step.step_payload`, opaque to the driver per §25.3.3.4):

1. **Read `step_payload`** (the managed-agents dispatch inputs): `agent_id: str`, `environment_id: str`, and the initial event (`event_type: str` + `payload: Mapping[str, Any]`); optional `title` / `metadata`. The exact key schema + the step-body→event mapping are implementation discretion (§14.20.7).
2. **Create session** — `session = await client.create_session(agent_id=..., environment_id=..., title=..., metadata=...)`.
3. **Send the step event** — `await client.send_event(session_id=session.session_id, event=ManagedAgentEvent(event_type=..., payload=...))`.
4. **Poll to terminal** — `await client.retrieve_session(session_id=...)` on a bounded poll loop until a terminal status (`IDLE` / `COMPLETED` / `FAILED` / `CANCELED` / `TERMINATED`) or the poll budget is exhausted (budget mechanism §14.20.7). The R-820 proof drove to `IDLE`. **On poll-budget exhaustion** the session is still running server-side and billable; the dispatcher MUST best-effort `await client.cancel_session(session_id=...)` before raising (§14.20.5 invariant 7), so a given-up session is not orphaned. A cancel that itself fails MUST NOT mask the primary budget-exhausted error (the load-bearing signal).
5. **Emit telemetry** — open `managed_agents_runtime_span(tracer=<from ctx.tracer_provider>, session=<final session>)` so the `managed_agents.runtime` span carries `session_id` / `runtime_ms` / `billable_seconds`.
6. **Return** a `Mapping[str, Any]` outcome the driver accumulates into `final_state` — at minimum `{session_id, status, runtime_ms, billable_seconds}` + any returned event payload.
7. **Error mapping** — a terminal `FAILED` / `TERMINATED` status (or poll-budget exhaustion, or an SDK error) → raise a typed error the driver maps to `RT-FAIL-MANAGED-AGENTS-SESSION` per the §11 §25.3.3.4 try/except discipline (the step fails; the workflow's failure-mode handling per C-CP-25 §25.7 applies). `CANCELED` (operator interrupt) maps to the same dispatch-failure class unless the caller treats cancellation as success (implementation discretion).

### §14.20.3 Lifecycle stage placement

**Stage 5 (LOOP_INIT):** NEW factory `materialize_managed_agents_dispatcher_stage(config: RuntimeConfig, ctx: _MutableHarnessContext) -> ManagedAgentsStepDispatcher | None`. The factory returns the dispatcher (or `None`); the stage-5 caller does the binding + facade-wrapping (so the `StepKindDispatcherRegistry` is constructed once with all dispatchers, the established stage-5 pattern). Factory body:

1. **If `config.managed_agents_config is None` OR `config.deployment_surface != DeploymentSurface.MANAGED_CLOUD`:** return `None`. (Opt-out / non-managed-cloud path — `ctx.managed_agents_client` stays `None`, no `StepKind.MANAGED_AGENTS` row is added → a `MANAGED_AGENTS` step then fails closed at `registry.lookup` with `StepKindDispatcherNotBoundError` → `RT-FAIL-STEP-KIND-DISPATCHER-NOT-BOUND`, no silent under-execution.)
2. **Else (opted-in on managed-cloud):** if `ctx.tracer_provider` is unbound OR `config.managed_agents_config.client` is absent → raise `ManagedAgentsStageMaterializeError` (`RT-FAIL-MANAGED-AGENTS-STAGE-MATERIALIZE`, bootstrap-fatal §14.20.4). Else construct + return `ManagedAgentsStepDispatcher(client=config.managed_agents_config.client, tracer_provider=ctx.tracer_provider)`.

**Stage-5 caller (`stage_5_loop_init`).** When the factory returns a dispatcher: bind `ctx.managed_agents_client = config.managed_agents_config.client`; add `StepKind.MANAGED_AGENTS → SyncDispatcherFacade(dispatcher, result_timeout_seconds=config.managed_agents_config.step_timeout_seconds)` to the dispatcher map. The facade timeout reads `managed_agents_config.step_timeout_seconds` (600s default) — **NOT** the shared `step_dispatch_timeout_seconds` (30s) the INFERENCE / SUB_AGENT / TOOL facades use. A vendor-run managed-agents session runs minutes; binding to the shared 30s bound would fire `RT-FAIL-STEP-DISPATCH-TIMEOUT` prematurely while the vendor session keeps running, billable, never cancelled (the abandoned coroutine never reaches its §14.20.2-step-4 cancel-on-give-up path). See §14.20.5 invariant 7.

**Stage 5 ordering.** Sibling-of `materialize_skill_activation_emitter_stage` / `materialize_validator_framework_stage` / `materialize_pause_resume_protocol_stage` at the stage-5 LOOP_INIT bucket; intra-stage ordering arbitrary (the factory's only dependency is the stage-4 `ctx.tracer_provider` + the registry being constructed before binding).

### §14.20.4 Failure-mode taxonomy

2 new fail classes added to §11 runtime-local fail-class taxonomy:

| Fail class | Trigger | Permanent? |
|---|---|---|
| `RT-FAIL-MANAGED-AGENTS-STAGE-MATERIALIZE` | `materialize_managed_agents_dispatcher_stage` cannot construct the client/dispatcher when opted-in on `MANAGED_CLOUD` (e.g. the operator-supplied client is absent/invalid; tracer provider unbound at stage-5 entry; dispatcher construction raises) | YES (bootstrap aborts; fail-closed per ADR-F4 v1.1) |
| `RT-FAIL-MANAGED-AGENTS-SESSION` | A managed-agents dispatch does not reach a success terminal status — terminal `FAILED` / `TERMINATED` (/ `CANCELED` unless caller-treated-as-success), poll-budget exhaustion, or an SDK/transport error | NO (step-failure; the workflow's C-CP-25 §25.7 failure handling applies) |

### §14.20.5 Invariants

1. **Dispatcher bound at most once per bootstrap; surface-gated.** Stage 5 binds `StepKind.MANAGED_AGENTS` only on `DeploymentSurface.MANAGED_CLOUD` + `managed_agents_config` non-None. No re-binding at dispatch-time.
2. **Fail-closed on non-managed-cloud / opt-out.** When unbound, a `MANAGED_AGENTS` step raises `StepKindDispatcherNotBoundError` → `RT-FAIL-STEP-KIND-DISPATCHER-NOT-BOUND` at `registry.lookup`; never silently skipped or downgraded.
3. **`managed_agents.runtime` span at every dispatch.** Each managed-agents dispatch emits the span carrying the AS §14.5 `managed_agents.*` namespace (session_id / runtime_ms / billable_seconds). Sampling per OD `sampling_mode` (the `managed_agents.runtime` always-sampled floor).
4. **Backward-compatible.** Default-config workflows (no `managed_agents_config`) bind no dispatcher + emit no `managed_agents.*` spans. Byte-identical to pre-v1.55.
5. **Vendor owns the loop — the architectural distinction from `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH`.** The dispatcher performs NO topology-admissibility check + emits NO `subagent.*`/`topology.*` spans; the vendor session runs the agent loop server-side. (This is exactly why Option A — riding `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH` — was foreclosed: its dispatcher hard-requires those harness-orchestration semantics. Fork doc §2.1.)
6. **No embedded credentials; live run never auto-fired.** The contract surface holds no API key / cloud identity; the SDK client is operator-supplied at the bootstrap site. A live managed-cloud run is surfaced at the dispatch boundary for authorization, never auto-fired (`[[feedback-background-agent-no-unilateral-paid-calls-or-secret-relocation]]`).
7. **Decoupled facade timeout + cancel-on-give-up — no orphaned billable session.** The `StepKind.MANAGED_AGENTS` facade binds to `managed_agents_config.step_timeout_seconds` (600s default), NOT the shared 30s `step_dispatch_timeout_seconds`. On poll-budget exhaustion the dispatcher best-effort cancels the still-running session before raising (§14.20.2 step 4). **Operator-sizing contract (documented, not enforced across the per-step/per-config boundary):** `step_timeout_seconds` MUST exceed the per-step poll budget (`max_poll_attempts × poll_interval_seconds`) + create/send/retrieve latency headroom. With sane defaults (30s budget ≪ 600s) this holds; an operator who bloats `max_poll_attempts` past the facade timeout re-opens the orphan window (the facade abandons the coroutine before the internal cancel runs). The harness does not enforce the relationship — it is an operator-sizing invariant.

### §14.20.6 X-AL-2 retirement implications (v1.55 → retirement event prerequisites)

H_T-AS-8f is already **SUBSTANTIVE_RETIRED** (R-820 live proof; `.harness/substitutions.yaml`). C-RT-28 closes the two owed M-arc gaps: (a) the formal contract (this §14.20), and (b) the production wiring (the `MANAGED_AGENTS` StepKind + the stage-5 dispatcher binding) — turning the dormant-driver-only carrier into a production-reachable consumer. The overlay's `carrier_files: []` for H_T-AS-8f is closed by the Slice-5 cite-bind (tag `managed_agents.py` + the new dispatcher/factory to C-RT-28 / H_T-AS-8f). The live managed-cloud production run (the credential/vendor gate) is surfaced, never auto-fired — it is NOT a retirement prerequisite (H_T-AS-8f already retired on the R-820 proof); it is the Slice-6 surfaced vendor-gate.

### §14.20.7 Deferred to implementation discretion

- **`step_payload` key schema + step-body→event mapping.** v1.55 names the required inputs (agent_id / environment_id / event_type / payload + optional title/metadata); the exact key names + how a declarative step body maps to the initial `ManagedAgentEvent` are implementation discretion at the landing arc.
- **Poll-budget mechanism + interval.** The bounded poll loop to a terminal status (a `RuntimeConfig` field, a per-step `step_payload` value, or a fixed default) + the poll interval/backoff are implementation discretion. The value MUST bound the loop (no unbounded poll). As-built: per-step `step_payload` keys `max_poll_attempts` (default 30) + `poll_interval_seconds` (default 1.0). The poll budget MUST be sized below the facade `step_timeout_seconds` (§14.20.5 invariant 7) so the internal cancel-on-give-up runs before the facade abandons the coroutine.
- **`ManagedAgentsClientProtocol` supply mechanism.** v1.55 keeps the empty-marker `ManagedAgentsConfig`; the concrete client (e.g. `AnthropicManagedAgentsClient` over a live SDK client) is supplied at the operator-controlled bootstrap site (a `run_bootstrap(...)` parameter; a singleton accessor; etc.) — parallel to C-RT-27's hook supply. Mechanism is operator-discretion at the landing arc.
- **`CANCELED`-as-success vs failure.** §14.20.2 step 7 maps `CANCELED` to dispatch-failure by default; a caller that treats operator-interrupt cancellation as a graceful outcome may override at the landing arc.
- **Engine-class interaction.** Whether a `MANAGED_AGENTS` step participates in the engine-class candidate set (managed-cloud admits event-sourced-replay / save-point / reconciler / WAL) or is engine-orthogonal is implementation discretion; v1.55 treats the managed-agents dispatch as a single step body (the vendor owns intra-session durability).

## §14.21 C-RT-34 — `InterStepOutputChannel` inter-step data-flow contract (new at v1.59)

**Contract surface.** A run-scoped, operator-opt-in **inter-step output channel** — the *"shared run context the dispatcher reads"* that `harness_cp.workflow_driver` §25.11 named as the home for inter-step DATA flow. The workflow driver records each completed step's output to the channel; a dispatcher that needs upstream context reads the immediately-prior step's output from it. This closes the gap where the driver threads only **control flow** between steps for every topology — most visibly in `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER`, where before v1.59 the evaluator never *saw* the generate draft and the regenerate never *saw* the evaluator's feedback (the §25.11 "regenerate-with-feedback" content flow was, at the driver, control-flow only). Constructed + bound at bootstrap stage 5 gated on a `RuntimeConfig` opt-in; the genuine consumer is the C-RT-15 LLM dispatcher, which injects the upstream output into the dispatched provider payload.

**PRD enablement.** Makes the multi-LLM agent loop's intra-workflow data flow real: an evaluator-optimizer / pipeline step can condition on a prior step's output (the basis for genuinely effective EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER + ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS with real model dispatchers — composes with B1 topology + B4 per-role selection).

**ADR commitment(s) honored.** ADR-F2 v1.2 (single-threaded-write — the wired scope records on the driver thread) + ADR-F1 v1.2 (provider-neutral dispatch — the injected upstream context is a provider-neutral message, not a per-provider shape).

**Fork-resolution provenance.** `.harness/class_1_fork_b_interstep_data_flow.md` — Class 1, R-FS-1 standalone arc **B-INTERSTEP** (spine ledger `.harness/beyond-mvp-capability-boundary-ledger.md` line 43, `design-fork-first per X-AL-3`). **NO operator gate** — additive + operator-opt-in (default off → byte-identical); the `StepDispatcher.dispatch` signature is UNCHANGED and §25.3.3.4 *step-body-opaque-to-driver* is PRESERVED; no committed invariant sacrificed. FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

### §14.21.1 Architectural surfaces introduced

**NEW carriers:**

- `InterStepOutputChannel` (`harness_runtime/lifecycle/inter_step_output_channel.py`) — a plain (`__slots__`, NON-Pydantic) by-reference holder of `(step_id, output)` pairs in **append order**:
  - `record(step_id: str, output: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None` — append a completed step's output (copied defensively).
  - `most_recent_output() -> Mapping[str, Any] | None` — the most-recently-recorded step output (the upstream output for the next dispatch), or `None` if no step has completed.
  - `outputs_by_step_id() -> Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]]` — a last-wins, insertion-ordered read-only view keyed by `step_id`.
  - Append order — NOT a `step_id`→output dict — is load-bearing: an `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER` loop re-dispatches the same generate `step_id` across iterations, so a step_id-keyed dict would make `most_recent_output()` return the wrong (overwritten-in-place) value on regenerate.
- `RuntimeConfig.inter_step_data_flow: bool = False` (§3) — the opt-in flag. Default `False` → no channel constructed → byte-identical to pre-v1.59.
- `HarnessContext.inter_step_output_channel: InterStepOutputChannel | None = None` (§4 NEW field) — bound at stage 5 LOOP_INIT to a fresh channel when opted-in; `None` otherwise. A plain by-reference holder under `arbitrary_types_allowed` (a typed container field would be Pydantic-copied at `freeze()`, disconnecting the driver's records from the dispatcher's read — the `CostRecordAccumulator` CA #625 precedent).
- `DriverContext.inter_step_output_channel: object | None` (CP-side Protocol field) — the driver consumes it via `getattr(ctx, ..., None)` dynamic dispatch (the `cp_is_wiring` idiom; harness-cp does NOT import the runtime holder).

**NEW dispatcher read (the genuine consumer):** `RuntimeLLMDispatcher` (C-RT-15) gains an `inter_step_channel` reference, threaded at stage 5 from the SAME `ctx.inter_step_output_channel` instance (the `cost_record_sink` threading precedent). When bound + non-empty, `dispatch` injects `most_recent_output()` into the **final per-provider `kwargs["messages"]`** — AFTER `kwargs.update(payload.params)` and AFTER the R-PM-1 system-prompt injection — as a single provider-neutral `user` "Upstream step output:" context message, placed after any leading `role:"system"` message. Injecting on the final kwargs (not `payload.messages`) is load-bearing: it cannot be silently dropped by a `params["messages"]` escape-hatch override, and it cannot mask the competing-system-source conflict check (mirrors the R-PM-1 post-`params` system-prompt injection; surfaced by out-of-family Codex review). The dispatch Protocol signature is UNCHANGED — the channel is read off the dispatcher's frozen construction reference, never a per-call parameter.

### §14.21.2 Recording + read discipline

1. **Record (producer — the CP driver).** After a step body completes (output produced + step.boundary emitted), the driver calls `inter_step_output_channel.record(str(step.step_id), step_output)` — at the `SINGLE_THREADED_LINEAR` `accumulated` site and in the `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER` loop BEFORE the next dispatch. The driver records the dispatcher's already-produced **opaque output Mapping**; it never introspects or mutates the frozen `step_payload` (§25.3.3.4 preserved). When `ctx.inter_step_output_channel is None` (opt-out), the record is a no-op.
2. **Read + inject (consumer — the LLM dispatcher).** `RuntimeLLMDispatcher.dispatch` reads `most_recent_output()` once; each per-provider kwargs translator (`_payload_to_{anthropic,openai,ollama}_kwargs`) then injects it into the **final** `kwargs["messages"]` — after the `params` merge + the system-prompt injection — as a `user` "Upstream step output:" message placed after any leading `role:"system"` message. The model genuinely receives the prior step's output. When the channel is `None` (opt-out) or empty (first step), the kwargs are unchanged. (Injecting on the final kwargs rather than `payload.messages` is required so a `params["messages"]` override cannot drop it and the system-conflict check is not masked — out-of-family Codex review.)
3. **EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER data flow (the load-bearing case).** generate → record(gen) → evaluate dispatch reads `most_recent_output()` = gen draft → record(eval) → regenerate reads `most_recent_output()` = eval feedback → … . The append-ordered `most_recent_output()` yields the correct upstream output across the generate-step re-dispatch.

### §14.21.3 Lifecycle stage placement

**Stage 5 (LOOP_INIT).** When `config.inter_step_data_flow` is `True` and `ctx.inter_step_output_channel is None`, the stage constructs `InterStepOutputChannel()`, binds it on the mutable ctx (threaded by-reference onto the frozen `HarnessContext` at `freeze()`), and threads the SAME instance into `materialize_llm_dispatcher_stage(inter_step_channel=...)`. Sibling-of the other stage-5 LOOP_INIT opt-in surfaces; the only ordering constraint is that the channel is constructed before the LLM-dispatcher factory call that threads it.

**Per-run boundary (`run_workflow` tool handler).** Because the channel is allocated at bootstrap but is run-scoped state, the `run_workflow` tool handler `reset()`s `ctx.inter_step_output_channel` at the start of each (non-resume) invocation — the run boundary a reused (daemon-client mode) `HarnessContext` re-enters — before dispatching `execute_workflow` (§14.21.5 invariant 7a). No-op when the channel is unbound. When the channel IS bound, `[reset + execute]` runs under a per-running-loop single-flight lock so concurrent invocations sharing the one channel are serialized rather than interleaved (§14.21.5 invariant 7b); the unbound default path never touches the lock. The lock cannot fence a non-cancellable worker thread that outlives a `drain_timeout_seconds` timeout — that systemic reused-ctx timeout-zombie residual is registered, not closed here (§14.21.5 invariant 7c → §14.21.7 `B-INTERSTEP-PERRUN-ISOLATION`).

### §14.21.4 Failure-mode taxonomy

**No new fail class.** The channel is a best-effort run-scoped carrier — recording + reading are infallible mapping operations. A malformed upstream output is serialized with `json.dumps(..., default=str)` (no raise). The opt-out default path adds no behavior.

### §14.21.5 Invariants

1. **Opt-out default is byte-identical.** `inter_step_data_flow=False` → `ctx.inter_step_output_channel is None` → the driver records nothing AND the LLM dispatcher injects nothing. Pre-v1.59 behavior is preserved verbatim.
2. **Dispatch Protocol signature UNCHANGED.** `StepDispatcher.dispatch(binding, step, *, step_context)` is byte-unchanged; the channel is a run-scoped surface read off the dispatcher's construction reference, never a per-call parameter (the §25.11 "never prior outputs" property).
3. **Step body opaque to the driver (§25.3.3.4 preserved).** The driver records the dispatcher's already-produced output Mapping; it does not introspect or mutate the frozen `step_payload`.
4. **Single-threaded-write (ADR-F2) for the wired scope.** `SINGLE_THREADED_LINEAR` + `EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER` record on the driver thread (sequential) — no concurrent writes to the shared holder. Concurrent-sibling-fan-out recording would require the buffered-branch drain path, but the deeper blocker (v1.74 correction) is the **absent non-vacuous consumer**: the concurrent strategies compose via a deterministic fold reading `branch_outputs` directly (C-CP-25 §25.12), so channel recording is hollow absent a post-join LLM synthesis step (a §25.12-determinism gate). See §14.21.7 — `B-INTERSTEP-NONLINEAR` is RESOLVED-AS-HOLLOW; the genuine capability is the gated `B-POSTJOIN-LLM-SYNTHESIS`.
5. **No §5.2-hash / IS-spec change.** The channel is an ephemeral run-scoped carrier (the `cost_record_accumulator` precedent), NOT persisted state — it is not in the C-IS-05 §5.2 entry hash nor any audit projection.
6. **Genuine consumer, not a hollow carrier.** v1.59 ships the real LLM-dispatcher consumer (the prior output reaches the actual provider call), proven by-execution against the provider boundary — the channel is non-vacuous on landing (`[[r-cxa-seam-wiring-is-producer-discovery]]` / advisor's *non-vacuity-is-the-deliverable*).
7. **Run-scoped, not bootstrap-scoped — cross-run leak closed for the normal completion paths; the timeout-zombie residual is registered.** Although the channel is *allocated* at bootstrap (stage 5), its contents are run-scoped. The per-run-boundary discipline closes cross-run leak for the two normal-completion cases, with one honestly-bounded residual:
   - **(a) Sequential reuse — closed by `reset()`.** The `run_workflow` tool handler `reset()`s the channel at the per-run boundary (on a non-resume invocation; a resume continues the same run) so a REUSED `HarnessContext` — the daemon-client mode where one bootstrapped ctx serves many `run_workflow` invocations (U-RT-108) — does NOT leak a prior run's step outputs into a later run's first dispatch (out-of-family Codex review r3). A resume is NOT reset (it continues the same run's in-flight outputs).
   - **(b) Concurrent, both within the drain timeout — closed by a single-flight lock.** Because the bootstrap-scoped ctx exposes ONE channel, two *concurrent* `run_workflow` invocations on the same ctx would share it and corrupt each other (run B's `reset()`/records overwriting run A's in-flight reads — out-of-family Codex review r4). So **when the channel is bound, the handler runs `[reset + execute]` under a per-running-loop single-flight lock** — the dispatch `await` is *inside* the `async with`, so run A holds the lock for its whole execution and concurrent inter-step runs queue rather than interleave. The opt-out default (channel unbound) NEVER acquires the lock → full concurrency is unchanged (byte-identical to pre-v1.59).
   - **(c) Concurrent, one exceeds `drain_timeout_seconds` — a registered residual, NOT closed here.** On a drain timeout `asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.to_thread(...))` raises and the `async with` releases the lock, but the non-cancellable worker thread can keep running and recording into the shared channel — so a following run can reset/interleave with it (out-of-family Codex review r5). This is the **SYSTEMIC reused-ctx daemon timeout-zombie exposure shared by EVERY mutable holder on the bootstrap ctx** (`cost_record_accumulator`, ledger writers, …) — a pre-existing property of the non-cancellable `to_thread` drain path, **NOT introduced by this arc** and NOT closeable by a lock (a released lock cannot fence a zombie thread). It is closed for all holders together by the proper per-run channel *isolation* (a `ContextVar`-scoped channel that also removes the (b) serialization AND covers the identical `cost_record_accumulator` exposure) — registered follow-on `B-INTERSTEP-PERRUN-ISOLATION` (§14.21.7).

### §14.21.6 X-AL-2 retirement implications

No substitution row is retired by C-RT-34 — inter-step data flow is a new H_T capability, not an H_E substitution surface. It composes with future arcs (`B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY` for resume-correct cross-step data flow) per §14.21.7. (The concurrent-fan-out follow-on `B-INTERSTEP-NONLINEAR` is RESOLVED-AS-HOLLOW at v1.74 — see §14.21.7; the genuine concurrent-fan-out inter-step read is the §25.12-gated `B-POSTJOIN-LLM-SYNTHESIS`, with which the channel would compose only once that operator-gated synthesis-step capability lands.)

### §14.21.7 Deferred to implementation discretion / registered follow-ons

- **Message shape of the injected upstream context.** v1.59 prepends a single `user` "Upstream step output:" message carrying the JSON-serialized prior output. A richer / per-provider role mapping, or a per-step manifest-declared data-dependency selecting *which* prior outputs feed *which* step (vs. the v1.59 "immediately-prior output" semantic), is implementation discretion at a follow-on arc.
- **Concurrent-fan-out recording — RESOLVED-AS-HOLLOW (`B-INTERSTEP-NONLINEAR`; v1.74 correction).** The DECENTRALIZED_HANDOFF case closed at `B-INTERSTEP-HANDOFF` (#677, the sequential single-owner cursor). The 3 *concurrent* strategies (ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS, PARALLELIZATION, HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION) would record via the #648 buffered-branch drain path (ADR-F2 — concurrent sibling writes cannot share the holder directly), **but recording is HOLLOW**: these topologies compose via a **deterministic fold** (C-CP-25 §25.11/§25.12, `_aggregate_orchestrator_workers` / `_aggregate_parallelization`) that receives `branch_outputs` **directly**, not from the channel, and topology is per-workflow so the fold output is the terminal `RunResult` — there is no post-join LLM read and no subsequent linear step to consume `most_recent_output()`. Recording siblings/aggregate would have no non-vacuous consumer (fails invariant 6). The v1.59 framing "the genuine inter-step reads are sequential (orchestrator synthesis post-join), so the channel composes once recording lands" was **false** (the aggregate fold is `_aggregate_orchestrator_workers`, which states "there is NO second 'compose' dispatch"). The genuine capability — a post-join **LLM synthesis** step reading sibling outputs — makes the fan-out output non-deterministic, contradicting §25.12 → a Class-1 topology-semantics / operator gate, registered as **`B-POSTJOIN-LLM-SYNTHESIS`** (spine ledger), NOT a silent build.
- **Cross-step resume rehydration (composes with `B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY`).** On a skip-prefix resume the replayed prefix is NOT re-dispatched, so a downstream cross-step consumer reads an empty channel (fresh-run ≠ resumed-run). Closing it needs the output-carrying event-history substrate (the F2 `EntryPayload` carries only a `response_hash` digest today) = the `B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY` arc. EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER's data flow lives *inside* one driver invocation's loop (atomic — no resume boundary crossed), so the wired consumer is resume-safe; cross-step *linear* data flow is resume-correct only once `B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY` lands.
- **Per-run channel isolation (registered follow-on `B-INTERSTEP-PERRUN-ISOLATION`).** v1.59 forecloses the *normal-completion* concurrent-inter-step corruption with a per-loop single-flight lock (§14.21.5 invariant 7b) — proportionate, but it *serializes* concurrent inter-step runs rather than isolating them, and it cannot fence the timeout-zombie (7c). The proper fix scopes the channel per run (e.g. a `ContextVar`-bound channel resolved at dispatch), which closes **three** things at once: (1) it removes the serialization (restoring full concurrency for the bound path — invariant 7b); (2) it closes the **timeout-zombie residual** (invariant 7c) — a per-run channel means a timed-out run's non-cancellable worker writes only to ITS OWN dead channel, never a later run's; (3) it closes the IDENTICAL bootstrap-scoped shared-holder exposure that `cost_record_accumulator` carries today (CA #625 — a concurrent-daemon cost-rollup cross-run mix, both at completion AND under the same timeout-zombie trigger; observability-additive so lower-severity, but the same root). This is a runtime-wide concurrency arc (the timeout-zombie is systemic across every bootstrap-ctx holder, not channel-specific — so a channel-only run-key would be a false-complete leaving the sibling holders corrupt), registered here because B-INTERSTEP is the first capability whose *correctness* (not just observability) depends on it.

## §14.22 C-RT-31 — `RuntimeEffectFence` at-most-once effect-execution contract (new at v1.60)

**Contract surface.** A hand-rolled (I-6 — no vendored Temporal/DBOS activity-dedup) durable, operator-opt-in **effect-boundary fence** at the `RuntimeToolDispatcher` `call_tool` sink. It guarantees **at-most-once EXECUTION** of a non-idempotent tool-step effect across durable-engine retries and resumes: before the external effect fires, the dispatcher crash-atomically claims the effect's per-(run, step, tool) `idempotency_key`; a re-dispatch of an already-claimed effect (a crash-then-resume re-run of an effected-but-uncommitted step, or an in-process retry) fail-closes rather than re-fire. **(As of v1.72, a lost-reserve re-dispatch SPLITS on a captured output — suppress-and-continue when present, an operator-resolvable §26.2 PAUSE when absent/corrupt — never an auto-re-fire; §14.22.1–.5 below describe the v1.60 interim fail-closed narrative, refined at §14.22.8.)** This closes the floor-(ii) "at-most-once execution" gap the durable engine classes advertise but did not deliver — the U-RT-123 reconciler CAS guarantees at-most-once *claim of a revision*, not at-most-once *execution* of the steps a resume re-runs (the `idempotency_key` was on the `cp.resume-attempted` AUDIT entry + the per-step ledger dedup, never on the external effect at its sink).

**PRD enablement.** Makes the durable engine classes' at-most-once promise real for non-idempotent external effects (the difference between at-most-once-*claim* and at-least-once-*effect*). A workflow with a `git_push`/`send_email`/payment side-effecting tool can be durably resumed without re-applying the effect.

**ADR commitment(s) honored.** I-6 (hand-rolled crash-atomic POSIX claim, no vendored activity-dedup framework) + ADR-F2 v1.2 (the fence is a separate durable store, NOT the single-threaded state-ledger writer — the per-step ledger entry remains the COMMIT, byte-unchanged) + ADR-D1 v1.2 (single-host bound, mirroring U-RT-123; cross-host folds into the deferred F-CC item).

**Fork-resolution provenance.** `.harness/class_1_fork_b_effect_fence_at_most_once_execution.md` — Class 1, R-FS-1 standalone arc **B-EFFECT-FENCE** (spine ledger `.harness/beyond-mvp-capability-boundary-ledger.md` line 49, `design-fork-first per X-AL-3, since a sink-fencing surface is new`; surfaced as E-impl-3b finding F-2). **NO operator gate** — additive + operator-opt-in (default off → byte-identical); the one nameable C10⊥C11 fence-scope tension is probe-resolved by durable-resume scoping (no `ToolContract` field, no AS fork); no committed invariant sacrificed. FULL-SPEC-pre-authorized (`[[feedback-full-spec-beyond-mvp-nothing-deferred]]`).

### §14.22.1 Architectural surfaces introduced

**NEW carriers:**

- `RuntimeEffectFence` (`harness_runtime/lifecycle/effect_fence.py`) — a `harness_runtime`-private durable single-host claim store (never leaks into a cleared CP Protocol — a substrate within §14.9 impl-discretion, not a new cross-axis contract):
  - `try_reserve(idempotency_key: str) -> bool` — the crash-atomic claim. Returns `True` iff THIS call won the right to fire the effect (fresh claim); `False` iff the key was already reserved (a resume re-dispatch or an in-process retry). The U-RT-123 `_claim_resume_revision` pattern verbatim, re-keyed from `(workflow, resource_version)` to the per-effect `idempotency_key`: write a best-effort `host:pid` incarnation stamp (for observability, NOT the win/lose discriminator) to a uuid-unique temp (`fsync`-ed), then `os.link` it into place — `link` is atomic and raises `FileExistsError` if the claim exists, so a crash can only ever leave an orphan temp, never a half-published claim; the won claim's dirent is `fsync`-ed.
  - The claim file = `sha256(idempotency_key)` under the fence directory. The key is already per-(run, step, tool) scoped (the run-scoped `_compute_step_idempotency_key` composed with `step_id`/`tool_id` at the dispatcher), so a flat directory is collision-free across runs — a fresh run derives a different `run_idempotency_key` → a disjoint claim namespace (the U-RT-123 finding O-E3b-1 run-scoping lesson).
- `EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError` — raised at the sink when `try_reserve` loses. NOT a transient class (a retry always re-loses), so the `RetryBreakerToolDispatcher` fail-fasts it per the §14.11 `_TRANSIENT_TOOL_DISPATCH_ERRORS` allow-list; the driver's generic `except BaseException` maps it to a FAILED `RunResult` (`fail_class="step-failure: EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError: …"`). The genuine §22.1 operator-resolvable pause is the registered `B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE` follow-on (§14.22.7).
- `RuntimeConfig.effect_fencing: bool = False` (§3) — the opt-in flag. Default `False` → no fence constructed → byte-identical to pre-v1.60.

**NEW dispatcher reserve (the sink):** `RuntimeToolDispatcher.__init__` gains an `effect_fence: EffectFenceProtocol | None = None` reference (threaded by the stage-5 tool-dispatcher factory from `config.effect_fencing`). When bound, `dispatch` calls `try_reserve(idempotency_key)` immediately AFTER composing the idempotency key and BEFORE `call_tool` — a lost claim raises `EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError` before the effect fires. `None` (opt-out) → no reserve. The `dispatch` Protocol signature is UNCHANGED.

### §14.22.2 Reserve discipline

1. **Reserve (at the sink, pre-fire).** `RuntimeToolDispatcher.dispatch` composes the per-(run, step, tool) `idempotency_key` (`_compose_idempotency_key(step_context.parent_idempotency_key, step_id, tool_id)`), then — if the fence is bound — `try_reserve`s it. WON → proceed to `call_tool` (the effect fires). LOST → raise `EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError`. When the fence is `None` (opt-out), no reserve.
2. **COMMIT is the existing per-step ledger entry.** The fence adds only the RESERVE (pre-fire) marker; the COMMIT remains `workflow_driver.py` `_append_step_ledger_entry` (`:2336`), one source of truth. A committed step is prefix-skipped on resume (`_determine_resume_at`) and never re-reaches the sink, so its stale claim file is never consulted (retention residual — the same accepted bar as the reconciler's claim files; compaction is a follow-on).
3. **The window the fence uniquely closes.** The effect fires at `workflow_driver.py:2031` (dispatch), the per-step ledger commit lands at `:2336`; a crash in between leaves the step uncommitted → `_determine_resume_at` returns its index → the loop re-dispatches it with a byte-identical `idempotency_key` → the fence resolves it to the SAME claim → LOST → fail-close (no double-fire). Distinct from the reconciler's *revision-claim* fail-close (which guards WHICH reconciler wins a resume, not the per-step effect-vs-commit ordering) and from prefix-skip (which protects only COMMITTED steps).

### §14.22.3 Lifecycle stage placement

**Stage 5 (tool-dispatcher factory).** When `config.effect_fencing` is `True`, `materialize_runtime_tool_dispatcher_stage` constructs `RuntimeEffectFence(fence_dir=config.repository_root / ".harness" / "effect-fence")` (the §14.21 `repository_root` basis for `.harness/`) and passes it to the bare `RuntimeToolDispatcher`. Default opt-out → `None`. Meaningful only under a durable engine class (where a resume re-dispatches uncommitted steps); auto-activation under durable engines is the registered `B-EFFECT-FENCE-DURABLE-AUTO` follow-on (§14.22.7).

### §14.22.4 Failure-mode taxonomy

**`EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError` (runtime-shape, not pre-registered in the §14.9 `RT-FAIL-*` taxonomy — the EDIT-carrier `HITLGateEditCarrierDriftError` interim precedent).** Raised when a re-dispatch loses the claim; fail-fast (non-transient) → the driver returns FAILED with an honest fail-class. Registering an `RT-FAIL-EFFECT-FENCE-*` taxonomy code + the §22.1 HITL routing is the `B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE` follow-on. The opt-out default path adds no behavior + no fail class.

### §14.22.5 Invariants

1. **Opt-out default is byte-identical.** `effect_fencing=False` → no fence constructed → the dispatcher reserves nothing, writes no claim files. Pre-v1.60 behavior is preserved verbatim.
2. **Dispatch Protocol signature UNCHANGED.** `StepDispatcher.dispatch(binding, step, *, step_context)` is byte-unchanged; the fence is read off the dispatcher's construction reference, never a per-call parameter. It keys on the EXISTING `step_context.parent_idempotency_key` (no CP contract change).
3. **At-most-once per (run, step) `idempotency_key` — across BOTH resume and retry, NOT conflating a legitimate loop iteration.** The fence claims the per-(run, step, tool) `idempotency_key` = `compose(_compute_step_idempotency_key(run_idempotency_key, <step ordinal>), step_id, tool_id)`. This key is the **harness's per-invocation identity**: a resume re-dispatch of the same step reuses it (same ordinal → same key → fenced — correct), AND the in-process `RetryBreakerToolDispatcher` retry reuses it (the fence error fail-fasts, not retried — for a non-idempotent effect, fail-closing a transient-failure retry is the correct conservative behavior). Crucially, a *fresh* re-invocation of the same declared tool step within one run is NOT conflated with a resume re-fire: the looping topology already assigns a **distinct** `idempotency_key` per invocation (EVALUATOR_OPTIMIZER uses the **monotonic `entry_index`** as `StepExecutionContext.parent_idempotency_key`, `workflow_driver.py:3620-3628`; fan-out strategies use the **branch-scoped** `compose_branch_path` key) — it MUST, else the IS writer's `idempotency_key`-only dedup (C-IS-07 §7.5) would silently drop iteration-2's ledger entry. So the same key that keeps loop iterations / branches distinct at the ledger is the key the fence claims → a loop iteration gets a NEW key (fires), only a resume re-dispatch reuses the key (fenced). The residual fire-then-crash-before-commit window is ambiguous to the harness, so the conservative fail-close (a reserved-but-unfired effect also fail-closes its re-dispatch) is the honest answer (mirrors the reconciler §22.1 posture) — **at-most-once per invocation, NOT exactly-once**.
4. **COMMIT = the existing per-step ledger entry.** The fence adds only the RESERVE marker; no second commit record (one source of truth). A committed step is prefix-skipped and never re-consults its claim.
5. **Single-host (ADR-D1 bound).** The default claim is atomic on a local filesystem; cross-host effect-fencing is distributed-impossible under {I-6 ∧ no-unsafe-TTL} and folds into the deferred F-CC item (exactly as U-RT-123).
6. **No §5.2-hash / IS-spec / CP-spec / OD-spec / ADR change.** The fence claim is a side file in a separate durable store, NOT a state-ledger entry — the per-step ledger entry shape is byte-identical, so the C-IS-05 §5.2 entry hash is unchanged. I-6 + ADR-F2 honored.
7. **Genuine non-vacuity, not a hollow surface.** v1.60 fences the REAL `call_tool` sink, proven by-execution with NO proxy: a real dispatcher re-dispatching the same effect fires the underlying counting tool EXACTLY ONCE; a NEGATIVE CONTROL proves double-fire without the fence; a fresh-dispatcher-over-the-same-on-disk-fence-dir test is a genuine restart (crash-then-resume); the driver hands the sink a byte-identical key on the real `execute_workflow` resume path (`[[r-cxa-seam-wiring-is-producer-discovery]]` / advisor's *non-vacuity-FIRST*).

### §14.22.6 X-AL-2 retirement implications

No substitution row is retired by C-RT-31 — at-most-once effect execution is a new H_T capability, not an H_E substitution surface. It composes with the durable engine classes (E) + `B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY` (suppress-and-continue replay) + the deferred F-CC multi-host recovery per §14.22.7.

### §14.22.7 Deferred to implementation discretion / registered follow-ons

- **Auto-activation under durable engine classes (registered follow-on `B-EFFECT-FENCE-DURABLE-AUTO`).** v1.60 is opt-in (`effect_fencing=True`). The fence is meaningful only under a durable engine (where a resume re-dispatches uncommitted steps), so a future arc may auto-construct it whenever `manifest_entry.engine_class` is durable (threading the engine class to the factory, or a per-run reserve gate keyed on the engine class), removing the operator flag for the common case while keeping non-durable runs fence-free.
- **Per-tool idempotency classification (registered follow-on `B-EFFECT-FENCE-PER-TOOL`).** v1.60 fences every tool-step effect uniformly when opted-in. A future arc may add a `ToolContract` idempotency classification (`{READ_ONLY, IDEMPOTENT, NON_IDEMPOTENT}` — absent today) so only declared-non-idempotent tools are fenced (read-only / idempotent tools skip the fence + its claim I/O). That is a cross-axis AS contract surface → design-fork-first per X-AL-3 at that arc.
- **HITL routing + suppress-and-continue (registered follow-on `B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE` — BUILT at v1.72, §14.22.8).** v1.60's interim was the honest fail-closed raise → FAILED `RunResult` (no silent double-fire). v1.72 builds the genuine posture: a lost-claim re-dispatch SPLITS on a newly-captured output — present ⟹ *suppress-and-continue* (return the captured output, no re-fire); absent/corrupt ⟹ an operator-resolvable **§26.2 `WorkflowPauseReason.EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS` PAUSE** (bound `PauseResumeProtocol`) else FAILED. The pause-reason homes in `WorkflowPauseReason` (C-CP-26 §26.2), NOT the engine-layer §22.1 `PauseReason` (the v1.60 prose mislabeled it; the driver-routed pause path is `WorkflowPauseReason`-typed). The 2026-06-22 probe debunked the "requires `B-ENGINE-OUTPUT-REPLAY`" deferral — replay carries only a `response_hash` digest + `resume_at`-driven rehydrate that ignores the suppressed step's own uncommitted output — so v1.72 adds its OWN post-fire output capture at the fence. See §14.22.8.
- **Ambiguous-pause RESOLUTION (registered follow-on `B-EFFECT-FENCE-PAUSE-RESOLUTION`).** v1.72 builds the ambiguous-pause CAPTURE (§14.22.8); the resume-side RESOLUTION — the operator's `it-fired-skip-as-done` / `did-not-fire-re-fire` (a deliberate double-execution on operator assertion → clear the fence claim) / `abort` — is a safety-sensitive committed-behavior surface deferred to its own focused, operator-gated arc. The snapshot must carry the `idempotency_key` + a `resume_context` resolution input + a fence claim-clear path. Until it lands, a naive resume re-pauses identically (INERT — resume is caller-initiated; pinned by `test_ambiguous_pause_resume_re_pauses_until_resolution_follow_on`).
- **Cross-host effect fencing (folds into the deferred F-CC item).** Multi-host at-most-once execution is distributed-impossible under {I-6 ∧ no-unsafe-TTL} (the same failure-detector/FLP bound as the reconciler's F-CC); it is reachable hand-rolled only after a fenced bounded-synchrony lease, fenced-safe at every sink — the same F-CC item U-RT-123 carries.

### §14.22.8 Two-case split — suppress-and-continue / ambiguous PAUSE (B-EFFECT-FENCE-HITL-ROUTE, v1.72)

v1.72 refines the v1.60 interim ("a lost claim raises → FAILED", §14.22.1–.5) into the genuine HITL-routed posture the §14.22.7 follow-on named. The reserve discipline (§14.22.2) and the at-most-once key identity (§14.22.5 inv 3) are UNCHANGED; what changes is the resolution of a LOST reserve.

**NEW output substrate at the fence.** `RuntimeEffectFence` gains:

- `capture_output(idempotency_key: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None` — crash-atomically persist the effect's VALIDATED output to `sha256(idempotency_key).output` under the fence directory, via the same `O_EXCL`/`os.link`/`fsync` primitive as `try_reserve`. A torn write can only leave an orphan temp, never a half-published output → **present ⟹ complete-and-valid**.
- `read_output(idempotency_key: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None` — return the captured output iff a complete, valid capture exists; `None` iff ABSENT (no file) OR CORRUPT (un-parseable / non-object — defensive; fail-closed, never a valid suppress source per `[[durable-recovery-presence-validity-scope]]`).

Both are added to `EffectFenceProtocol`. The carrier `EffectFenceReservedUncommittedError` is RENAMED `EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError` (the two-case split removes its sole unconditional raise site).

**Dispatcher capture point.** `RuntimeToolDispatcher.dispatch` calls `capture_output(idempotency_key, response)` as the LAST step before the success return — AFTER `call_tool` fires, AFTER `output_schema` validation, AFTER cost-attribution — gated on the SAME `_fence_gate_open` as the reserve. So "captured ⟹ validated success ∧ cost attributed exactly once". A fired-but-schema-invalid response is NOT captured (it raises before the capture point), so a re-dispatch of it is correctly ambiguous, not a suppress source.

**The two-case split (at the lost reserve).** When `try_reserve` returns `False` (a re-dispatch of an effected-but-uncommitted step, or an in-process retry):

1. **`read_output` present** → the effect demonstrably completed AND its validated result is in hand → **suppress-and-continue**: the sink RETURNS the captured output (wrapped in the normal dispatch result; trust/sandbox metadata recomputed this dispatch, so the shape is byte-identical to a fresh success), NEVER re-firing `call_tool`. This is the value of the arc.
2. **`read_output` absent or corrupt** → the crash fell in the fire→capture window → genuinely ambiguous → the sink raises `EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError`.

**Driver routing (the §26.2 PAUSE).** The `RetryBreakerToolDispatcher` re-raises the ambiguous error verbatim (non-transient — §14.22.5 inv 3 unchanged). The workflow driver name-matches `type(exc).__name__ == "EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError"` at the linear/TOOL_STEP step-dispatch boundary (harness-cp cannot import harness-runtime — the `HITLPauseRequestedSignal` precedent) and:

- **bound `pause_resume_protocol`** → `capture_pause_snapshot(pause_reason=WorkflowPauseReason.EFFECT_FENCE_AMBIGUOUS)` → `RunStatus.PAUSED` with a hash-valid `PauseSnapshot`. A `PAUSE_CAPTURED` CP→IS audit entry is emitted with `event_sequence_id = (step_index << 2) | 3` (the effect-fence disambiguator, distinct from drain-flag [=1] + HITL-signal [=2]).

**Scope boundary — capture now, resolution is the registered follow-on.** v1.72 builds the ambiguous-pause **CAPTURE** (a labeled, non-terminal, inspectable, hash-valid pause — a strict improvement over the v1.60 terminal FAILED). The resume-side **RESOLUTION** of that pause — the operator's `it-fired-skip-as-done` / `did-not-fire-re-fire` (a deliberate double-execution on operator assertion, which requires clearing the fence claim) / `abort` — is a **safety-sensitive committed-behavior surface deferred to the registered follow-on `B-EFFECT-FENCE-PAUSE-RESOLUTION`** (snapshot carries the `idempotency_key` + a `resume_context` resolution input + a fence claim-clear). Until it lands, a naive `api.resume` re-enters the same step with the claim still held + still no output → re-raises → an **identical re-PAUSE**. This is INERT, not a busy-loop: resume is **caller-initiated** (`api.resume` / `execute_workflow(pause_snapshot_input=...)`), never auto-driven by an engine loop — the paused run sits until a caller resumes. The interim re-pause is pinned by a by-execution test (`test_ambiguous_pause_resume_re_pauses_until_resolution_follow_on`) so it is intentional + documented, not a silent surprise.
- **unbound** → falls through to the generic FAILED mapping — behaviorally equivalent to the pre-v1.72 fail-closed (FAILED, NO auto-re-fire); only the `fail_class` STRING differs (it now names `EffectFenceAmbiguousUncommittedError`).

**The at-most-once invariant preserved (the #701 decline-mirror transferred).** Auto-proceed (suppress-and-continue) happens ONLY on proof-of-completion (captured output present + valid); EVERY ambiguous case fails to the operator. Neither branch ever auto-re-fires. Both crash windows fail safe: (a) crash after-fire-before-output-fsync → reserve present + output ABSENT → PAUSE (cannot auto-re-fire); (b) crash after-output-fsync-before-commit → reserve present + output PRESENT → suppress-and-continue (recover, cannot re-fire).

**Pause-reason home (§26.2, NOT §22.1).** The new value is a `WorkflowPauseReason` (C-CP-26 §26.2, the workflow-driver pause taxonomy — the enum `capture_pause_snapshot` + `PauseSnapshot.pause_reason` are typed to), NOT the engine-layer §22.1 `PauseReason` (the engine-native replay-pause substrate, which the driver's exception handler never calls). This mirrors HITL exactly: a driver-detected HITL pause uses `WorkflowPauseReason.HITL_PENDING`, not the engine `HITL_INVOCATION_PENDING`.

## §14.24 C-RT-33 — `PostJoinSynthesisStepDispatcher` post-join synthesis contract (new at v1.75)

**Purpose.** The runtime executable-consumer for the opt-in `StepKind.POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` terminal step (CP spec v1.54 §5.2/§25.2/§3). After a concurrent fan-out (ORCHESTRATOR_WORKERS / PARALLELIZATION / HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION) barriers, the CP driver carves the terminal synthesis step out of the branch set and dispatches it post-barrier supplying the branch-index-ordered sibling worker outputs on `StepExecutionContext.sibling_outputs`; this dispatcher LLM-composes them into the run's synthesized terminal aggregate (the canonical "orchestrator synthesizes" completion the deterministic §25.12 fold omits).

**Contract.**

1. **Binding.** Bound to `StepKind.POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` in the stage-5 `StepKindDispatcherRegistry` (§14.7.1), under the `ctx.requires_inference` predicate (it makes an LLM call) — alongside `INFERENCE_STEP` / `SUB_AGENT_DISPATCH`. A `POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` step in a provider-free (tool-only) workflow → the row is omitted → `lookup` raises `StepKindDispatcherNotBoundError` → `RT-FAIL-STEP-KIND-DISPATCHER-NOT-BOUND` (no silent under-execution), exactly as `INFERENCE_STEP`.

2. **Inner-dispatcher wrap (sync).** The dispatcher wraps the **inner LLM dispatcher** — the stage-5 `inference_step_dispatcher`, which is the C-RT-16 `RetryBreakerFallbackDispatcher` chain already wrapped in the `SyncDispatcherFacade`. The synthesis dispatcher is therefore itself **sync** (it composes + delegates to the already-sync facade — no further facade). It satisfies the `@runtime_checkable` `StepDispatcher` Protocol (`dispatch(binding, step, *, step_context)`), unchanged.

3. **Sibling composition (minimal dispatch).** On `dispatch`, read the branch-index-ordered `step_context.sibling_outputs` (each entry `(branch_index, output)`; `None`/absent → empty). Compose them into ONE trailing context `user` message — `[post-join siblings]\n` + the deterministically-serialized (`sort_keys`, `default=str`) `[{branch_index, output}, …]` list — appended AFTER the synthesis step's declared `payload.messages` (the operator's synthesis instruction). Dispatch the composed step (via `WorkflowStep.model_copy(update={"step_payload": …})`, `step_kind` preserved) through the inner LLM dispatcher. **Reducer DSLs / configurable templating / per-level HIERARCHICAL synthesis are the registered follow-ons** (out of scope, CP spec v1.54 change-note).

4. **Read-only / effect-free.** The synthesis is a pure read-of-siblings + LLM compose — NO external effect, NO effect-fence-carrying tool dispatch inside the step. This is the load-bearing safety property that makes the step re-dispatch-at-most-once-safe on any resume path (CP spec v1.54 §3).

5. **Disclosure home (CP driver, NOT this dispatcher).** The §25.12 Point-2 (aggregator-purity) sacrifice — the synthesized aggregate is non-deterministic — is disclosed by the CP driver via a **durable, self-disclosing synthesis step ledger entry** (`action_id` `workflow:{wf}:post-join-synthesis:{N}`). That ledger entry IS the loud disclosure; the OTel span/trace-attribute layer is the standard deferred D6-ingestion (the v1.59 RESUMPTION precedent — CP emits the typed disclosure, OD/runtime populates the span). This dispatcher emits no separate disclosure; it inherits the inner LLM dispatcher's `gen_ai` span like any inference.

**Invariants.** (a) **Opt-out byte-identical** — absent a declared `POST_JOIN_SYNTHESIS` terminal step the concurrent strategies run the deterministic §25.12 fold verbatim (no dispatcher invoked). (b) **No §5.2-hash / IS change** — the `sibling_outputs` carrier is hash-inert (CP spec v1.54 §2); disclosure rides the CP driver's step entry, not a new IS field. (c) **No Protocol widening / no new CXA edge** — reuses the existing sync `StepDispatcher` Protocol + the C-RT-16 LLM-dispatch seam.

**§14.24.7 (registered follow-ons).** `B-FANOUT-OUTPUT-REPLAY` (reproducible cached-replay of the synthesized aggregate across a fan-out crash-resume — requires a durable per-branch-completion substrate + a §25.12-D1 reckoning, its own council + gate); synthesis-per-level for HIERARCHICAL_DELEGATION; configurable reducers / synthesis-over-arbitrary-strategies / reducer DSL / operator-supplied prompt templating beyond the minimal dispatch.

P2-S4-CK should verify this is acceptable for any anticipated Track A integration test scenarios (cached-context optimization is Track B). v1.1 added the concurrency invariant (`RT-FAIL-CONCURRENT-RUN`) which makes the bootstrap-per-call discipline enforceable, partially closing this.
